# SS Replay — Full Product, Architecture, UX/UI, Performance and Bug-Risk Audit

**Build v125 · MQL5 · 123 files · 51,278 lines · 74 classes**

## How this audit was produced, and how far to trust it

Seventeen agents read the codebase by subsystem, each file in full, and produced an architecture map plus candidate defects. That yielded **255 candidates, 248 after deduplication**.

Every one of the 248 was then put to **three independent adversarial refuters** — one tracing the execution path and looking for a guard that prevents the outcome, one checking every MQL5 runtime semantic the finding assumes, one judging whether the state is reachable and what the user actually observes. All three were instructed to refute, and to default to refuted when uncertain. A finding survives only if two of three could not refute it; it is marked CONFIRMED only if two of three could also prove it from source.

| Verdict | Count | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| **CONFIRMED** | **197** | provable from the source read |
| POTENTIAL_RISK | 30 | survived, but turns on runtime or broker behaviour |
| **NOT_A_BUG** | **21** | refuted — kept in the record with the reason |

Confirmed by severity: **2 CRITICAL** · **14 HIGH** · **58 MEDIUM** · **105 LOW** · **18 IMPROVEMENT**

**Two cautions the reader is owed.**

First: *confirmed* here means confirmed **from source by adversarial review**, not observed on a running terminal. The author of this codebase has never run it on a real MetaTrader terminal — MT5 cannot be installed in the build environment — so section U exists precisely because compilation proves nothing about runtime.

Second: the 21 refutations are **not** failures of the audit, they are its quality control, and they are printed in section D with their reasons. An audit that refutes nothing has not been checked.

> **Incomplete.** These sections are not present in this build of the document: **A** (EXECUTIVE SUMMARY), **B** (CURRENT ARCHITECTURE ASSESSMENT), **D** (POTENTIAL TECHNICAL RISKS), **R** (COACHING / SESSION REVIEW), **S** (TRADE JOURNAL), **T** (PRIORITY ROADMAP), **U** (REAL MT5 TEST PLAN), **V** (RECOMMENDED NEXT DEVELOPMENT STEP).

### CRITICAL (2)

#### `host-expert-1` — OnInit's object sweep deletes the handover stash before it is read, so the second pass of one-window mode can never find its origin symbol

**`MQL5/Experts/SSReplay/SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1806`** · category: session-resume

```mql5
   SSRPurgeChart(0, SSR_PICK_LINE);
...
   string stashed = ReadStashedOrigin();          // line 1869
...
   if(ObjectFind(0, SSR_PICK_STASH) >= 0)         // line 1884
```

**What goes wrong:** With the shipped defaults (InpOneChart=true), pass 1 stashes the origin in the chart object SSR_ORIGIN_HANDOFF and hands the chart to the replay symbol. Pass 2's OnInit sweeps that object away at line 1806, 63 lines before it reads it at 1869, so stashed=="", origin=="" at line 1903, the on_replay && origin=="" branch fires at 1911 and FailInit() returns INIT_FAILED. Because g_origin is "", FailInit's chart-restore branch (825: `if(g_on_replay_chart && g_origin != "")`) does nothing, so the user is left on a chart showing a custom replay symbol with no expert on it and no automatic way back - the exact outcome the FailInit comment (810-821) exists to prevent. The picked start (SSR_PICK_HANDOFF) and the failed-pass poison ("!"+origin) are destroyed by the same sweep, so neither the recovery path nor the picked window can survive the handover either.

**Why:** SSRPurgeChart (Ui/SSR_Widgets.mqh:676-694) enumerates ObjectsTotal(chart,-1,-1) and deletes every name where StringFind(nm,"SSR")==0 unless nm equals the single `keep` argument. Both handoff objects are named with that prefix: #define SSR_HANDOFF "SSR_ORIGIN_HANDOFF" (line 536) and #define SSR_PICK_STASH "SSR_PICK_HANDOFF" (line 556); keep is SSR_PICK_LINE ("SSR_PICK_LINE", Ui/SSR_Theme.mqh:508). Both are created on chart 0 (ObjectCreate(0, SSR_HANDOFF, ...) line 540; ObjectCreate(0, SSR_PICK_STASH, ...) line 2536) - the same chart the sweep runs on, and the same chart that becomes the replay chart. The sweep is the second statement of OnInit and is unconditional. git log -S confirms the call was moved into OnInit by commit f3f7ddb (v102), after the stash mechanism it breaks (v55): this is a regression, not an original design. The claim needs no assumption about whether objects survive ChartSetSymbolPeriod - the delete and the read are in the same pass of the same function.

**Verifiers:** Traced exactly as described. SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1806 `SSRPurgeChart(0, SSR_PICK_LINE)` is unconditional and is the second statement of OnInit; SSR_Widgets.mqh:676-694 enumerates ObjectsTotal(chart,-1,-1) and deletes every object whose name starts with "SSR" except the single `keep` name (SSR_PICK_LINE, SSR_Theme.mqh:508). Both handoff objects are SSR-prefixed and created on chart 0 (SSR_ORIGIN_HANDOFF, #define at 536, created in StashOrigin; SSR_PICK_HANDOFF created at ~2536). ReadStashedOrigin() runs 63 lines later at 1869 and ObjectFind(0,SSR_PICK_STASH) at 1884 - both after the delete, in the same invocation. So on pass 2 stashed=="" -> origin=="" (1903) -> the on_replay&&origin=="" branch at 1911 -> FailInit(), whose restore branch is gated on g_origin != "" and therefore does nothing. No guard, clamp or earlier check anywhere prevents this; the outcome holds whether or not objects survive ChartSetSymbolPeriod. With the shipped default InpOneChart=true this makes every one-window run fail on the pass that owns the replay chart and strands the user on a custom-symbol chart with no expert / Provable from source with no runtime assumption required. SSRPurgeChart (Ui/SSR_Widgets.mqh:675-693) enumerates ObjectsTotal(chart,-1,-1) and deletes every object whose name satisfies StringFind(nm,"SSR")==0 unless it equals the single `keep` argument, which is SSR_PICK_LINE (Ui/SSR_Theme.mqh:508). Both handover objects match that prefix - SSR_HANDOFF="SSR_ORIGIN_HANDOFF" (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:536) and SSR_PICK_STASH="SSR_PICK_HANDOFF" (556) - and both are created on chart 0 (540, 2536), the same chart the sweep runs on. The sweep is at line 1806, unconditional; ReadStashedOrigin() is at 1869 and ObjectFind(0,SSR_PICK_STASH) at 1884, i.e. 63 and 78 lines later in the same invocation of OnInit. So `stashed` is always "", origin is "" at 1903, the guard at 1911 fires, and FailInit() (824-836) cannot restore the chart because its own guard tests g_origin != "". MQL5 semantics do not rescue this: ObjectGetString on a non-existent object cannot return the text, and whether chart objects survive ChartSetSymbolPeriod is irrelevant because the delete and the read are in one pass of one function. Corollary I verified while judging the rest of the batch: because `stashed` is always empty, the "!"-poison branch at 1894-1900 is also dead, so one_chart_ok can never diverge from InpOneChart anywhere in the program / Verified end to end. SSRPurgeChart (Ui/SSR_Widgets.mqh:676-694) enumerates ObjectsTotal(chart,-1,-1) and ObjectDelete()s every name where StringFind(nm,"SSR")==0 except the single keep argument, which here is SSR_PICK_LINE. SSR_HANDOFF=="SSR_ORIGIN_HANDOFF" (mq5:536) and SSR_PICK_STASH=="SSR_PICK_HANDOFF" (mq5:556) both match that prefix and are both created on chart 0 (540, 2536). The sweep is at 1806, unconditional, and ReadStashedOrigin() is at 1869 in the same function - 63 lines later. So on pass 2 stashed=="", origin=="" at 1903, the guard at 1911 fires and FailInit() returns INIT_FAILED; FailInit's restore branch at 825 requires g_origin!="" and is therefore skipped, leaving the user's chart pointed at a custom replay symbol with no expert and no automatic way back. This is the shipped default (InpOneChart=true, InpPickStart=true), so it is not an edge case - it is every normal run. Impact lens: the product does not function at all in its default configuration and it damages the user's workspace on the way out; the picked start and the '!' poison die in the same sweep, so neither the chosen window nor the two-window recovery path survives either. #### `trading-exec-1` — Rewind drops positions placed after the cut without reversing their P/L, commission and swap from the balance

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Trading/SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:640`** · category: event-handling

```mql5
long placed = (m_pos[i].request_msc > 0 ? m_pos[i].request_msc
                                        : m_pos[i].open_msc);
if(placed > msc)
   continue;

//--- every exit taken in the deleted future, newest first
UnwindLegsAfter(i, msc);
```

**What goes wrong:** State: a BUY is opened at 10:05 and closed at 10:10 with realised +50 (or by SL with -30), commission 7/lot charged twice. Action: step back to 10:00 (OnRewind(10:00)), or press Reset ('0' key -> GroupPort.Reset -> controller.Reset -> PublishRewind(start_msc)). Outcome: the position vanishes from the log but m_balance keeps the +50 (or -30) and the -14 commission and any accrued swap. After Reset the account shows an empty log with the whole session's realised P/L still in the balance; Equity, stats, prop-evaluation daily-loss/target and the next LotForRisk (sized off Equity()) are all computed on the corrupted figure. A later Save/Restore then prints the 'balance replayed from the trades is X, but the file recorded Y' warning because RestoreFrom recomputes balance from the log.

**Why:** The `continue` at line 643 skips the position entirely, so it is never copied to m_pos[keep] and none of the money it moved is reversed. The money was moved at Open() line 754 (`m_balance -= m_pos[i].commission`), CheckPendings line 356, BookExit line 222 (`m_balance += realised - fee`) and AccrueSwap line 427. The only reversal code, UnwindLegsAfter (263-291) and the un-fill branch (660-690), is placed AFTER the continue and only runs for kept positions. Nothing else recomputes m_balance from the log (grep of m_balance: lines 222, 273, 356, 427, 563, 579, 664, 754, 1167, 1221 only). T9.7 (lines 340-361) only asserts the ticket is gone, with an OPEN trade and commission 0, so the leak is invisible to the test. Fix: before `continue`, run UnwindLegsAfter(i, msc) (all legs are > msc) and then `m_balance += m_pos[i].commission - m_pos[i].swap`.

**Verifiers:** Traced OnRewind (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh 634-702): the `continue` at 643 fires for any position whose request_msc/open_msc is after the cut, BEFORE UnwindLegsAfter(646) and before the un-fill refund branch (660-690). The only money-reversing code in the class is UnwindLegsAfter (273) and that un-fill branch (664), both after the continue, so a position opened AND closed inside the deleted window keeps every balance move it made: Open() 754 (-commission), CheckPendings 356 (-commission), BookExit 222 (+realised-fee) and AccrueSwap 427 (swap). The trailing AccrueSwap() at 701 only restates positions still in m_pos, so a dropped position's swap is also stranded. The Reset path is real: SSR_GroupPort.mqh 425-437 -> CSSRReplayController::Reset (SSR_ReplayController.mqh 1268-1293) calls only PublishRewind(cut) at 1286 and never re-publishes OnSessionStart (the only place m_balance is reset, line 579), so after Reset the log is empty and the whole session's realised P/L, fees and swap remain in m_balance. Everything derived (Equity 971, FloatingPL, LotForRisk via Equity at 767/797, prop evaluation, statistics) reads that figure, and RestoreFrom 1221/1253 recomputes balance from the log so the 'balance replayed from the trades' warning does fire. T9_Trading.mq5 330-363 asserts only ByTicket/OpenCount and never the balance, so the leak is untested / Provable from source and reachable through a first-class button. In OnRewind the 'continue' at 642-643 drops a position placed after the cut before UnwindLegsAfter (646) and before the un-fill refund branch (660-690), so none of the money it moved is reversed: the entry commission (754, or 356 on a pending fill), every leg's realised - fee (222) and any accrued swap (427). The position is not copied to m_pos[keep], so the AccrueSwap restatement at 701 cannot refund its swap either, and no other code recomputes m_balance from the surviving log (only RestoreFrom 1167-1221 does, on file load). The Reset path is confirmed end to end: Panel 2241/2248 -> GroupPort.Reset 425-436 -> CSSRReplayController::Reset, which calls PublishRewind(cut) at 1286 with cut = timeline start and never re-runs OnSessionStart, the only code that restores m_balance = m_balance_initial (579). The host configures the account once, before Load (SSReplayStandalone 1167-1169), so a Reset leaves an empty trade log with the whole session's realised P/L, commissions and swap still in m_balance - and Equity(), LotForRisk sizing off Equity, the prop evaluation and the save-file balance check all read that figure. The test the finder names (T10.9, 'an order placed after the cut simply never existed', SSR_T10_Statistics.mq5 675-689) asserts only Total() == 0 on an open position with commission 0 from e.Init(), so the leak is invisible to the suite / Provable and reachable through the product's headline feature. OnRewind (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:640-643) `continue`s past any position whose placed msc > cut, so it is dropped from m_pos without any of its money being reversed: the entry commission subtracted at line 754 / 356, every leg's realised-fee added at line 222, and the swap moved at line 427 all stay in m_balance. The only reversal code (UnwindLegsAfter 263-291 and the un-fill branch 660-690) sits after the continue. Grep of m_balance writers (222, 273, 356, 427, 563, 579, 664, 754, 1167, 1221) shows nothing recomputes the balance from the log after a rewind, and OnSessionStart - the only place m_balance is reset to m_balance_initial - is published exactly once, from Load (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:837), never from Reset or a step-back. Every backward path lands here: SeekTo/step-back (controller 1240), Reset (controller 1286, which cuts to timeline.start_msc and therefore drops the ENTIRE session's trades while keeping their P/L, commission and swap in the balance), and checkpoint restore (1644). User-observable: an empty or truncated trade log with a balance that does not match it; Equity(), FloatingPL(), MarginLevel(), the prop-evaluation daily-loss/target gates and the next LotForRisk (sized off Equity()) all run on the corrupted figure, and a later Save/Restore surfaces it only as the soft 'balance replayed from the trades is X but the file recorded Y' warning (1253-1257). Silent money-arithmetic corruption in the core account, so CRITICAL stands

### HIGH (14)

#### `core-sync-1` — Group idle gap-skip fires mid-bar at human speeds and bulk-writes the unfinished bar, so observers (trading engine) never receive the rest of that bar's ticks

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Core/SSR_MasterClock.mqh:208`** · category: sl-tp-execution

```mql5
      else if(AnyPlaying() && ++m_idle_pumps >= 25)
        {
         m_idle_pumps = 0;
         long nb = NextBarAcross(m_master.now_msc);
         if(nb != SSR_INVALID_TIME && nb > m_master.now_msc + 2 * SSR_MSC_PER_MIN)
           { ... SeekAllTo(nb - 1); }
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Accurate as described, with one clarification: bar B is still drawn correctly on the replay chart (SeedBars writes it whole); what is lost is the observer stream - no OnBarContext and no OnTicks for bar B reach the trading/statistics engines, so a stop or target inside B's range is never evaluated and the engine's next price is bar nb's first tick. Trigger needs >= 2 consecutive missing M1 bars immediately after the current bar (so nb >= B_open+3min), which is the last bar of every index/futures CFD session, every weekend edge, and any 2-minute hole in thin forex.

**Why:** Trigger arithmetic: synthetic stamps are open + i*59999/7 (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:147), so at 1x consecutive ticks are 8571 ms apart and 25 pumps x 40 ms = 1 s of idle is reached inside every minute; the condition 'nb > now + 120000' with now = B_open + ~1s holds whenever the next existing bar is >= B_open + 3 min. Skip path: SeekAllTo (line 296) -> m_member[i].JumpTo(t) -> controller JumpTo (1484) -> JumpForward (1333): lo = m_cursor.emitted_msc + 1; bar_lo = SSRBarOpenMsc(lo) (1363-1364) which is B_open when B is partially emitted; last_bar = SSRBarOpenMsc(target) = nb - 60000 (1365); 'if(last_bar > bar_lo)' (1370) is true because nb - 60000 > B_open; ReadBars(bar_lo, last_bar - 1) returns bar B and m_sink.SeedBars(bulk, n) (1383) writes it; m_cursor.Advance(last_bar - 1, 0, n) (1390) moves the cursor past B. JumpForward never calls PublishBar/PublishTicks/OnClock (1333-1420) — the header comment says so ('publishes none of them', EA 2792-2794). The comment at lines 202-204 assumes 'the pause between two live ticks - never more than a minute of bar time - is left untouched', but the threshold is measured from the mid-bar clock, not from the current bar's end. Mt5 provider NextBarOpen (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:302-321) returns the first open strictly after after_msc via CopyTime, confirming nb = next EXISTING bar. Fix direction (RECOMMENDATION): measure the gap from the end of the current bar (BarOpen(now)+60000) rather than from now, or skip only when cursor.emitted >= BarOpen(now)+59999.

**Verifiers:** Traced end to end and found no guard. Synthesizer stamps are base+i*59999/(n-1) (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:147), so at 8 ticks/bar consecutive ticks are 8571 ms apart; InpPumpMs defaults to 40 (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:78) and g_group.Pump is called every timer tick (2788), so 25 emitted==0 pumps (=1 s) is reached inside almost every minute at human speeds. CSSRReplayGroup::Pump only resets m_idle_pumps when emitted>0 (206-208) and then measures the gap from m_master.now_msc, i.e. from the MID-BAR clock, not from the end of the current bar (212). NextBarAcross -> NextTimelineBarOpen -> CSSRMt5BarProvider::NextBarOpen (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:302-322) filters `open > after_msc`, so it returns the next EXISTING bar strictly after the mid-bar clock; with two or more missing M1 bars after the current bar B, nb >= B_open+180000 > now+120000 and the skip fires. SeekAllTo(nb-1) (296-322) -> controller JumpTo (1484-1519) -> JumpForward (1333): lo = m_cursor.emitted_msc+1 (mid-bar B, because EmitWindow advances consumed_to=hi every pump, SSR_ReplayController.mqh:523-531), bar_lo = B_open, last_bar = nb-60000 > bar_lo, so ReadBars(B_open, last_bar-1) returns bar B and m_sink.SeedBars writes it in bulk (1383) with the cursor advanced past it (1390). JumpForward never calls PublishBar/PublishTicks/OnClock, and CSSRTickObserver has no seek/jump callback at all (SSR_ITickObserver.mqh) - so the trading engine receives no OnBarContext and no ticks for bar B. The 'market closed from <mid-bar time>' print (214-216) is emitted from the same mid-bar instant / Every link is provable from source. Synth stamps are base+i*59999/(n-1) (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:147), so with InpTicksPerBar=8 and InpPumpMs=40 (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:75,78) consecutive ticks are 8571 ms of bar time apart and 25 empty pumps = ~1 s of wall time is reached inside a bar at any speed up to ~8x. NextTimelineBarOpen -> CSSRMt5BarProvider::NextBarOpen uses CopyTime and returns the next EXISTING bar open strictly after after_msc (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:302-323), so with the clock at B_open+dt the test nb > now+120000 is satisfiable exactly when the two M1 bars after B are absent (session close, weekend edge, 2-minute hole) - the threshold is measured from the mid-bar clock, not from B's end, as the comment at SSR_MasterClock.mqh:202-204 assumes. SeekAllTo -> JumpTo -> JumpForward then has lo = emitted+1 (mid-bar B), bar_lo = SSRBarOpenMsc(lo) = B_open, last_bar = nb-60000 > bar_lo, so ReadBars(B_open, last_bar-1) returns bar B and m_sink.SeedBars writes it in bulk (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1360-1390). JumpForward's bulk branch calls neither PublishBar nor PublishTicks (only Publish(), which touches state, and m_sink.OnSeek), and the trailing EmitWindow covers only [last_bar, nb-1], a minute with no bar, so it returns 0. CSSRTradingEngine drives CheckPendings/CheckStops/CheckStopout exclusively from OnTicks (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:600-615), so ticks 1..7 of bar B (its high/low/close path) are never evaluated; at BAR fidelity the bar's single tick at B_open+59999 is lost entirely. Chart correctness is preserved (the bar arrives via SeedBars); the loss is to observers / Every precondition is provable from source and the path is the only one the shipped host uses. The EA always pumps through the group (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1320 g_group.Add(g_ctrl), :2788 g_group.Pump(delta)) at InpPumpMs=40 with InpTicksPerBar=8, so at human speeds consecutive synthetic stamps are 8571 ms apart (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:147) and 25 emit-less pumps (1 s) elapse inside a bar whose path is only partly emitted. SSR_MasterClock.mqh:212 measures the gap from the mid-bar clock, not from the current bar's end, so whenever the next EXISTING bar (CopyTime-based, SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh NextBarOpen) is >= B_open+3min - the last bar before any daily close, any Friday close, any 2-minute hole - the test passes and SeekAllTo(nb-1) runs. JumpForward then bulk-writes bar B: lo=emitted+1 is still inside B so bar_lo=B_open, last_bar=nb-60000 > bar_lo, ReadBars(bar_lo,last_bar-1) includes B, SeedBars writes it and cursor.Advance(last_bar-1) steps past it (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1361-1391). SeedBars is a sink call only - no PublishBar/PublishTicks - and CSSRTradingEngine evaluates CheckPendings/CheckStops/CheckStopout exclusively inside OnTicks (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:600-616; OnClock only moves m_now_msc, :617). So the account never sees B's high/low: a stop or target inside that bar is not filled at its price and is instead evaluated against the next session's first tick, i.e. the gap price. That is corrupted money arithmetic in the virtual-trading guarantee, on the last bar before every closure, so HIGH is right. The chart itself is not blank (the candle arrives via SeedBars), which is why nothing looks wrong

#### `core-engine-4` — FULL_TICK window with zero broker ticks is consumed silently; tick availability is never re-evaluated per window

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Core/SSR_ReplayController.mqh:349`** · category: zero-empty

```mql5
            int n = tp.ReadTicks(m_state.symbol, lo - 1, hi, m_ticks);
            ...
            n = m_guard.FilterTicks(m_ticks, n);
            ...
            emitted = n;
            m_cursor.Advance(hi, emitted, 0);
            return emitted;
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Accurate as written, with one qualification: the retry path at SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:425-440 means a broker that answers a tick-less range with -1 rather than 0 would surface SSR_ERR_LOAD_FAILED instead of freezing silently. The silent-freeze outcome requires CopyTicksRange to return 0 for the range, which is the ordinary MT5 answer for held-but-empty tick history but is not verifiable from this repo.

**Why:** Lines 349-369: no branch handles n == 0 while bars exist; the only degradation trigger is `tp == NULL` (line 337-346), and CSSRFidelityPolicy::Decide (SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh line 114-118) consults m_ticks_available which is set only at Load (line 806) and at line 344. CSSRTickProvider::HasTicks(symbol, from, to) exists (SSR_IDataSource.mqh line 179) but is never called by the controller. Whether a given broker's tick depth is shorter than its M1 depth is an inference about deployments (it is the common case for MT5 brokers); the engine behaviour for that case is confirmed from code.

**Verifiers:** Traced the whole FULL_TICK branch and found no guard anywhere on the path. SSR_ReplayController.mqh:334-369: the ONLY degradation trigger is `tp == NULL` (337-346). #### `core-engine-1` — Per-pump budget cap silently DROPS bars instead of deferring them (dead 'stop short' branch)

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Core/SSR_ReplayController.mqh:524`** · category: future-data-leakage

```mql5

        {

...

```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: The logic error is exactly as described; two details in the write-up are wrong. (1) 'the UI reports the pump as deferred' overstates it: m_pump_deferred reaches only CSSRMetrics (perf.deferred_pumps) and CSSRPumpBudget::Deferrals(), and grep shows no UI consumer — SSRUiState carries no deferral field and BudgetText() is used only by SSR_T7_Performance.mq5:236, so the drop is not merely mislabelled, it is entirely unreported. (2) The PgDn scenario as written needs a calibrated us/tick high enough to clamp MaxTicks to 32 (cap 4 bars); with the uncalibrated fallback cap is 4096/8 = 512 bars, so the reachable triggers are a slow-calibrated machine plus either a >cap-bar step or a large owed window after a stall (at BAR fidelity, cap == MaxTicks, so >32 owed minutes). The determinism point stands: the cut-off is a function of wall-clock measurement, so the emitted stream is machine-dependent.

**Why:** Line 399-404 overwrite `nb = cap`. The loop at line 437 runs `i = first..nb-1` and increments `bars_used` for every iteration (w > 0 is guaranteed because m_ticks was resized to `need` at line 418), so after the loop `first + bars_used == nb` always holds and the condition at line 524 `(first + bars_used) < nb` is false whenever the cap bit. `consumed_to` therefore stays `hi` and line 531 `m_cursor.Advance(consumed_to, ...)` moves the cursor past the unread bars. The comment at lines 519-522 documents the opposite intent ('Anything above it stays owed'). T7.6 cannot catch this: after the capped pump it only checks that TicksEmitted keeps rising, which the following bars satisfy. Because the cap comes from wall-clock measurement (CSSRPumpBudget::MaxTicks via CSSRMetrics::UsPerTick), the emitted stream also becomes machine-dependent, breaking the determinism claim. Trigger frequency on a real terminal depends on the measured cost of CustomTicksAdd (unmeasured in the repo); the logic error itself is unconditional.

#### `core-engine-2` — StepBars(n) from a bar end advances n-1 bars; StepBars(1) is a no-op after the first step

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Core/SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1169`** · category: boundary

```mql5
      long base = SSRNextBarOpenMsc(m_clock.now_msc, PERIOD_M1);
      long nb   = NextTimelineBarOpen(m_clock.now_msc);
      if(nb != SSR_INVALID_TIME && nb > base)
         base = nb;
      long target = base + (long)(bars - 1) * SSR_MSC_PER_MIN - 1;
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Correct. Precise statement of the invariant: StepBars leaves the clock at (last emitted bar's open + 59999), and from that resting point the formula re-derives the same instant for bars == 1 and lands bars-1 bars ahead for bars > 1. So '->' is a no-op on every press after the first, and PgDn moves 9 bars instead of 10, until something else advances the clock (Play, a jump, or a backward step). The group path reports success (CSSRMasterClock::StepBars returns true) while nothing moves.

**Why:** SSRNextBarOpenMsc(msc) = SSRBarOpenMsc(msc)+60000 (SSR_Time.mqh line 37-43). For now = open+59999, SSRBarOpenMsc floors to `open`, so base = open+60000 and target = open+60000-1 = open+59999 = now. `nb` (first bar strictly after now) equals base in dense data and cannot raise it. Lines 1173-1178 then skip emission because now did not move. T1.7 (SSR_T1_CoreEngine.mq5 line 283-291) calls StepBars(1) ten times but asserts only `after10 > start`, which the first step alone satisfies; no test asserts the position after repeated steps.

**Verifiers:** Arithmetic verified against the helpers. SSRBarOpenMsc floors by PeriodSeconds*1000 and SSRNextBarOpenMsc adds one period (SSR_Time.mqh:27-43). The production path is identical, not merely analogous: CSSRMasterClock::StepBars (SSR_MasterClock.mqh:341-352) uses the same formula on the master, then PumpTo(t) per member, and AdvanceTo returns early on `t <= now_msc` (SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:131) so nothing is emitted — yet StepBars still returns true, so the panel (SSR_Panel.mqh:2293-2294 -> SSR_GroupPort.mqh:439) reports success. The test blind spot is as claimed: SSR_T1_CoreEngine.mq5:283-291 calls StepBars(1) ten times and asserts only `after10 > start`, which the first step alone satisfies; SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:743-752 asserts only that the clock moved at all / Fully provable from the integer arithmetic in source. #### `data-1` — has_ticks is probed over the last 24 hours of history but then selects FULL_TICK fidelity for a replay window that may be years earlier — the replay emits nothing, the clock runs to the end, and nothing reports it

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Data/SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:136`** · category: future-data-leakage

```mql5
      long to_msc   = out.last_msc;
      long from_msc = to_msc - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
      int  got = CopyTicksRange(symbol, probe, COPY_TICKS_INFO,
                                (ulong)MathMax(from_msc, 0), (ulong)to_msc);
      out.has_ticks = (got > 0);
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Correct as a trace; two qualifications. Category is wrong - nothing future-dated leaks; this is a range-blind capability probe producing a silent no-data replay plus a fidelity claim the run cannot honour. And the failure is not total: Decide() falls to SSR_FIDELITY_BAR on any bulk pump (owed_msc >= SSR_BULK_THRESHOLD_MSC, SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh:119-123), so bars DO flow at high speed and after jumps while a 1x pump emits nothing - which makes the symptom intermittent and the misdiagnosis worse rather than better. Severity HIGH rather than CRITICAL: the session visibly fails to play instead of producing wrong results, and no trade or price data is corrupted.

**Why:** The probe range is hardcoded to [last_msc-86400000, last_msc] — the newest day of history — and is the only thing that sets out.has_ticks. CSSRMt5DataSource::Ticks() (SSR_Mt5DataSource.mqh:91-96) returns the provider whenever m_has_ticks is true, so the engine's only fallback (`if(tp == NULL) { ... m_fidelity.SetTicksAvailable(false); }`, SSR_ReplayController.mqh:337-345) never fires. CSSRFidelityPolicy::Decide degrades FULL_TICK only on !m_ticks_available (SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh:114-118), which was set true. The range-aware question already exists — CSSRMt5TickProvider::HasTicks(symbol, from_msc, to_msc) at SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:379 — and a repo-wide grep shows it has no caller. This is exactly the failure the Ticks()-returns-NULL contract was written to prevent: its own comment at SSR_Mt5DataSource.mqh:86-89 says "Returning it unconditionally would let the engine run at FULL_TICK fidelity against an empty tick history and emit nothing - a replay that silently shows a frozen market." The file header itself states "Tick history is OPTIONAL and usually shallow, especially for CFDs" (lines 16-19). If CopyTicksRange instead returns -1 while the terminal tries and fails to fetch old ticks, ReadTicks burns its 15 s retry budget per pump and then returns -1, which at least surfaces an error — so the silent variant is the 0 case.

**Verifiers:** Every link in the chain checks out and I found no guard that breaks it. Discover()'s probe window is hardcoded to the newest 24h (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:135-139) and is the ONLY writer of out.has_ticks (grep confirms: the only other has_ticks assignment in production is the memory source). CSSRMt5DataSource copies it once (SSR_Mt5DataSource.mqh:68) and Ticks() returns the provider whenever it is true (91-96), so the NULL-fallback at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:337-345 never fires. Load() sets SetTicksAvailable(range.has_ticks) (806), and Decide() only degrades FULL_TICK on !m_ticks_available (SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh:113-117). With a non-bulk pump, EmitWindow takes the FULL_TICK branch, ReadTicks returns 0 with Succeed() (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:428-430: got==0 -> break -> return total==0), n>0 gates both EmitTicks and PublishTicks, and the code does `emitted = n; m_cursor.Advance(hi, emitted, 0); return emitted;` (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:365-368) - clock advances, nothing emitted, no warning. I grepped for any stall/zero-emit detector in Core and Data: none exists. CSSRMt5TickProvider::HasTicks(symbol, from, to) (line 379) genuinely has no production caller. #### `mt5-symbol-1` — Warmup repair after a jump is silently skipped whenever the seed was reused from the cache

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Mt5/SSR_CustomSymbolSink.mqh:265`** · category: session-resume

```mql5
bool is_warmup = (m_warmup_to_msc > 0 &&
                  SSRToMsc(bars[count - 1].time) <= m_warmup_to_msc);

if(m_reused_seed && is_warmup)
  {
   m_seed_bars += count;
   return true;
  }
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Not merely "a session where CanReuse returned true": because the handover only fires after pass 1 has seeded the warmup and saved the manifest, m_reused_seed is true on pass 2 of the DEFAULT one-window flow, so the silent repair no-op is on the normal path of every session, not an edge case.

**Why:** m_reused_seed is set once in Prepare (line 162) and never cleared for the life of the session; the early return keys only on it and on the bar range, so it cannot distinguish the initial warmup delivery (which the cache legitimately covers) from a later repair of bars the terminal has since discarded. The controller cannot tell either: SeedBars reports success. The next session self-heals only because CanReuse's SERIES_FIRSTDATE evidence check misses.

**Verifiers:** Full trace confirms the silent no-op, and it is worse than latent. m_warmup_to_msc is set by OnWarmupPlanned to m_timeline.start_msc-1 (Controller:814-816). RepairWarmupIfLost (Controller:934-968) re-reads exactly lo=warmup_first_msc..hi=start_msc-1, so bars[n-1].time <= m_warmup_to_msc and is_warmup is unconditionally true at Sink:262-263; with m_reused_seed still set the method returns true at 265-269 without calling WriteBars, and the controller logs "%d bars written back" at 963-967 regardless. m_reused_seed is assigned only in Prepare (Sink:145, 162, 170) and never cleared for the life of the session - there is no other writer in the file. The state is not exotic: pass 1 writes the manifest (Sink:283-293), so on pass 2 of the one-window handover CanReuse (SSR_SeedCache.mqh:161-196) finds a matching version/origin/range with the bars still in the symbol and returns true, meaning the repair is disabled for the normal second pass of every session. RepairWarmupIfLost is reached only from the jump path (Controller:1409), so every forward jump in such a session silently loses the warmup while reporting success / I tried to refute this on three fronts and failed on all three. (1) Range arithmetic: RepairWarmupIfLost reads lo = warmup_first_msc, hi = start_msc - 1 (Controller:951-952), and m_warmup_to_msc is set to exactly start_msc - 1 by OnWarmupPlanned (Controller:814-816 -> Sink:366-367). MqlRates.time is the bar OPEN, so SSRToMsc(bars[count-1].time) <= start_msc-1 always holds for the repair payload; is_warmup (Sink:262-263) is therefore unavoidably true on the repair call. (2) Flag lifetime: m_reused_seed is written in exactly three places, all inside Prepare - cleared at Sink:145, set from CanReuse at Sink:162, re-cleared only if Adopt fails at Sink:170. Nothing in SeedBars, EmitTicks, TruncateFrom, OnReset or Release clears it, so it stays true for the whole session. (3) Reachability: Prepare sets it true on pass 2 of the one-window handover and on T6 run 2, and RepairWarmupIfLost is reached from the jump/seek path at Controller:1409, right after the bulk write the comment blames for the loss. So SeedBars takes the early return at Sink:265-269, does m_seed_bars += count and returns true with WriteBars never called, and the controller - which only checks the boolean - logs 'the sink dropped the warmup ...; %d bars written back' (Controller:963-967). Silent no-op reported as a repair, repeating on every subsequent jump. The precondition (terminal discarding tick-less warmup bars) is the repair routine's own documented, measured trigger, not an assumption this finding introduces. refuted=true records that I could not break it; classification CONFIRMED / Provable end to end, and far more reachable than the finding suggests. m_warmup_to_msc is set to start_msc-1 (Controller:814-816); RepairWarmupIfLost reads lo=warmup_first_msc, hi=start_msc-1 and calls SeedBars (Controller:952-958), so bars[count-1].time <= m_warmup_to_msc and is_warmup is true; with m_reused_seed still true the early return at Sink:265-269 writes nothing and returns success, and the controller then logs "%d bars written back" (963-967). m_reused_seed is set once at Sink:162 and never cleared - not by TruncateFrom, not by OnReset - so the no-op repeats for the life of the session. Reachability: the seed cache is enabled by default (SeedCache:92, the host never disables it), the one-window handover is the default (InpOneChart=true) and is only performed once the replay symbol demonstrably HAS bars (Standalone:2609-2611), which means pass 1 always wrote the warmup and saved the manifest - so pass 2, i.e. every ordinary session, runs with m_reused_seed=true. Any forward jump (the only caller, Controller:1409, placed there precisely because the bulk write is what costs the warmup) therefore leaves the warmup permanently gone while reporting it restored. Observable: the replay chart loses all pre-session history, every indicator lookback on it is wrong for the rest of the session, and attached strategies trade off those values - and the one log line that would have revealed it says the opposite. #### `spikes-audits-1` — SSR_BarToTicks never emits a tick at the bar's high or low unless (n-1) is divisible by 3

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Spike/SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:579`** · category: sl-tp-execution

```mql5
double u   = (cnt == 1) ? 0.0 : (double)i * 3.0 / (double)(cnt - 1);
int    seg = (int)MathFloor(u);
if(seg > 2) seg = 2;
double f   = u - (double)seg;
double p   = k[seg] + (k[seg + 1] - k[seg]) * f;
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Confirmed and broader than the title: the same defect is in the shipping engine (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:134-144) at its default 8 ticks/bar, where the shortfall is ~14.3% of the adjacent leg, and because CheckStops evaluates SL/TP off the tick price alone it silently misses stops placed near a bar's extreme. The spike kit is only where it was first written.

**Why:** u only hits the integer keypoints when (cnt-1) is a multiple of 3. Replaying the formula for cnt in {4,7,10,16} gives an exact high and low; for cnt in {8,20,50} it does not (shortfalls of 1.43, 0.53 and 0.20 on an O=100/H=140/L=90/C=130 bar). cnt = MathMax(n,4) at kit:565, and the final forced write at kit:595-597 fixes only the close, never the extremes. The header at kit:560 calls this 'the same assumption the engine will make, tested here first', and the engine's CSSRTickSynthesizer::Synthesize (Include/SSReplay/Core/SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:134-143) is the identical formula with a default InpTicksPerBar of 8 - the worst case measured - while its own header (line 13) claims 'The OHLC of the resulting bar is exact'.

**Verifiers:** The arithmetic replays exactly and the defect reaches the product. In SSR_BarToTicks (SpikeKit:565-598) u = i*3/(cnt-1), so k[1] and k[2] are sampled only when some i makes u an integer, i.e. when (cnt-1)%3==0; the forced write at 594-597 fixes the close alone. For cnt=20 (B1:23 InpPerBar) the nearest samples to u=1 and u=2 are 0.9474/1.1053 and 1.8947/2.0526, giving the quoted ~5.3% shortfall on each extreme. Crucially CSSRTickSynthesizer::Synthesize (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:134-183) is the identical formula with m_ticks_per_bar defaulting to 8 (line 71) and InpTicksPerBar=8 in the shipping host (Standalone.mq5:75, 1148), where the step is 3/7 and the extremes are under-reached by 14.3% of the adjacent leg - contradicting the file header's "The OHLC of the resulting bar is exact" (line 11). The sl-tp-execution category is right, not a stretch: CSSRTradingEngine::OnTicks feeds m_bid/m_ask per tick and CheckStops (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:513-544) compares only that tick price against sl/tp, so a stop sitting in the outer 14% of the O-to-extreme leg is never triggered even though BarIsAmbiguousFor considers the bar's real range / I re-derived the arithmetic rather than trusting it, and it holds. u = i*3/(cnt-1) reaches the interior keypoints k[1] and k[2] exactly only when some i makes u == 1.0 and u == 2.0, i.e. when (cnt-1) % 3 == 0. cnt = MathMax(n,4) (SpikeKit:565). For B1's InpPerBar=20: cnt-1 = 19, nearest u values to 2.0 are 12*3/19 = 1.8947 (seg 1, f 0.8947) and 13*3/19 = 2.0526 (seg 2, f 0.0526), giving a peak of H - 0.0526*(H-C); nearest to 1.0 are 0.947 and 1.105, giving a trough of L + 0.0526*(O-L). On O=100/H=140/L=90/C=130 that is 139.47 and 90.53 - the 0.53 the finding states. The forced final write (SpikeKit:595-597) fixes only the close, and i = cnt-1 already lands on the close anyway (u=3 -> seg clamped to 2, f=1.0 -> p = k[3]). The load-bearing part is that the product shares the formula verbatim: CSSRTickSynthesizer::Synthesize (Core/SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:130-175) is the same u/seg/f interpolation with m_ticks_per_bar defaulting to 8 and the host input InpTicksPerBar = 8 (Standalone:75, 1148, 497). With n=8, cnt-1 = 7: the low is missed by 0.143*(O-L) and the high by 0.143*(H-C) - a 14.3% shortfall on every synthesised bar - while that file's own header line 12 states 'The OHLC of the resulting bar is exact'. No integer-division or array-bounds misreading is involved; the arithmetic is all double. Only cnt in {4,7,10,13,16,...} is exact. refuted=true records that I could not break it / The arithmetic checks out exactly. u = i*3/(cnt-1) reaches the interior keypoints only when (cnt-1) is a multiple of 3; for cnt=8 the samples straddle 1 and 2 at 0.857/1.286 and 1.714/2.143, so the nearest approach to the extreme keypoint k2 is k2 + (k3-k2)/7 - the replayed high falls short by (H-C)/7 and the low by (O-L)/7 on a bullish bar (1.43 on the finding's 100/140/90/130 bar, matching). The forced write at SpikeKit:595-597 (and Synthesizer:181-185) repairs only the close. What earns HIGH is not the spike file the finding is filed against but the identical formula in the shipped engine (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:134-143) with default InpTicksPerBar=8 (Standalone:75, 1148): live replay at synthetic fidelity puts bars into the symbol ONLY through these ticks - SeedBars/CustomRatesUpdate is used exclusively for warmup, repair and jump bulk (Controller:893, 960, 1383), and nothing ever rewrites a completed bar - so the replayed candle is genuinely narrower than the source bar and the virtual engine's stop/target checks never see the wick tip. ```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Accurate except for "no OnBarContext for the whole session": any pump owing >= SSR_BULK_THRESHOLD_MSC (10 minutes, e.g. after a real timer stall) degrades to SSR_FIDELITY_BAR in CSSRFidelityPolicy::Decide and does take the bar-driven path, publishing bars and refreshing the view. **Why:** Host SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1197 calls g_prop.Reset() (state RUNNING when enabled) and :1200 Watch(g_prop); g_ctrl.Load (:1252) fires OnSessionStart -> Reset() again (RUNNING); then :1483 g_session_mgr.Restore() -> SSR_SessionManager.mqh:381 m_group.At(i).NotifyRestored() -> SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1669 PublishRewind(m_clock.now_msc) -> every observer's OnRewind including this one, whose only guard is m_state != RUNNING. g_ctrl is in g_group (host :1320). **Verifiers:** Every link in the chain is in the source I read. Host: g_prop.Reset() runs unconditionally after SetRules and Watch(GetPointer(g_prop)) runs when CfgProp() (SSReplayStandalone.mq5, the prop block around l.1184-1203), and Watch() is g_ctrl.AddObserver (l.869-877), so the evaluation is an observer of g_ctrl. g_ctrl is m_group's first stream (l.1320 g_group.Add(GetPointer(g_ctrl))). g_ctrl.Load (l.1252) fans OnSessionStart out to every observer (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:835-837), whose override calls Reset() (l.343-349) leaving m_state = SSR_PROP_RUNNING because enabled. Later, l.1483 g_session_mgr.Restore(CfgSession()) ends with 'At(i).NotifyRestored()' per stream (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:379-381) = PublishRewind(m_clock.now_msc) (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1668-1669) = OnRewind on every observer (l.233-238). OnRewind's only guard is m_state != SSR_PROP_RUNNING (l.445-446), which does not hold, so the run goes VOID with m_pause_pending = true before a single candle plays, and the reason text asserts a backwards clock move that did not happen - the rewind is to 'now'. The pending pause is then consumed by CheckObserverPause at the end of the first Pump. Requires InpProp plus InpResume plus an existing session file, exactly as claimed / The whole chain is in source and unconditional. Host: g_prop.SetRules/Reset() (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1195-1197) leaves m_state = SSR_PROP_RUNNING whenever rules.enabled, Watch(g_prop) adds it to g_ctrl's observer list (Watch at l.869-871 calls g_ctrl.AddObserver), g_ctrl is in g_group (l.1320), and g_ctrl.Load fires OnSessionStart -> Reset() again (RUNNING). CSSRPropEvaluation::OnRewind guards only on enabled && state == RUNNING (l.445-446), so it flips to SSR_PROP_VOID and sets m_pause_pending, which CheckObserverPause consumes on the first pump. The reason string claims the clock moved backwards when the 'rewind' is to now_msc itself. No runtime assumption is involved - this is pure call-graph, and it disables the evaluation feature entirely for anyone who uses InpSession + InpResume / The chain is fully verifiable. Host: g_prop.Reset() at :1197 (state -> RUNNING when CfgProp()), Watch(g_prop) at :1200 adds it to g_ctrl's observers (Watch -> g_ctrl.AddObserver, :869-877); g_ctrl.Load at :1252 publishes OnSessionStart to every observer (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:835-837), whose prop override calls Reset() again -> RUNNING; g_ctrl is in g_group (:1320); then :1483 g_session_mgr.Restore -> SSR_SessionManager.mqh:378-381 m_group.At(i).NotifyRestored() -> SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1668-1669 PublishRewind(m_clock.now_msc) -> l.233-238 calls OnRewind on every observer, and CSSRPropEvaluation::OnRewind (l.443-452) guards only on enabled && RUNNING, so it goes VOID with a reason text asserting the clock moved backwards when in fact it was published AT now. I downgrade from HIGH because the failure is fail-safe and loud rather than silent: it produces VOID, never a false PASS or FAILED, announces itself through PauseRequested ('evaluation VOID - ...') and names the remedy. **`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Trading/SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:263`** · category: event-handling


**What goes wrong:** State: long at 1.1000 with trail_points=200 (SetTrailing is applied automatically to every new trade when a trail distance is set, GroupPort 1062-1063). Price runs to 1.1100 so ApplyTrailing moves sl to 1.1080 and trail_peak to 1.1100. Action: step back to the minute when price was 1.1020. Outcome: OnRewind keeps the position (placed before the cut) but leaves sl=1.1080 and trail_peak=1.1100. The first re-emitted tick has bid 1.1020 <= sl, so CheckStops closes the trade at StopFill = 1.1020 - slip, reason SL, and AutoPause announces 'stop loss hit' - at a moment when the stop had really been at 1.1000 and the trade was +20 pips. The same applies to a manual Modify() or BreakEven() done in the deleted future: the un-happened stop/target stays. mae/mfe and spread_at_exit likewise keep values from the deleted future for kept positions.

**Why:** SSRTradeLeg (SSR_TradeTypes.mqh 143-169) records only volume/price/msc/realised/fee/closing/prev_swap_locked/prev_swap_from_msc/prev_ambiguous. OnRewind (634-702) touches sl/tp/trail_peak/mae/mfe only in the un-fill branch for pendings (676-679) and never for a kept open position. ApplyTrailing (302-323) is the only writer of trail_peak and it only ever moves the long stop up (`if(want > m_pos[i].sl)`), so a future-trailed stop is never lowered again. CheckStops 526-527 then compares the current bid to that stale sl.

**Verifiers:** Verified from the leg struct and OnRewind. SSRTradeLeg (SSR_TradeTypes.mqh 143-168) stores volume/price/msc/realised/fee/closing/prev_swap_locked/prev_swap_from_msc/prev_ambiguous only - no sl, tp, trail_peak, mae or mfe. OnRewind (634-702) resets trail_peak/mae/mfe/risk_at_entry only inside the pending-un-fill branch (676-679); a position placed before the cut and still open is copied forward untouched (692-694), keeping the sl a future ApplyTrailing wrote. ApplyTrailing (302-323) only ever raises a long's sl (`if(want > m_pos[i].sl)`), so the future stop is never retracted, and on the first re-emitted tick CheckStops 526-527 compares the current bid to it and 539/543 books a SL close at StopFill (492-511) = bid - slip. GroupPort MarketAt/Market apply SetTrailing to every new trade when m_trail_points > 0 (SSR_GroupPort.mqh 1061-1063), so the trigger is one panel setting, not an exotic path. Modify (844-853) and BreakEven (920-927) write sl/tp with no versioning either, so a stop moved in the deleted future also survives / Provable from source. SSRTradeLeg (SSR_TradeTypes.mqh 144-168) records volume/price/msc/realised/fee/closing/prev_swap_locked/prev_swap_from_msc/prev_ambiguous and nothing about sl, tp, trail_peak, mae or mfe, so there is no snapshot for a rewind to restore. OnRewind (634-702) writes sl/tp/trail_peak/mae/mfe only inside the pending-un-fill branch (670-679); a position that was already open at the cut keeps every value the deleted future set. ApplyTrailing (302-323) ratchets one way only ('if(want > m_pos[i].sl)' for a long), so a stop trailed up in the deleted future is never lowered again, and CheckStops 526-527 compares the re-emitted bid against it, closing at StopFill (492-511) with reason SL. GroupPort 1060-1064 does arm trailing automatically on every risk-sized trade when m_trail_points > 0, so the precondition is a user setting, not an exotic path. Severity trimmed from HIGH: the fabricated SL close needs trailing armed or a Modify/BreakEven in the deleted future; what is unconditional for every rewound open position is stale mae/mfe (and spread_at_exit on a re-opened leg), which corrupts reported excursions rather than the balance / Confirmed from source and reachable without any unusual user action. SSRTradeLeg carries no sl/tp/trail_peak/mae/mfe, and OnRewind (634-702) rewrites those fields only inside the pending-un-fill branch (676-679); a position that was already open before the cut keeps whatever sl/tp/trail_peak/mae/mfe the deleted future gave it. ApplyTrailing (302-323) only ever ratchets the long stop up (`if(want > m_pos[i].sl)`) / the short stop down, so a stop trailed in the deleted future can never be walked back, and CheckStops (526-527) compares the re-emitted bid to that stale level. The trailing path is armed automatically, not manually: GroupPort.MarketAt applies m_trail_points to every new trade (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:1062-1063) and GroupPort.SetTrailing back-applies it to everything already open (811-829), so one typed trailing distance in the panel puts every subsequent trade on this path. The same hole covers a manual Modify (844-853) or BreakEven (920-927) performed in the deleted future. What the user observes: they step back to a moment when the trade was in profit, the very next re-emitted tick books it as 'stop loss hit' (auto-pause announces it) at a level the replay has just un-happened, and the loss lands in m_balance. That is future price data leaking across a rewind into a real money outcome, which is exactly the guarantee the file's own REWIND CORRECTNESS header claims, so HIGH is right

#### `host-expert-8` — Replay and extra-timeframe chart windows are leaked on every re-init that is not a user removal

**`MQL5/Experts/SSReplay/SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2203`** · category: object-lifecycle

```mql5
   bool user_removed = (reason == REASON_REMOVE || reason == REASON_PROGRAM ||
                        reason == REASON_CLOSE);
   if(user_removed)
     {
...
      g_charts.CloseOwned();
```

**What goes wrong:** The header of this file says a timeframe change on the host chart 'rebuilds the session from scratch. The replay chart is unaffected'. It is worse than unaffected: OnDeinit closes no chart unless the user removed the EA, and CSSRChartManager::OpenChart always calls ChartOpen with no reuse, so the rebuild opens a fresh set of windows and orphans the old ones. Two-window mode (InpOneChart=false): each period change on the host chart leaks one replay window plus one window per entry in InpExtraTfs. One-window mode: pass 2 opens the InpExtraTfs layout (1300-1305, g_replay_chart != 0 there), and every later REASON_CHARTCHANGE or REASON_PARAMETERS on that chart opens the layout again. A user who changes the period three times with InpExtraTfs="M15,H1" ends with six stale windows nothing will ever close; once the registry passes SSR_MAX_CHARTS the newest ones also lose the follow policy (Chart/SSR_ChartManager.mqh Sync, m_untracked). The same path leaks a window when BuildSession returns false after opening the replay chart, because INIT_FAILED deinits with a reason that is not in the user_removed set.

**Why:** OnDeinit's only close site is inside `if(user_removed)` (2203, plus 2206 for the extra streams); REASON_CHARTCHANGE, REASON_PARAMETERS, REASON_RECOMPILE and REASON_INITFAILED all fall outside it, as the comment at 2115-2122 intends for the symbol but not for the windows. CSSRChartManager::OpenChart (Chart/SSR_ChartManager.mqh:204-215) is `long id = ChartOpen(m_symbol, tf); ... NoteOwned(id)` with no search for an existing chart on that symbol/period, and OpenLayout (229-242) just calls it per timeframe. The new pass's g_charts is a freshly constructed object, so the previous ids are no longer owned; CSSRLeakGuard only counts charts (Chart/SSR_LeakGuard.mqh:44-63), it never closes one.

**Verifiers:** Confirmed by trace. CSSRChartManager::OpenChart (SSR_ChartManager.mqh:204-215) is an unconditional ChartOpen + NoteOwned with no search for an existing chart on that symbol/period, and OpenLayout (229-242) just loops it. The only close site in the whole Chart tree is CloseOwned (line 292; grep for ChartClose finds no other), and OnDeinit calls it only inside `if(user_removed)` at 2202-2206, so REASON_CHARTCHANGE, REASON_PARAMETERS, REASON_RECOMPILE and REASON_INITFAILED all leave the windows open while the replay symbol is deliberately kept. The next pass's manager is a fresh object, so the old ids are no longer in m_owned and Sync (332-377) only discovers and policies them - it never closes. CSSRLeakGuard::Scan (SSR_LeakGuard.mqh:44-63) only counts. So each non-removal re-init opens a new replay window plus one per InpExtraTfs entry and orphans the previous set / Verified. OnDeinit's only close sites are inside `if(user_removed)` at 2201-2211, and user_removed covers REMOVE/PROGRAM/CLOSE only, so REASON_CHARTCHANGE, REASON_PARAMETERS, REASON_RECOMPILE and REASON_INITFAILED all skip CloseOwned. CSSRChartManager::OpenChart (Chart/SSR_ChartManager.mqh:204-215) is an unconditional ChartOpen + NoteOwned with no search for an existing chart on that symbol/period, and OpenLayout (229-242) loops it. Crucially I confirmed the ownership gap the claim rests on: Sync() registers a rediscovered chart with Add(id) only (332-351), never NoteOwned, and CloseOwned closes m_owned exclusively (278-306) - so windows left by a previous instance are tracked but can never be closed by any later pass. Add() also returns -1 past SSR_MAX_CHARTS (82-83), so surplus windows drop out of the follow policy as claimed. The INIT_FAILED leak is sound under MQL5 semantics: OnDeinit runs with REASON_INITFAILED after OnInit returns a non-zero value, which is outside the user_removed set / Confirmed from source on all three legs: OnDeinit's only close sites are inside `if(user_removed)` (2203/2206) and REASON_CHARTCHANGE, REASON_PARAMETERS, REASON_RECOMPILE and REASON_INITFAILED all fall outside it; CSSRChartManager::OpenChart is an unconditional ChartOpen + NoteOwned with no search for an existing chart on that symbol/period (Chart/SSR_ChartManager.mqh:204-215) and OpenLayout just loops it (229-242); CloseOwned walks m_owned (278-306), which a freshly constructed manager on the next pass no longer holds; and the destructor is empty (139). Reachable without any other fix: in two-window mode (InpOneChart=false, a configuration a user can and does pick) simply clicking OK in the inputs dialog raises REASON_PARAMETERS and orphans the previous replay window, and the same happens on every recompile. Kept at MEDIUM rather than raised: the leak is visible - stale windows on a replay symbol the user can close by hand - and costs no money arithmetic or data integrity; kept at MEDIUM rather than lowered because it accumulates silently, the orphans keep showing a frozen replay that looks like the live session, and past SSR_MAX_CHARTS the newest windows also drop out of the follow policy

#### `chart-4` — Blind mode's record of the user's original chart settings does not survive a reinit, and the next Apply saves the blinded state as the original

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Chart/SSR_BlindMode.mqh:152`** · category: session-resume

```mql5
      if(Find(chart_id) < 0)
        {

            return false;

```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Accurate. Worth adding that the poisoned-record path is only one of two: if the rebuilt instance never calls BuildSession, m_policy is never set, RestoreAll() is a no-op over an empty registry, and the chart stays blind with no record at all - so the chart is left blinded across a non-user-removal deinit regardless of whether Apply runs again.

**Why:** The save-once guard is keyed on Find(chart_id) within the live instance only; nothing persists m_had_dates/m_had_ohlc/m_had_price (no session-file field, no terminal global - grep for CHART_SHOW_DATE_SCALE matches only this file). The chart properties themselves are terminal state and outlive the program, so after a reinit the 'before' state is unrecoverable. One-chart mode guarantees at least one reinit per session (the handover), and that first one is harmless only because pass 1 has no chart on the replay symbol yet (Expert:1421-1425 with Count()==0); every later reinit while blind is applied poisons the record.

**Verifiers:** Every link in the chain is present in source. CSSRBlindMode::Apply (SSR_BlindMode.mqh:147-176) records m_had_dates/m_had_ohlc/m_had_price only when Find(chart_id) < 0, and Find scans only the live instance's m_id[0..m_saved). The record has no persistence: a repo-wide grep for CHART_SHOW_DATE_SCALE / CHART_SHOW_OHLC / CHART_SHOW_PRICE_SCALE matches only this file and the QA smoke test - no session-file field, no terminal global. OnDeinit (SSReplayStandalone.mq5) computes `user_removed = (reason == REASON_REMOVE || REASON_PROGRAM || REASON_CLOSE)` and calls g_blind.RestoreAll() only inside that branch (line 2176), so REASON_CHARTCHANGE / REASON_PARAMETERS / REASON_RECOMPILE tear the instance down with the chart still blinded. The rebuild then re-runs BuildSession, which calls SetPolicy (1002) and Apply on every synced chart (1421-1430); with m_saved back at 0 the already-hidden properties are recorded as the originals, and Restore (184-186) later writes those falses back. Chart properties are terminal state and outlive the program, so the true 'before' values are unrecoverable. The one runtime dependency is MQL5 reinitialising program globals across a deinit/init cycle, which is standard terminal behaviour rather than broker-specific; on that basis I cannot refute it / The control flow is provable. OnDeinit computes user_removed = (REASON_REMOVE || REASON_PROGRAM || REASON_CLOSE) (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2152-2153) and calls g_blind.RestoreAll() only inside that branch (2176), so REASON_CHARTCHANGE / REASON_PARAMETERS / REASON_RECOMPILE leave the chart blind. Nothing persists m_had_dates/m_had_ohlc/m_had_price: they are plain member arrays (SSR_BlindMode.mqh:117-119), CollectSettings writes no such field, and a repo-wide grep shows CHART_SHOW_DATE_SCALE / CHART_SHOW_OHLC / CHART_SHOW_PRICE_SCALE are touched only in SSR_BlindMode.mqh and the QA smoke script. The global CSSRBlindMode is reconstructed on reload with m_saved = 0 (SSR_BlindMode.mqh:131), so Find(chart_id) < 0 and Apply() records the already-hidden values as the originals (152-164) - the exact failure the boxed comment at 143-145 warns about, defended against only within one instance's lifetime. I also checked the branch the finding does not mention: if the rebuilt pass never reaches BuildSession, SetPolicy is never called, IsOn() is false and RestoreAll() restores nothing, so the chart stays blind anyway. Both branches end with the user's date scale, OHLC and price scale off. Residual runtime dependence is only that a chart's display properties outlive an EA reload, which is standard MT5 chart-level state and is the same assumption the class itself is built on / Mechanism verified. The save-once record is per-instance only: m_id/m_had_* are private members with no persistence anywhere (grep for CHART_SHOW_DATE_SCALE hits only this file), the guard is Find(chart_id) < 0 against the live registry (line 152), and OnDeinit calls g_blind.RestoreAll() only inside `if(user_removed)` (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2152 defines user_removed as REMOVE/PROGRAM/CLOSE; 2176 restores). REASON_CHARTCHANGE / PARAMETERS / RECOMPILE therefore destroy the record while the chart stays hidden, and the rebuilt instance's Apply (via BuildSession:1421-1430 or the housekeeping loop at 2822-2824) records the already-hidden values as the originals, so the eventual Restore writes false back. Only properties the policy actually hides are poisoned, which matches the claim in FULL. Downgraded from MEDIUM on impact: the consequence is that the user's own chart (one-chart mode; tool-opened charts are closed on removal anyway) comes back with date scale, OHLC and price scale off - three checkboxes in the chart properties dialog, self-evident on sight and trivially reversible. No trade data, journal, money arithmetic or session content is lost, and nothing about virtual-trading safety is weakened

#### `chart-3` — The blind-mode reveal is undone within ~200ms: RestoreAll leaves the policy on and the host re-applies on IsOn()

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Chart/SSR_BlindMode.mqh:203`** · category: session-resume

```mql5
      while(m_saved > 0)
         if(Restore(m_id[0]))
```
