LOW, not HIGH

#### `strategy-integration-report-2` — OnBar is detected from the last tick of a published batch, so its firing point and the resulting fill price are functions of wall-clock pump boundaries

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Strategy/SSR_StrategyHost.mqh:184`** · category: tick-ordering

```mql5
      long now = ticks[count - 1].time_msc;
...
         long bar_open = SSRBarOpenMsc(now, m_tf[i]);
...
         else if(bar_open > m_last_bar[i])
           { m_last_bar[i] = bar_open; m_bar_calls++; m_strat[i].OnBar(); }
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: The defect is real; the worked arithmetic is not. With the defaults, InpPumpMs=40 caps a starved pump at ceiling = 4*40 = 160 ms of wall time (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2754-2759), so at the ladder's top (SSR_SPEED_MAX = 100000, i.e. 1000x) one FULL_TICK batch covers at most ~160 s of replay. That is enough to contain two or three M1 boundaries - so M1 bar closes are genuinely skipped - but not two M15 boundaries. Skipping an M15 close additionally requires a larger InpPumpMs (e.g. 250 ms, giving a 1000 s ceiling at 1000x).

**Why:** The host reads only ticks[count-1] and derives bar_open from it; every tick before the last in the batch is invisible to the bar-close test. Contrast CSSRTradingEngine::OnTicks, which loops over all count ticks updating m_bid/m_ask/m_now_msc and calling CheckStops per tick - the account is therefore batch-size independent and deterministic, while the strategy layer is not. In the bar-driven path the batch is one M1 bar's ticks (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:506-507), and whether that bar arrives whole or clipped mid-minute depends on where the pump's `hi` landed (ClipBar, SSR_ReplayController.mqh:159). In the FULL_TICK path the batch is the entire window (line 366), so the number of bar boundaries inside one batch is unbounded and m_last_bar jumps over the ones in between, silently.

**Verifiers:** Both halves check out against the source. CSSRStrategyHost::OnTicks derives `now` solely from ticks[count-1] (184), computes bar_open from it (194) and can advance m_last_bar past several boundaries in one step (202-207), so any bar close that is not the last boundary in the batch is silently skipped - and OnTick likewise fires once per batch, not per tick. In FULL_TICK the batch is the whole window (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:366), so the number of boundaries inside one batch is bounded only by the pump ceiling. The wall-clock dependence is also provable: SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2735 computes `delta` from GetMicrosecondCount() and feeds it to Pump, which reaches m_clock.Advance(wall_delta_ms) (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1006), so window boundaries - and in the bar-driven path the ClipBar/tick-trim boundary at 459-470 - move with CPU load, which moves the tick on which OnBar fires and therefore the Bid/Ask the strategy reads and the price the engine fills at. Contrast confirmed: CSSRTradingEngine::OnTicks iterates all ticks, so the account layer is batch-independent while the strategy layer is not. This breaks the explicit contract at SSR_IStrategy.mqh:20-24 / The mechanism is source-provable. The host reads only ticks[count-1] (184) and derives bar_open from it, so every earlier tick in the batch is invisible to the `bar_open > m_last_bar[i]` test (202-207) and m_last_bar jumps straight over any intermediate boundary; contrast CSSRTradingEngine::OnTicks, which iterates all ticks, making the account batch-invariant. Batch size is a wall-clock artefact: Pump takes wall_delta_ms (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:996, whose own comment only promises determinism for 'identical delta sequences'), the FULL_TICK branch publishes the whole window in one PublishTicks (366), and in the bar-driven path the newest bar is ClipBar'd at wherever `hi` fell (159, 280-309), so the replay instant at which OnBar fires - and hence the ctx.market.Bid()/Ask() CSSRRefBreakout tests at RefStrategy:115 and the price the engine fills at - moves with pump boundaries / The mechanism is confirmed. The host reads only ticks[count-1].time_msc (line 184) and derives bar_open from it, so every earlier tick in the batch is invisible to the bar-close test, and OnBar therefore fires at whatever replay instant the batch happens to end on. In the bar-driven path that instant is wall-clock dependent through clipping: the per-M1-bar segments are built from ClipBar against the pump's `hi` (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:~455 and 506-507), so whether the first M1 bar of a new group arrives whole or clipped mid-minute - a function of the wall delta the clock scaled - moves the Bid()/Ask() the strategy sees at OnBar and hence the fill CSSRTradingEngine gives it and whether CSSRRefBreakout's `sl >= Bid()` gate trips. Contrast with CSSRTradingEngine::OnTicks, which loops all count ticks and calls CheckStops per tick, is correct: the account layer is batch-size independent while the strategy layer is not. Downgraded from HIGH: nothing here corrupts money arithmetic or weakens the virtual-only guarantee - the account still prices every tick - the strategy layer is opt-in, and the per-run deviation is a few ticks of entry price. It breaks reproducibility for strategy trades, which is a documented promise, so MEDIUM rather than lower

#### `trading-analytics-4` — Class report and CSV consumers see a different per-trade result than the statement (raw profit vs net)

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Trading/SSR_Journal.mqh:82`** · category: commission

```mql5
p.profit, p.commission, p.swap,
         //--- R is left EMPTY, never zero, when it does not exist:
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: A three-column CSV layout (profit / commission / swap) is defensible on its own - MT5's own statement uses it. The actual defect is that the CSV's only consumer classifies with the wrong column: SSR_ClassReport.mqh:259-266 derives won/lost from the raw 'profit' column while the journal and SSR_Statistics define a result as profit + swap - commission, so with a non-zero commission or swap the class report's win rate (and the '# net_profit' header versus the sum of the 'profit' column) contradicts the statement written from the same trades. Either the CSV needs a 'net' column that ReadOne prefers, or ReadOne must combine the three columns it already has.

**Why:** Row() writes p.profit raw (l.82) with no net column; ExportHtml computes net = p.profit + p.swap - p.commission for its Profit column (l.394) and ComputeFor uses the same net for wins/losses (SSR_Statistics.mqh:431-450). ClassReport ReadOne locates only 'open_time', 'profit', 'r' columns (l.243-245) and derives won/lost from 'profit' (l.259, 266). With the default commission 0 and swap 0 all three agree, which is why no test catches it.

**Verifiers:** Traced and provable. SSR_Journal.mqh:72-89 Row() writes p.profit raw into the 'profit' column with commission and swap as separate columns and no net column (header l.218-220). ExportHtml computes 'double net = p.profit + p.swap - p.commission' (l.394) for its Profit column, and CSSRStatsEngine::ComputeFor uses the identical net for wins/losses/gross/net_profit (SSR_Statistics.mqh:429-448) - the comment at 405-427 records exactly this accounting split being fixed for the statement. Commission really is charged twice per round trip (Open l.753, closing leg l.203/218), so at InpCommission=3 a 1-lot +2 trade nets -4 while the CSV 'profit' says +2. SSR_ClassReport.mqh:242-244 locates only open_time/profit/r and 259-266 derives won from that raw 'profit' (pnl > 0.0), so the class report marks it won. '# net_profit' (l.201) is the net sum and no longer equals the sum of the printed 'profit' column. Default commission 0 and swap 0 make all three agree, which is why QA does not catch it / Verified in source. Row() (SSR_Journal.mqh:69-90) writes p.profit, p.commission, p.swap as three raw columns; ExportHtml (l.394) and CSSRStatsEngine::ComputeFor (SSR_Statistics.mqh:430-452, with its own comment about exactly this trap) define the result as profit + swap - commission, and win/loss classification uses that net. SSR_ClassReport.mqh (l.240-266) locates only 'open_time', 'profit', 'r' and sets out.won = (pnl > 0.0) from the raw 'profit' column, so with a non-zero InpCommission/InpSwap a trade that made +2 and cost 3 to place is a loss in the statement and a win in the class report. Latent only because InpCommission, InpSwapLong and InpSwapShort all default to 0.0 (host l.90-93), which is why no test catches it / The mechanics are as described and provable: Row() (l.72-89) writes p.profit raw with commission and swap as separate columns, ExportHtml's Profit column writes net = profit + swap - commission (l.394, 421), ComputeFor uses the same net to decide wins/losses and net_profit (SSR_Statistics.mqh:429-434, 512), and CSSRClassReport::ReadOne locates only open_time/profit/r and sets out.won = (pnl > 0.0) from the raw column (SSR_ClassReport.mqh:243-245, 259-266). But the impact is much smaller than MEDIUM. Points (a) and (b) of the claim are not defects: profit / commission / swap as three separate columns with a net total in the header is exactly the convention MT5's own HTML statement and every broker statement use, so `# net_profit` not equalling the raw sum of the `profit` column is correct labelling, not a contradiction - and the CSV carries both components, so a reader can net. The only real defect is (c): this product reads its OWN file with a different accounting rule than it wrote it with, and out.won drives nothing but the colour of one marker in the class-report timeline (SSR_ClassReport.mqh:573). The class report's profit_factor rendering is even guarded (l.622). Requires InpCommission != 0 or a swap input (all default 0). User-observable effect: a green dot where a red one belongs on a coach's timeline

#### `trading-analytics-12` — A jump forward never runs the evaluation; a jump that completes the window leaves it IN PROGRESS

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Trading/SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:358`** · category: prop-rules

```mql5
virtual void      OnClock(const long now_msc) override
     {
      if(!m_rules.enabled || m_state != SSR_PROP_RUNNING || m_acct == NULL)
         return;
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Accurate for the jump-to-end case, with two refinements: (a) when the forward jump does NOT complete the replay, the next Pump's OnClock does judge - RollDay recomputes m_total_days from the new day index, so the deadline fires late rather than never; what is permanently lost is any breach or target reached inside the skipped span (equity is only sampled at the jump's end). (b) The 'review card' does not print the verdict - SSR_Review.mqh has no prop fields; the stuck 'IN PROGRESS' shows in the HTML statement (SSR_Journal.mqh:286-297) and the panel's prop sheet.

**Why:** SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1333-1420 JumpForward calls EmitWindow, m_sink.OnSeek, Publish() and Transition(COMPLETED) but contains no m_obs[i].OnClock loop, unlike Pump (l.1027-1029) and PumpTo (l.1102-1104); Pump early-returns when status != PLAYING (l.998). The evaluation has no OnTicks override, so OnClock is its only judging point.

**Verifiers:** Provable. A full grep of MQL5/ finds exactly two OnClock fan-out sites, SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1027-1029 (Pump) and 1102-1104 (PumpTo); JumpForward (l.1333-1419) does the bulk SeedBars, EmitWindow for the partial bar, m_sink.OnSeek, RepairWarmupIfLost, Publish and Transition(COMPLETED) with no observer OnClock loop and no CheckObserverPause. CSSRPropEvaluation overrides only OnClock/OnRewind/OnSessionStart, so the ticks EmitWindow publishes reach it not at all. JumpForward is user-reachable: JumpTo (l.1484-1519) is the 'unified entry point: the panel and the dialog both call this' and forwards to it. When the jump lands on the timeline end, m_clock.IsCompleted() transitions to COMPLETED, Pump early-returns 0 for any status != PLAYING (l.997-998), and Play() refuses outright after COMPLETED (l.971-976) - so no OnClock ever runs again and State() stays SSR_PROP_RUNNING, which the statement prints as 'IN PROGRESS' (SSR_Journal.mqh:286-297 via StateName(), SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:57). The per-pump rather than per-tick judging is also correct as described / Confirmed by reading all three paths. CSSRPropEvaluation overrides only OnClock and OnRewind (no OnTicks), so OnClock is its only judging point. Pump (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1027-1029) and PumpTo (l.1102-1104) each run the OnClock loop after EmitWindow; JumpForward (l.1333-1418) does SetHorizon, bulk SeedBars, EmitWindow for the partial bar, m_sink.OnSeek, RepairWarmupIfLost, Publish and Transition(COMPLETED) with no OnClock loop anywhere, and JumpTo forwards every forward jump to it (l.1519). Pump/PumpTo both early-return 0 when status != PLAYING (l.997-998, 1071-1072), so once the jump lands on the timeline end and the clock completes, no OnClock ever fires again and the state stays SSR_PROP_RUNNING -> StateName() 'IN PROGRESS' in both Report() (used by the statement, SSR_Journal.mqh:295) and the panel. The secondary point is also accurate: even in normal play the rules are evaluated once per pump against end-of-pump equity, so an intra-pump breach that recovers is not seen / Verified line by line: JumpForward (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1333-1419) does the bulk SeedBars, EmitWindow for the partial bar, m_sink.OnSeek, RepairWarmupIfLost, Publish and Transition(COMPLETED) - and contains no m_obs[i].OnClock loop, unlike Pump (l.1027-1029) and PumpTo (l.1102-1104); Pump returns 0 immediately when status != PLAYING (l.997-998). CSSRPropEvaluation overrides only OnSessionStart, OnClock, OnRewind and PauseRequested - no OnTicks - so OnClock is its sole judging point, yet the trading engine DOES process the emitted ticks, so stops fill and equity moves through the whole jumped span unjudged. JumpTo is the unified panel/dialog entry point (l.1482-1519), so this is a first-class control, not an edge path. I upgrade from LOW because the consequence is a dishonest verdict, not a cosmetic one: a jump that reaches the window end leaves the exported statement and review card printing 'IN PROGRESS' forever, and - worse - a daily-loss or drawdown breach that occurred inside the jumped span and had recovered by the next pump is never judged at all, so a run that should read FAILED can go on to read PASSED. Only the once-per-pump granularity remark is unavoidable design rather than defect

#### `trading-analytics-2` — Prop evaluation state is not persisted; a resumed or reset run re-bases every rule on current equity

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Trading/SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:366`** · category: session-resume

```mql5
if(!m_started)
        {
         m_started     = true;
         m_first_day   = now_msc / SSR_PROP_DAY_MSC;
         m_day         = m_first_day;
         m_day_open_eq = eq;
         m_peak_eq     = eq;
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Accurate, with the sequencing worth stating: after a resume the evaluation is already SSR_PROP_VOID (see trading-analytics-1), so OnClock early-returns at l.360 and the re-basing only takes effect once the user presses Reset - which finding 1 forces them to do. Note also that the omission is a recorded design decision (docs/audit/maps/ui-port-session.md:247-248 'Not stored: ... the prop evaluation'), so this is an acknowledged gap rather than an accidental one; the wrong-verdict consequence is real either way.

**Why:** The class has no SaveInto/RestoreFrom (grep of the file). SSR_SessionManager.mqh:195-200 and 367-375 save/restore only m_acct and m_stats. Reset() (l.327-341) and the first-clock branch (l.366-377) initialise every counter from m_rules.start_balance / current Equity(). The trading engine and the equity curve ARE restored, so the account carries its history while the judge forgets it.

**Verifiers:** Traced and provable. CSSRPropEvaluation has no SaveInto/RestoreFrom (grep of the file: none), and CSSRSessionManager writes only the streams, m_acct and m_stats (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:193-198) and restores only those (l.366-374); docs/audit/maps/ui-port-session.md:247-248 states outright 'Not stored: ... the prop evaluation'. Reset() (l.327-341) re-bases m_peak_eq/m_low_eq/m_day_open_eq on m_rules.start_balance, zeroes m_trading_days and m_total_days, and takes m_last_positions from the restored count; the first-clock branch (l.366-377) then overwrites m_peak_eq/m_day_open_eq with CURRENT equity and sets m_total_days = 1 and m_first_day to the resumed day. So with trailing rules the total floor rebases to 9400-1000 = 8400 instead of 10000-1000 = 9000, the deadline restarts at day 1 of 30, and the minimum-days count restarts at 0 - while the account and its equity curve ARE restored. The verdict genuinely differs from the same trades taken in one sitting, and it differs in the trader's favour / Verified: SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh contains no SaveInto/RestoreFrom (the whole 481-line file was read), and CSSRSessionManager persists only the group streams, m_acct and m_stats (Save l.193-199, Restore l.366-375) - so no prop counter is written to or read from the session file. Reset() (l.327-341) re-bases m_peak_eq/m_low_eq/m_day_open_eq on m_rules.start_balance and zeroes m_trading_days/m_total_days, and the first-clock branch (l.366-377) then overwrites m_peak_eq, m_day_open_eq, m_low_eq with current Equity() and sets m_total_days = 1. With trailing on and equity at 9400 that makes TotalFloor() 8400 rather than 9000, restarts the deadline at day 1 and the min-days count at 0, while the account and the equity curve are restored in full - so the judge forgets a history the account still carries / Confirmed: CSSRPropEvaluation has no SaveInto/RestoreFrom (nothing in the 481-line file), and CSSRSessionManager persists only the streams, m_acct and m_stats (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:194-200) and restores only those (l.361-375). So the account, its trades and the equity curve come back while the judge's peak, day index, day-open equity, trading-day count and elapsed-day count do not. Combined with trading-analytics-1 (resume forces VOID, so the user must press Reset), the first OnClock after the reset takes the m_started branch (l.366-377) and sets m_peak_eq = m_day_open_eq = current restored equity and m_total_days = 1. With trailing rules, a trader who is 600 down gets TotalFloor() re-based to 8400 instead of 9000 - a fresh full 10% allowance carried on an account that has already spent part of it - and the deadline and min-days counters restart. That is a path to a PASSED verdict an unbroken run would have FAILED, with nothing on the panel saying the peak was re-based, which is why MEDIUM is right and I do not downgrade it to a missing feature. One detail in the claim is off: Reset() itself sets m_peak_eq/m_day_open_eq to m_rules.start_balance (l.335-338); the re-basing to current equity happens on the next OnClock, not in Reset

#### `trading-analytics-3` — Closed-only drawdown walks trades in open order, not close order

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Trading/SSR_Statistics.mqh:703`** · category: drawdown-calc

```mql5
for(int i = 0; i < total; i++)
        {
         SSRVirtualPosition p;
         if(!m_acct.At(i, p) || !p.IsClosed())
            continue;
         bal += p.profit + p.swap - p.commission;
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Accurate for max_drawdown_closed. The secondary remark about win_streak/loss_streak is weaker: counting streaks by entry order is a defensible convention, so only the balance-curve drawdown (and, per trading-analytics-7, revenge) is provably wrong.

**Why:** At(i) returns positions in slot (creation) order (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:1005-1011, m_pos appended in Open() l.719). Nothing sorts by close_msc before accumulating bal/peak/worst. The same slot-order walk also drives win_streak/loss_streak/revenge in ComputeFor (l.406-513). T10.2 (SSR_T10_Statistics.mq5:204) only checks a sequential, non-overlapping case.

**Verifiers:** ClosedDrawdownFor (SSR_Statistics.mqh:694-717) accumulates `bal += p.profit + p.swap - p.commission` while walking i=0..total-1 through m_acct.At(i, p), and At() is a straight slot read (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:1004-1011) with slots appended in Open() order (l.719) and never sorted or compacted - I grepped the engine for ArraySort/ArrayRemove/compaction and there is none. Nothing orders by p.close_msc, and slot order is not even open order for pendings (open_msc is stamped at request time, l.734). So whenever positions overlap the running balance follows a path the account never took and the peak/worst pair is wrong, as the finder's A/B/C example shows. The wrong number is printed as 'Max drawdown, closed only' (SSR_Journal.mqh:1129-1130) and as 'Drawdown / On closed trades' (SSR_Review.mqh:135), and the statement asks the reader to compare it against the equity drawdown. MEDIUM is fair: a user-visible metric is wrong under ordinary multi-position use, with no guard / Provable from source and arithmetic. ClosedDrawdownFor (SSR_Statistics.mqh:697-719) accumulates bal in At(i) order, which is creation/open order (m_pos append-only, SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:719; At :1005; nothing sorts by close_msc anywhere in the engine - I grepped for ArraySort/compaction and found none). A closed-trade balance curve is by definition ordered by close time, so whenever closes are out of open order the walked curve never existed. I checked the example: real path 10000->11000->10500->10400 has worst 600; slot order gives 9900->10900->10400, worst 500. The figure is published, not internal (SSR_Journal.mqh:1130, SSR_Review.mqh:135 'Drawdown / On closed trades'), and T10.2 only covers a sequential case. This is ordinary control-flow, not runtime-dependent / ClosedDrawdownFor (l.697-719) accumulates bal in At(i) slot order with nothing sorting by close_msc, and slot order is creation order (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:1004-1011 At, Open appends at m_count++ l.719). The finder's worked example is arithmetically right (600 real vs 500 reported). Overlap is the normal case here, not an exotic one: the panel opens multiple positions, CloseAll/BreakEvenAll act on all of them, and pendings take their slot at placement, so the balance path walked is not the path the account took. The number is printed as 'Max drawdown, closed only' with copy inviting the reader to compare the gap with the equity drawdown (SSR_Journal.mqh:1128-1131) and is re-parsed into the class report, so a wrong value is read as a conclusion about holding losses. MEDIUM is right: money-shaped reporting error, reachable by default, but no effect on balance, equity, or the virtual-trading guarantee

#### `trading-exec-5` — Ambiguity test uses the whole bar range, so a target hit after a mid-bar entry is booked as a stop loss when the bar's earlier low was below the stop

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Trading/SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:164`** · category: sl-tp-execution

```mql5
if(p.IsLong())
  {
   sl_in = (m_bar.low  <= p.sl);
   tp_in = (m_bar.high >= p.tp);
  }
...
return (sl_in && tp_in);
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: BarIsAmbiguousFor (164-174) tests the whole cached M1 range, which includes price printed before a mid-bar entry, so pre-entry excursion is charged to the position. Reachable when the stop sits ABOVE the bar's earlier low for a long (e.g. buy the breakout at tick 3 with a tight stop 10 points under the entry while tick 2 already printed a low 30 points lower) and the target is inside the bar's high: CheckStops 537-541 then books SSR_CLOSE_SL at StopFill and flags the trade ambiguous although every tick from the entry onward was above the stop. The claim's illustration ('SL 5 points below that bar's low') does not trigger it - with sl below the bar low, sl_in is false. The same whole-bar test at 371-384 flags a pending fill against a low printed before the fill. mae (293-300) already holds the post-entry excursion the test should use.

**Why:** m_bar is the bar cached by OnBarContext (593-598); ClipBar in the controller only trims it to the pump window end (controller 446-459), so inside one emitted segment it is the full minute. BarIsAmbiguousFor (141-175) never compares open_msc with the ticks already seen nor uses the running excursion (mae, updated at 293-300, already records the worst move since entry). CheckStops 537-541 calls it whenever either level is touched. This is a stated pessimism policy, but the pessimism is applied to price that occurred before the position existed, which the design comment (9-20) does not claim.

**Verifiers:** The mechanism is provable: BarIsAmbiguousFor (141-175) compares p.sl/p.tp against the whole cached m_bar low/high and never against open_msc or the running mae (293-300); m_bar is the full minute up to the pump-window end (OnBarContext 593-598; ClipBar keeps 'everything in this minute UP TO the window's end - including the part an earlier pump already emitted', SSR_ReplayController.mqh 446-459). CheckStops 537-541 therefore books ClosePosition(StopFill, SSR_CLOSE_SL, true) - a loss plus slippage - even when every tick after the entry stayed above the stop, and the fill-time flag at 371-384 has the same whole-bar test. BUT the claim's own numbers are self-refuting: with 'SL 5 points below that bar's low' the test `m_bar.low <= p.sl` is FALSE and no ambiguity is raised. The defect needs the stop ABOVE the bar's earlier low, which the title states correctly / The finding's core premise is that the engine's own synthesised tick order is evidence about what happened. The file states the opposite at lines 11-20 ('that ORDER IS OUR ASSUMPTION, not the market's behaviour'), and it is true: an M1 bar cannot say whether the minute's low printed before or after the instant the user clicked Buy mid-minute, so for a mid-minute entry whose stop sits under that minute's low the outcome genuinely is unknowable and the pessimistic-plus-flag policy (R11) is exactly what is documented. The one case where unhappened price would be used is already guarded twice: ClipBar (ReplayController 240-279) rebuilds a forming bar from only the ticks up to the pump window end, and BarIsAmbiguousFor 156-158 rejects a cached bar the current tick does not live in. 'Every synthesised tick after the entry was above the stop' is precisely the self-flattery the design refuses, and the trade is flagged rather than silently booked, with AmbiguousPercent reporting the fraction. No defect provable from source; at most a possible refinement (weighting by entry time within the minute), which would itself require inventing intra-minute order / The code path is provable: BarIsAmbiguousFor (141-175) tests p.sl/p.tp against m_bar.low/m_bar.high with no reference to open_msc, to the ticks already seen, or to the running mae (which UpdateExcursions 293-300 already maintains), and CheckStops (537-541) routes any touched level through it, booking ClosePosition(i, StopFill(i), SSR_CLOSE_SL, true). The bar it tests is the whole minute up to the pump window end - ClipBar (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:269-300, called at 459) deliberately rebuilds the shown bar from the bar's own open, 'the window's LOWER bound is deliberately not applied' - so a low printed in an already-emitted segment, before the position existed, still makes a later TP hit book as a stop loss. Reachable in the stated way (SYNTHETIC_TICK is the automatic fidelity whenever the broker has no real ticks, SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1153-1154) and user-visible: the chart the user watched shows price never returning to the stop after their entry, yet the journal records SL and marks the trade ASSUMED. Not upgraded past MEDIUM because the loss is flagged rather than hidden and the mid-bar entry instant itself sits on the synthesised timeline, so some pessimism here is defensible; the defect is its extent, not its existence. The fill-time half of the claim (371-384) only sets an honesty flag and moves no money

#### `trading-exec-6` — No margin check on entry when margin is modelled: an unaffordable order is accepted, charged, then stopped out on the next tick

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Trading/SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:741`** · category: margin

```mql5
bool is_long = SSRIsLong(type);
m_pos[i].state        = SSR_POS_OPEN;
m_pos[i].open_price   = FillPrice(is_long, true);
...
m_pos[i].commission = m_exec.commission_per_lot * volume;
m_balance          -= m_pos[i].commission;
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Open() performs no free-margin check before booking a fill, so when margin is modelled an unaffordable order is accepted, charged, and then liquidated by CheckStopout on a later tick instead of being rejected at zero cost. Reachable only when the user sets both InpMarginLot > 0 and InpStopout > 0 (both default 0), so it is an opt-in fidelity gap rather than a default-path defect.

**Why:** Open() 705-756 checks capacity, volume > 0, price > 0 and nothing else; OpenWithRisk/OpenPendingWithRisk (759-801) add only sizing checks. FreeMargin() (946) is defined but a repository-wide grep finds no caller outside the engine. CheckStopout (436-470) is the only margin enforcement and runs after the fill.

**Verifiers:** Open() (705-756) checks capacity, Reserve, volume > 0, m_bid > 0 and, for pendings, price > 0 - nothing else; it then fills at FillPrice and debits commission at 753-754. OpenWithRisk/OpenPendingWithRisk (759-801) add only lot-sizing checks. FreeMargin() (946) and MarginLevel() (949) exist but no caller in the engine or in GroupPort/Publisher/Strategy gates an entry on them, and CheckStopout (436-470) runs from OnTicks 613 only after the fill, so the oversized position is charged round-turn commission (BookExit 203) and slippage (StopFill/FillPrice) before being force-closed as SSR_CLOSE_STOPOUT with m_stopouts++ (464). Margin modelling is opt-in (InpMarginLot default 0.0, SSReplayStandalone.mq5 94-95), which bounds the blast radius but does not refute the path / The absence is provable: Open() 705-756 performs no affordability test, OpenWithRisk/OpenPendingWithRisk 759-801 add only sizing checks, FreeMargin() (946) has no production caller anywhere in the tree (only SSR_T10_Statistics.mq5 461 reads it), and CheckStopout 436-470 runs from OnTicks 613 only after the fill has been booked and its commission taken at 753-754. So with margin modelled, an order that a terminal would refuse with 'not enough money' at zero cost is instead accepted, charged entry commission, then force-closed by CheckStopout at FillPrice(...,false) with a second commission and adverse slippage, incrementing m_stopouts and tripping the SSR_PAUSE_ON_STOPOUT announcement. Severity cut from MEDIUM: the whole path needs two non-default inputs (InpMarginLot > 0 and InpStopout > 0, both default 0.0 at host lines 94-95), and MarginModelled() is explicitly an opt-in model / Confirmed: Open() (705-756) validates capacity, volume > 0 and m_bid > 0 and nothing else; OpenWithRisk/OpenPendingWithRisk add only sizing checks; FreeMargin() (946) has no caller anywhere outside SSR_T10 (repo-wide grep), and CheckStopout (436-470) runs only from OnTicks, i.e. after the fill and after the commission has been taken (754). Reachable without a deliberately silly order: LotForRisk (SSR_RiskEngine.mqh:95-134) sizes from Equity and a stop distance and caps only at vol_max, so a tight-stop entry legitimately produces a lot whose margin exceeds the account whenever margin is modelled. What the user observes is a trade a terminal would have refused at zero cost being accepted, charged commission, then stopped out on the next tick at bid-slip with a second commission, incrementing Stopouts and firing the 'stop out' auto-pause. Kept at MEDIUM rather than higher because both InpMarginLot and InpStopout default to 0, so the harmful cascade is opt-in (or depends on the origin symbol declaring SYMBOL_MARGIN_INITIAL), and the money lost is modelling error rather than a safety-guarantee breach - no real order exists

#### `trading-exec-8` — BreakEven/Modify accept a stop on the wrong side of the market and the engine then closes the trade instead of rejecting the change

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Trading/SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:920`** · category: sl-tp-execution

```mql5
bool              BreakEven(const long ticket)
  {
   int i = Find(ticket);
   if(i < 0 || m_pos[i].state != SSR_POS_OPEN)
     { m_last_error = "no open position"; return false; }
   m_pos[i].sl = m_pos[i].open_price;
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: BreakEven sets a long's stop to its ask-side fill price and CheckStops tests it against the bid, so the condition px <= sl is already satisfied when the stop is written: pressing 'be' before price has advanced past the entry spread closes the trade on the very next tick as an SL. This holds even with zero spread and zero slippage, where sl == open_price == bid triggers on equality (a flat 'stop loss' in the statistics). Modify() has the same missing wrong-side check, and neither path marks the close as a rejected modification.

**Why:** BreakEven (920-927) and Modify (844-853) write sl/tp with only a state check; neither compares against m_bid/m_ask. GroupPort.BreakEven/BreakEvenAll (867-915) add no price check either. CheckStops treats any sl on the wrong side as an immediate hit and StopFill (492-511) takes the worse of level and price, so the fill is at the current market minus slippage.

**Verifiers:** Traced end to end with no guard anywhere. BreakEven (920-927) sets sl = open_price after only a state check; for a long open_price = FillPrice(true,true) = ask + slip (743), which is above the bid by the whole spread plus slippage. On the next tick CheckStops 526-527 evaluates `px <= sl` with px = m_bid and fires; with tp == 0 BarIsAmbiguousFor returns false at 160-161, so 543 closes at StopFill = min(sl, bid) - slip = bid - slip, i.e. a guaranteed loss of spread + 2x slippage booked as SSR_CLOSE_SL. Modify (844-853) writes any sl/tp with no side check. No caller filters: GroupPort BreakEven (867-874) and BreakEvenAll (899-914) only null-check m_acct, and the panel wires them raw ('be' button SSR_Panel.mqh:2116, per-row action 2679) with no price comparison / Provable from source and stronger than the finding states. BreakEven (920-927) sets sl = open_price with only a state check, and for a long open_price = FillPrice(true,true) = m_ask + slip (743), while CheckStops compares px = m_bid against it (524-527). Since bid <= ask always, the new stop is at or above the comparison price from the moment it is written, so the very next tick satisfies px <= sl and ClosePosition books reason SL at StopFill = min(sl, bid) - slip (492-511) - a loss of the spread plus slippage, counted as a losing trade and announced by the SSR_PAUSE_ON_SL watcher. No guard exists upstream either: GroupPort.BreakEven 867-874 and BreakEvenAll 899-914 pass the ticket through untouched, and Modify 844-853 writes any sl/tp with no comparison to m_bid/m_ask. A terminal rejects a long SL above bid (invalid stops) and leaves the position running, so nothing about this depends on unsettled runtime behaviour / Confirmed and easy to reach. BreakEven (920-927) writes sl = open_price with only a state check, and open_price for a long is FillPrice(true,true) = ask + slip, i.e. strictly above the current bid; Modify (844-853) writes any sl/tp with no side check; GroupPort.BreakEven / BreakEvenAll (867-915) add none either. CheckStops (526-527) then reads px = bid <= sl as a stop hit and StopFill (492-511) takes min(level, price) - slip, so the position is closed at bid - slip: a certain loss of spread + slippage, booked with reason SL, counted as a losing trade by Statistics, and announced by auto-pause. The worst reachable case is the panel's one-press BreakEvenAll, which moves EVERY open stop to its entry including positions currently in drawdown - each of those has open_price on the wrong side of the market and is force-closed at market on the next tick, so a user who meant 'protect my winners' silently liquidates their losers. A real terminal rejects the modification ('invalid stops') and the position keeps running. MEDIUM is right: reachable through ordinary UI use and it manufactures closed losing trades, but each individual loss is small (spread + 2x slippage) and nothing beyond the virtual account is touched

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Accurate. Two notes: the 39.05 ms figure is quoted from SSR_Widgets.mqh:31-38 and is not a measurement of this path, so the latency claim is unvalidated (hence MEDIUM); and there is an additional, unprovable-from-source risk the finding does not raise - the sheet's OBJ_BUTTONs (buy, sell, openln, px0.., flat, be, stmt) are deleted and recreated 10 times a second, and the panel learns about clicks by polling the latched OBJPROP_STATE (SSR_Widgets.mqh:338-347), so a press that latches while Render() is executing is destroyed with the object.

**Why:** HideSheets() (:1284) is called unconditionally as the first statement of DrawSheet, and its id list at :1301-1316 contains the ids of EVERY sheet including the one about to be drawn ('risklbl','riskval','riskmon','slrow','tprow','rrrow','sizerow','hintrow','setuprow','openln','flipbtn','enbtn','clrbtn','buy','sell','g1_fr','g1_lb','g1_lg','g2_fr','g2_lb','g2_lg'...). CSSRWidgets::Remove (SSR_Widgets.mqh:627-633) does ObjectDelete then Forget. DrawSheet is called from Render() at :752 (rail) / :757 (fallback) on every frame, i.e. every 100 ms (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3063). Per frame the cost is 70 named Remove() + 4*3 meter Remove() + SSR_POS_MAX(12)*6 row Remove() = 154 ObjectFind+Forget, plus ~20-25 ObjectCreate and their full property writes to rebuild the sheet. The project's own measurement is 561 property writes = 39.05 ms mean repaint (SSR_Widgets.mqh:31-38), which is the whole reason the cache exists.

**Verifiers:** HideSheets() is the unconditional first statement of DrawSheet (:1270-1272), and its id list (:1301-1316) names the objects of EVERY sheet including the one about to be drawn on this frame - risklbl, riskval, riskmon, slrow, tprow, rrrow, sizerow, hintrow, setuprow, openln, flipbtn, enbtn, clrbtn, buy, sell, g1_fr/_lb/_lg, g2_fr/_lb/_lg, taglbl - plus the four meters (3 objects each) and SSR_POS_MAX=12 rows of 6 objects each. CSSRWidgets::Remove does ObjectDelete then Forget (SSR_Widgets.mqh:627-633), which invalidates both caches: CSSRPanel::Text()'s early return requires m_w.Exists(id) (:194-198) and CSSRWidgets::Same() requires ObjectFind>=0 (:90). DrawSheet is reached from Render() at :752/:757 on every non-compact frame, i.e. every 100 ms per SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3062-3066. The tagbox is the one exception (Hidden, not Removed). This does break the project's own written invariant at :2999-3004 and the assertions I read at SSR_T5_Ui.mq5:236 (spent<=2) and SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:5045 (cached_labels==0) - neither of which can have been run, since MT5 is not installed here / Provable. DrawSheet (:1270) calls HideSheets() as its first statement, HideSheets's id list (:1301-1316) contains the ids of every sheet including the one about to be drawn, and CSSRWidgets::Remove (SSR_Widgets.mqh:627-633) is ObjectDelete + Forget. DrawSheet is reached every non-compact frame (:752/:757), and Render() runs on the host's 100 ms gate (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3063-3067). Both caches are therefore defeated by construction: CSSRPanel::Text requires m_w.Exists(id) (:198) and Same() requires ObjectFind >= 0 (SSR_Widgets.mqh:86-88). I checked the two cited assertions: on the default Trade tab with lines unarmed, risklbl/riskmon/riskval/hintrow alone give Writes() >= 4 on a still frame, so SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:5045-5046 (cached_labels == 0) and SSR_T5_Ui.mq5:236 (spent <= 2 over 20 renders) cannot pass, and the invariant documented at :2994-2998 does not hold / Provable. HideSheets() is the unconditional first statement of DrawSheet (:1270-1284) and its id list (:1300-1316) contains the ids of the sheet about to be drawn ('risklbl','riskval','riskmon','slrow','tprow','g1_fr','g1_lb','g1_lg','g2_fr',...); Remove() does ObjectDelete + Forget, so both caches miss on every frame - the panel's Text() cache because Exists(id) is false and the widget cache because Same() checks ObjectFind. That provably breaks the documented still-frame invariant at :2994-2998 and the assertions in SSR_T5_Ui.mq5:236 (spent <= 2 over 20 identical renders) and SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:5046 (cached_labels == 0). Downgraded from HIGH on impact: the user-visible consequence is paint cost, which is unvalidated, and the 561-writes = 39.05 ms arithmetic conflates a whole-repaint time with a per-write cost. No wrong value is shown and no state is corrupted - there is no moment where a stale or missing sheet is visible, because ChartRedraw only runs at the end of Render()

#### `ui-panel-5` — Two cache slots (12 and 17) write the same object 'setuprow' at the same coordinates, so order_why is visible for one frame only

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Ui/SSR_Panel.mqh:1432`** · category: redraw

```mql5
         if(m_state.order_why != "")
            Text(17, "setuprow", x + 8, gy + 12, m_state.order_why,
                 SSR_C_STOP, SSR_FS_SMALL);
```

**What goes wrong:** With lines armed and an illegal geometry (order_why = e.g. 'drag the stop below the price'), the reason is drawn on the frame the string first changes and is overwritten by 'LONG setup'/'SHORT setup' on every subsequent frame - so at 10 fps it is on screen for ~100 ms and then gone for good. The user is told only 'cannot place' on the openln button and never why, which is the opposite of what the comment at :1424-1430 claims the slot split achieved.

**Why:** Both Text(12, "setuprow", x + 8, gy + 12, ...) at :1402 and Text(17, "setuprow", x + 8, gy + 12, ...) at :1432 target the SAME object id at the SAME x,y. Text() (:194-207) keys its early return on (slot, text, x, y, Exists(id)) and returns after only setting OBJPROP_COLOR. Because HideSheets() deletes 'setuprow' at the top of every DrawSheet (:1270, id listed at :1306), Text(12) always finds Exists==false and writes the side text; Text(17) then finds the object present with m_cache[17] == order_why and x,y unchanged, takes the early return, and leaves the side text in place. Only on the frame where order_why's value differs from m_cache[17] does the second call actually write.

**Verifiers:** Traced both calls. Text(12,"setuprow",x+8,gy+12,...) at :1402 and Text(17,"setuprow",x+8,gy+12,...) at :1432 write the SAME object id at the SAME coordinates; I grepped the slot numbers and 17 is used nowhere else, so m_cache[17] holds order_why persistently. Because HideSheets() deleted "setuprow" at :1270 (id listed at :1306), Text(12) can never take its early return (m_w.Exists is false) and always writes the LONG/SHORT side text; Text(17) then finds the object present with m_cache[17]==order_why and x,y unchanged, takes the early return at :196-200 and only sets OBJPROP_COLOR. So the reason survives exactly one frame - the frame its string value changes - and thereafter the side text stands in its place. An extra detail the finding does not mention: on those frames the early return paints the side text in SSR_C_STOP, so the row reads as a red "LONG setup" while the openln button says only "cannot place" / Provable by walking the cache. Text(12, "setuprow", x+8, gy+12, ...) at :1402 and Text(17, "setuprow", x+8, gy+12, ...) at :1432 address the same object id at the same coordinates. Text()'s early return (:195-201) keys on (m_cache[slot], m_cache_x, m_cache_y, m_w.Exists(id)) and returns after only ObjectSetInteger(OBJPROP_COLOR). HideSheets() Removes "setuprow" (:1306) at the top of every DrawSheet, so slot 12 always misses on Exists and writes the side text; slot 17 then finds the object present with m_cache[17] == order_why and the same x,y, takes the early return, and leaves "LONG setup"/"SHORT setup" on the chart tinted SSR_C_STOP. order_why is therefore on screen only on the single frame its value differs from m_cache[17] - about 100 ms at the host's paint gate - and the user is left with only T(SSR_S_CANNOT_PLACE) on the openln button / Provable, and the mechanism is exactly as stated. Both :1402 (slot 12) and :1432 (slot 17) write id 'setuprow' at the same (x+8, gy+12). HideSheets() deletes 'setuprow' at the top of every DrawSheet, so Text(12) always misses on Exists(id) and writes the side text, recreating the object; Text(17) then finds m_cache[17]==order_why with x,y unchanged AND Exists(id) now true, takes the early return at :196-200, and only sets OBJPROP_COLOR. The reason is therefore on screen for the single frame its value changes (~100 ms) and never again, including if the same reason recurs after order_why has been empty. Impact is a real loss of actionable feedback at the moment of placing a trade, which is why it stays MEDIUM rather than dropping to LOW - though it is partly mitigated: the surviving 'LONG setup'/'SHORT setup' text is painted in SSR_C_STOP by the early return, so the user does get a red signal plus 'cannot place' on the openln button, just not the reason

#### `ui-dialogs-7` — The range dialog enables START for any date the broker can serve, but its only caller can only jump inside the already-loaded window

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Ui/SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:139`** · category: boundary

```mql5
   bool              CanStart(void)
     {
      return (m_req.IsComplete() && m_quote.IsFeasible() &&
              (m_problem == "" || StringFind(m_problem, "warning") == 0));
     }
```

**What goes wrong:** Press J, type a date three months before the replay window but well inside broker history, press START. Every check passes (the catalogue has that history), m_confirmed is set and the dialog closes - and then nothing at all happens on screen: the host only jumps when the date lies inside [g_group.StartMsc(), g_group.EndMsc()) and otherwise just prints 'that range needs a fresh session' to the Experts log. The dialog refuses what the BROKER cannot serve and accepts what the SESSION cannot serve, which is the opposite of what its only use needs; the title 'NEW SESSION' and the button 'START' reinforce the wrong expectation.

**Why:** g_dialog.Open() is reached only from RunHostCommand(SSR_CMD_JUMP) (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3096-3103), which seeds start=g_group.Now(), end=g_group.EndMsc(). The confirm handler is SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3181-3192: `if(r.start_msc >= g_group.StartMsc() && r.start_msc < g_group.EndMsc()) g_group.JumpTo(...) else Print(...)`. CanStart's validation comes from SSRValidateRange(m_req, m_cat) (:135), which measures against cat.EarliestStart/cat.LastMsc - the broker's M1 range - and knows nothing about the loaded window. Close() runs before the host's check (:313-318), so there is no surface left to report the refusal on.

**Verifiers:** Traced end to end and every link holds. RunHostCommand(SSR_CMD_JUMP) (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3093-3106) is the ONLY caller of g_dialog.Open(); it seeds r.start_msc = g_group.Now(), r.end_msc = g_group.EndMsc(). Because start_msc > 0 the catalogue-default branch in Open() (SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:105-110) is skipped, so the user's typed start is validated only by SSRValidateRange (SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:135), which measures against cat.EarliestStart(warm) and cat.LastMsc() (SSR_SessionRange.mqh:82-87) - the BROKER's M1 range, with no knowledge of the loaded replay window. CanStart() (:139-143) therefore returns true for any broker-servable date, 'start' sets m_confirmed and calls Close() (:313-318), and only then does RouteEvent check `if(r.start_msc >= g_group.StartMsc() && r.start_msc < g_group.EndMsc())` else Print(...) (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3181-3192). Close() has already destroyed every object (:115-122), so no surface remains to report the refusal; the user gets a closed dialog and an Experts-log line. Title is literally "NEW SESSION" and the button "START" (SSR_Strings.mqh:517-518), reinforcing the wrong expectation. No guard, clamp or earlier check anywhere narrows the accepted set to the loaded window / Verified end to end. CSSRRangeDialog::CanStart (SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:139-143) gates only on m_req.IsComplete(), m_quote.IsFeasible() and m_problem, and m_problem comes from SSRValidateRange (SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:135), which measures exclusively against cat.EarliestStart(warm) and cat.LastMsc() (SSR_SessionRange.mqh:78-92) - the broker's M1 catalogue, never the loaded window. The only caller is RunHostCommand(SSR_CMD_JUMP) (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3095-3106) and the only consumer of the confirmed request is SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3181-3192, which jumps only when r.start_msc is in [g_group.StartMsc(), g_group.EndMsc()) and otherwise only Prints. OnEvent calls Close() (SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:313-318) before the host sees the request, and Close() does m_w.RemoveAll() + ChartRedraw, so every object that could carry a refusal is already gone. No guard, no alternative surface: a broker-servable but session-external date is accepted, closes the dialog, and produces nothing visible / Verified end to end. SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:135 validates only against the catalogue (SSR_SessionRange.mqh:76-90 measures cat.EarliestStart/cat.LastMsc), and CanStart (:139-143) therefore enables START for any broker-servable instant. The sole caller is RunHostCommand(SSR_CMD_JUMP) (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3095-3107) and the confirm handler (:3181-3192) acts only when r.start_msc is inside [g_group.StartMsc(), g_group.EndMsc()); otherwise it Prints to the Experts log. Close() at :316 has already removed every dialog object, so no surface remains for feedback. Reachability is high rather than incidental: the dialog itself prints the BROKER's full range on the 'avail' label (:175-180) as the guide the user types against, so an out-of-window date is the natural thing to enter, and the title 'NEW SESSION' plus the button 'START' promise a reload the host cannot perform. Observable result is a primary command (J) that silently does nothing. No money arithmetic, no future-data exposure, no weakening of the virtual-trading guarantee, so MEDIUM is the ceiling - it is a silent no-op on a reachable path, not corruption

The omission is provable; the severity is bounded by the fact that the product guards it and the smoke test asserts it, so a user is not shipped a broken engine by this alone - the preflight just fails to fail early / Verified in full: section 4 sets only SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE (line 312) - there is no CustomSymbolSetInteger(SYMBOL_CHART_MODE, ...) anywhere in SSR_QA_Preflight.mq5 - and after `int nadd = CustomTicksAdd(test, add);` the only test is `nadd == ArraySize(add)`; no CopyRates, Bars() or SeriesInfoInteger call follows the tick add before the cleanup block. The ticks carry flags TICK_FLAG_BID|TICK_FLAG_ASK only. The semantics that make acceptance meaningless are established (CustomTicksAdd accepts ticks that build no bar; bars need CHART_MODE_BID for BID/ASK ticks) and the project has its own recorded measurement of exactly that case plus the assertion the preflight is missing (SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:452-481, CSSRCustomSymbolManager.mqh sets and reads back CHART_MODE). The missing assertion is a source-provable defect in the gating QA script / The coverage gap is provable: :397-403 inspects only the CustomTicksAdd return count, and there is no CopyRates/Bars read after it anywhere in section 4, nor any SYMBOL_CHART_MODE assertion on the test symbol. But the impact claim is wrong. The scenario described - replay advances its clock, emits ticks and produces no candle - is not what a GO from this script licenses, because the product does not inherit the origin's chart mode: CSSRCustomSymbolManager (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:383) forces SYMBOL_CHART_MODE_BID on the replay symbol and reads it back at :387-395, printing an explicit named diagnostic if the terminal refused, and SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:473-481 asserts it on the live replay symbol before every downstream tick check. The preflight's blind spot therefore costs a user a later, noisier diagnosis - not a silent no-candle replay. A short count runs Done() and returns (400-405), so the priming read at 409 `CopyRates(origin, PERIOD_M1, 0, InpReplayBars, back)` is unreachable. The lazy-series semantics are established ground truth and the repo's own A21 rule (tools/ssr_audit.py:1553-1580) exempts PERIOD_M1 only on the grounds that 'M1 is what this program WRITES' - which is true of the replay symbol and false for `origin`, a symbol this harness only reads. #### `spikes-audits-4` — A3 has no positive control: on M5..D1 an unbuilt series gives the same answer as 'no future data'

**`MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Spike/SSR_A3_FutureIsolation.mq5:48`** · category: future-data-leakage

```mql5
checks++;
```

**Why:** Path 2 is iTime(sym,tf,0) > T, path 3 is Bars(sym,tf,T+1,far) > 0, path 4 is (datetime)lastbar > T - each of which is false when the value is 0. The lazy-series behaviour that makes 0 ambiguous is the documented reason audit A21 exists (tools/ssr_audit.py:1556-1583) and is handled explicitly by A2 (SSR_A2_RatesAndAggregation.mq5:208-209, 'an unasked-for series answers zero, and this metric is the whole point of the experiment') and by D1 (SSR_D1_SeedPerformance.mq5:117-120, 'TOUCH EACH SERIES BEFORE COUNTING IT'). **Verifiers:** Traced AuditCut (lines 35-93) and OnStart (96-169) in full. All four paths only ever increment leaks on a positive finding: got>0, it>T, nb>0, (datetime)lastbar>T. Every one of those is false when the underlying value is 0, and nothing in the file asserts that bars BELOW T exist on any timeframe - there is no Bars()/CopyRates check against the seeded range, and the only wait is SSR_WaitSeries on PERIOD_M1 at line 141. The rest of the suite treats this ambiguity as load-bearing and handles it explicitly (A2:204-209 'an unasked-for series answers zero, and this metric is the whole point of the experiment'; D1:113-120 'TOUCH EACH SERIES BEFORE COUNTING IT'), which makes A3's omission a genuine gap in the suite's strongest verdict rather than a difference of style / AuditCut (lines 35-93) is fully read: all four paths only ever call SSR_Verdict inside an `if(<found something past T>)` branch, and nothing in the file asserts that bars BELOW T exist on any timeframe - the only priming is SSR_WaitSeries(InpTest, PERIOD_M1, 10000) at line 141, M1 only. `got > 0`, `it > T`, `nb > 0` and `(datetime)lastbar > T` are all false when the value is 0, and an all-zero answer increments checks (2800 of them) while leaving total_leaks at 0, which line 163 publishes as zero_future_leaks PASS. With the lazy-series behaviour established, the absence of a positive control means a clean PASS is indistinguishable from a terminal that built no series - and the author already handles this explicitly in A2 (:203-209) and D1 (:112-120). The missing control is structural and provable; only the magnitude is runtime, so MEDIUM rather than the claimed HIGH for a developer spike / The missing positive control is provable: AuditCut (:35-93) records a verdict only on the leak branches, every path is false when the value is 0 (got>0, it>T, nb>0, lastbar>T), and OnStart primes only PERIOD_M1 (:141) - M5..D1 are never touched with a below-T read. The project applies the opposite discipline everywhere else (A2:205-209, D1:113-120, and T3:376-382 which asserts M1/M5/H1 bars > 0 immediately before its own 'no future data in any timeframe' check). Two things cap the impact. First, the product-level guarantee is tested with a positive control: SSR_T3_CustomSymbol.mq5:386-396 is the one that runs against the real engine, and it checks presence before absence. A3 is a Phase-0 spike. Second, the vacuity is not as total as claimed: paths 1-3 themselves request each timeframe, so from the first cut onward the higher series are instantiated as a side effect and iTime/Bars begin returning real values - a terminal that answers 0 on all seven for all 100 cuts is possible but not the default case. #### `spikes-audits-2` — B1's wick_expanded_to_extremes verdict fails deterministically no matter how MetaTrader behaves

#### `spikes-audits-23` — D3's throughput_stable gate still uses the minute-10 baseline that the same file documents as hiding the finding

**`MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Spike/SSR_D3_SustainedRun.mq5:216`** · category: measurement-validity


**What goes wrong:** rate_drop is computed from rate_first, which is only assigned once minute >= 10 (line 125-129). On the run the file describes - 12,000 ticks/s falling to about 780 before minute 10 - rate_first is already ~780 and rate_last is ~780, so rate_drop is near zero and throughput_stable PASSES on a run that lost 94% of its throughput. The remedy applied was to add rate_peak, rate_at_min1, decay_peak_to_end and decay_min1_to_end as metrics; the gate that produces the PASS/FAIL line and the verdicts.csv row was left on the window the comment says hides the problem.

The only other guard is have_baseline (203-211), which handles runs shorter than 10 minutes, not the windowing problem. Nothing clamps or corrects rate_drop before line 216 / Confirmed at SSR_D3_SustainedRun.mq5. rate_first is assigned only inside `if(minute >= 10.0 && mem_first < 0)` (lines 125-129); rate_drop at line 160 is 100*(rate_first-rate_last)/rate_first; the else-branch verdict at 216-217 consumes exactly that. The file's own comment at 176-182 states that this window hides the decay ('fell from ~12,000 to ~780 ticks/s before minute 10, then reported a comfortable PASS'). rate_peak/rate_at_min1/decay_peak_to_end/decay_min1_to_end (183-194) are SSR_Metric calls only — I grepped the file, no SSR_Verdict reads any of them. This one keeps MEDIUM under the impact lens because, unlike the other measurement-validity findings in this batch, the false PASS conceals a product behaviour the user does observe: a sustained replay decaying ~94% in throughput, which is a visibly stalling replay after an hour or two

#### `spikes-audits-8` — D4's 1-bar tail-delete timing skips the series rebuild on 16 of 20 trials, inflating the rewind ratio

**`MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Spike/SSR_D4_RewindCost.mq5:97`** · category: timer

```mql5
datetime cut = m1[InpDepth - 1 - i].time;
ulong t = SSR_Now();
CustomRatesDelete(InpTest, cut, D'2038.01.01 00:00');
CustomTicksDelete(InpTest, (long)cut * 1000, LONG_MAX);
SSR_WaitLastBarBefore(InpTest, PERIOD_M5, cut, 15000);
double e = SSR_ElapsedMs(t);
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: D4's strategy-1 propagation wait (SSR_WaitLastBarBefore on PERIOD_M5) is vacuous on 16 of 20 trials because the M5 bar enclosing the cut minute already opens before the cut whenever the minute index is not a multiple of 5; tail_1bar.avg therefore times only the synchronous CustomRatesDelete/CustomTicksDelete calls and omits the series-rebuild cost on those trials, while the full_rebuild side (strategy 3) waits on exact M1 equality - inflating rebuild_over_tail_ratio and letting step_back_interactive pass on an incomplete measurement. Severity is capped at MEDIUM because this is spike/measurement code, not product runtime, and the delete calls' own cost is still real.

**Why:** D'2023.01.02 00:00' is 1672617600, divisible by 300, and m1[k].time = start + k*60, so the M5 slot of cut is start + (k/5)*300 which is < cut unless k % 5 == 0. For i = 0..19 the cut indices are 99999..99980, of which only 99995, 99990, 99985 and 99980 are multiples of 5 - replaying the comparison gives 16 of 20 waits satisfied before the delete. Strategy 2 (cut 100 bars below the last bar) is unaffected. The spike's own comment at lines 64-70 says every timing here used to include SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED and that the published '317x cheaper' 'was mostly a measurement of a flag' - the data-based wait it was replaced with is vacuous here for a different reason.

**Verifiers:** Traced completely. SSR_GenM1 sets out[i].time = start + i*60 (SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:491) and InpStart = D'2023.01.02 00:00' = 1672617600, which is exactly divisible by 300, so the M5 grid is aligned to the seed. SSR_WaitLastBarBefore (SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:433-445) returns on the first CopyRates whose r[0].time < cut. For cut = m1[k].time with k not a multiple of 5, the enclosing M5 bar's open is start + (k/5)*300 < start + k*60 = cut BOTH before and after the delete, so the predicate is already satisfied on entry and the loop exits without observing any propagation. For k in 99999..99980 only 99995/99990/99985/99980 are multiples of 5, so 16 of 20 trials are vacuous exactly as claimed. sum1/InpTrials then feeds step_back_interactive (line 149), step_back_usable (line 152) and rebuild_over_tail_ratio (line 146), while strategy 3 uses SSR_WaitLastBar on PERIOD_M1 with exact equality (line 138) and strategy 2's cut indices (99899, 99799, ...) are never multiples of 5 so its pre-delete M5 last bar (start+19999*300) is not below cut and it does wait. No clamp, guard or earlier check prevents this. Downgraded from HIGH only because this is spike measurement scaffolding, not shipped engine code / The MQL5 semantics check out. SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:433-445 returns the moment CopyRates(sym,tf,0,1,r)>0 && r[0].time < cut. SSR_GenM1 (SpikeKit:492) sets time = start + i*60, and InpStart D'2023.01.02 00:00' = 1672617600 is divisible by 300, so with minute-grid alignment (24/7 sessions are set by SSR_Set247Sessions) the M5 bar enclosing m1[k] opens at start + (k/5)*300. That is strictly less than cut = start + k*60 for every k not a multiple of 5 - i.e. the predicate is ALREADY true before CustomRatesDelete has propagated anything, and it is equally true after propagation, so the instrument cannot distinguish the two states. For i=0..19 the cut indices are 99999..99980 and only 99995/99990/99985/99980 are multiples of 5, so 16 of 20 trials skip the propagation wait entirely. Strategy 2 is genuinely unaffected: its cut sits 100 bars below the current last bar, so the pre-delete M5 open (start+19999*300) is well above cut and the wait blocks. This is the same class of measurement-validity defect the file's own comment at lines 64-70 says it was fixing / Arithmetic verified independently. InpStart D'2023.01.02 00:00' = 1672617600, exactly divisible by 300, and SSR_GenM1 writes out[i].time = start + i*60 (SpikeKit:491). The M5 slot containing m1[k] opens at start + (k/5)*300, which is strictly below start + k*60 for every k not a multiple of 5. SSR_WaitLastBarBefore (SpikeKit:433-445) returns the moment CopyRates yields r[0].time < cut, so for cut indices 99999..99980 only 99995/99990/99985/99980 force a real wait - 4 of 20. With InpOpenChart=true the M5 series is already built (chart opened at line 82 + Sleep(2000)), so the first CopyRates in the loop succeeds immediately and the wait is satisfied before CustomRatesDelete has propagated to the M5 series on 16 trials. avg1 therefore gates step_back_interactive (<=500ms) and step_back_usable (<=3000ms) on what is largely call-return time, and inflates rebuild_over_tail_ratio whose numerator (strategy 3) waits properly via SSR_WaitLastBar on M1 with exact equality (line 138). Severity downgraded from HIGH: this is a Tier-D measurement harness, not product code; nothing here touches money arithmetic, future-data leakage or the virtual-trading guarantee. The reachable harm is one-step-removed - a UI design decision ('Previous Candle' as an interactive button) taken on a number biased in the optimistic direction, which the operator would later discover as a stall. The spike has also never been executed, so no wrong number has yet been published

#### `spikes-audits-9` — D4 loses its chart at the strategy-2 restore, so the three rewind strategies are not measured under the same conditions

**`MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Spike/SSR_D4_RewindCost.mq5:106`** · category: object-lifecycle

```mql5
//--- restore, then strategy 2: delete a 100-bar tail
SSR_DropSymbol(InpTest);
SSR_MakeSymbol(InpTest, g_origin);
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Accurate as to mechanism, but the resulting bias is conservative: the with-chart/without-chart asymmetry lowers rebuild_over_tail_ratio and raises avg1, so it makes the spike's gates harder to pass rather than easier. The substantive defect is the header instructing an indicator-attach step the script structurally prevents, plus the stale cid.

**Why:** SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:213-224 walks ChartFirst/ChartNext and calls ChartClose(cid) for every chart whose ChartSymbol() matches, inside SSR_DropSymbol. Strategy 3 calls SSR_DropSymbol again at line 134 on every trial. The header (lines 9-14) states the spike 'Compares three strategies at a realistic seed depth, with and without indicators on the chart, because indicator recalc is the cost that is easy to forget' and instructs 'Attach MA, RSI and Bollinger to the test chart before running the indicators pass' - but the chart is created by the script at line 82 and there is no input, pause or second pass that would let that happen; ChartIndicatorsTotal(cid,0) at line 85 is read two seconds after ChartOpen.

**Verifiers:** SSR_DropSymbol (SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:209-224) walks ChartFirst/ChartNext and ChartClose()s every chart whose ChartSymbol() equals the symbol, and SSR_MakeSymbol (SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:303-305) itself begins with SSR_DropSymbol and never opens a chart. So the ChartOpen at D4 line 82 is the only chart creation in the script, it is destroyed at line 106, and strategies 2 (line 114) and 3 (line 131) run with no chart while strategy 1 ran with one - the two halves of rebuild_over_tail_ratio are therefore measured under different conditions. cid is left holding a closed chart id that line 158 still passes to ChartClose (harmless no-op, but stale as described). The header's 'with and without indicators' pass is also unreachable: there is no second pass and no input controlling indicators, and the chart whose indicators the operator is told to attach is created by the script itself two seconds before ChartIndicatorsTotal reads it (lines 82-85) / Provable from source. SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:209-224 (SSR_DropSymbol) walks ChartFirst/ChartNext and ChartCloses every chart whose ChartSymbol() equals the symbol, and SSR_MakeSymbol:305 calls SSR_DropSymbol first as well. So D4:106-107 destroys the PERIOD_M5 chart created at D4:82, and nothing reopens it: strategy 1 (lines 91-101) runs with a chart attached, strategies 2 (114-124) and 3 (131-140) run with none, yet avg1 and avg3 are divided into one published rebuild_over_tail_ratio (line 146) and three verdicts. cid is never zeroed, so the ChartClose(cid) at line 158 acts on a destroyed chart id (harmless, but a no-op). The header's 'with and without indicators' pass is also unreachable as written: the chart is created by the script and ChartIndicatorsTotal(cid,0) is read 2s later (lines 82-86), leaving no point at which an operator can attach MA/RSI/Bollinger to it / Mechanism verified: SSR_DropSymbol (SpikeKit:209-224) walks ChartFirst/ChartNext and ChartCloses every chart whose ChartSymbol() matches, and SSR_MakeSymbol (SpikeKit:303-305) calls SSR_DropSymbol as its first act. So line 106 destroys the M5 chart opened at line 82, line 107 cannot bring it back, and nothing reopens it - strategy 1 runs with a chart, strategies 2 and 3 without. cid is stale from line 106 onward and ChartClose(cid) at line 158 is a no-op. The header's 'Attach MA, RSI and Bollinger to the test chart before running the indicators pass' is unperformable: the chart is created by the script itself, and any pre-existing chart on InpTest is closed by the SSR_MakeSymbol at line 50. Severity downgraded from MEDIUM to LOW on impact: unlike finding 8 the bias here runs in the safe direction - a chart makes the strategy-1 tail delete slower and its absence makes the strategy-3 rebuild faster, so both effects push rebuild_over_tail_ratio and the step_back gates toward pessimism, not toward wrongly approving an interactive button. The stale ChartClose is harmless, and the only real casualty is a documentation promise the script cannot keep

#### `tests-b-1` — T15.7 asserts R still means RESET; the key table maps R to LINES_TOGGLE, so the assertion is false at runtime

**`MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Tests/SSR_T15_Ux.mq5:402`** · category: tick-ordering

```mql5
      Check("and the other keys still mean what they did",
            SSRKeyToCommand(SSR_VK_SPACE) == SSR_CMD_TOGGLE &&
            SSRKeyToCommand(SSR_VK_J)     == SSR_CMD_JUMP &&
            SSRKeyToCommand(SSR_VK_B)     == SSR_CMD_BOOKMARK &&
            SSRKeyToCommand(SSR_VK_R)     == SSR_CMD_RESET);
```

**What goes wrong:** Run T15 on a terminal: SSRKeyToCommand(SSR_VK_R) returns SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE, not SSR_CMD_RESET, so the conjunction is false and Check records a FAIL. Phase 15 can never print GREEN, and because the harness never aborts, this looks like a product regression rather than a stale assertion.

**Why:** SSR_Keys.mqh binds R with `SSRAddKey(out, i, SSR_VK_R, "R", SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE, "stop and target lines on / off", true);` and binds reset to '0' with `SSRAddKey(out, i, SSR_VK_0, "0", SSR_CMD_RESET, ...)`, under a comment headed "RESET MOVED OFF R, and off every letter". SSRKeyToCommand is a linear scan of that one table and returns the first vk match, so R can only yield SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE. The test was not updated when reset moved; SSRKeyHint()'s trailing literal "R reset" (same file) shows the same stale belief, which is why the mistake reads as plausible.

**Verifiers:** Provable from the two files. SSRKeyBindings binds R at SSR_Keys.mqh:162-164 as SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE and reset at l.200-202 as SSR_VK_0 -> SSR_CMD_RESET, under the comment 'RESET MOVED OFF R, and off every letter' (l.192-199). SSRKeyToCommand (l.224-232) is a first-match linear scan over that one table and R (82) appears exactly once, so it can only return SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE. SSR_T15_Ux.mq5:398-402 ANDs `SSRKeyToCommand(SSR_VK_R) == SSR_CMD_RESET` into its conjunction, so the whole Check is false, g_fail becomes non-zero, and the tail print at l.508-510 makes Phase 15 report RED unconditionally. I checked for any shadowing or alternate table and there is none. Severity downgraded from the finder's HIGH: the product behaviour is correct and only the test is stale, but the phase can never go green, so the suite stops functioning as a regression gate / Settled entirely from source. SSRKeyBindings() adds R exactly once, as SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE (SSR_Keys.mqh:162-164), and RESET is on '0' (:200-202) under the banner 'RESET MOVED OFF R, and off every letter' (:192-199). SSRKeyToCommand is a first-match linear scan over that single table (:224-232), so SSRKeyToCommand(SSR_VK_R) is SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE and the conjunction at SSR_T15_Ux.mq5:398-402 evaluates false. MQL5 compiles the enum comparison fine, so this is a guaranteed runtime FAIL, not a compile error: Phase 15 can never print GREEN. Severity lowered from HIGH because nothing in the product misbehaves - it is a stale assertion producing a permanent false alarm (and the suite has at least one other, tests-b-2, in the same file) / Provable and deterministic: SSR_Keys.mqh:162-164 binds SSR_VK_R to SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE, reset is on SSR_VK_0 (l.200-202), and SSRKeyToCommand is a first-match linear scan (l.224-232) with no other R row, so the T15.7 conjunction is false on every run and Phase 15 can only print RED. The suite's own QA smoke asserts the opposite pair (SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:3205 and 3211-3212: R == LINES_TOGGLE and R != RESET), which settles that the test assertion is the stale side. Downgraded from HIGH: this is test-only, changes no product behaviour, leaks no data and touches no money path; its cost is a permanently red phase whose Check() call passes no detail string, so the log says only 'FAIL and the other keys still mean what they did'

#### `tests-b-2` — T15.9's premise is false: SetCorner does not move the panel, so both of its assertions fail

**`MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Tests/SSR_T15_Ux.mq5:460`** · category: redraw

```mql5
      panel2.SetCorner(0);                       // top-left
      long x_before = ObjectGetInteger(ChartID(), "T15_move_stbal",
                                       OBJPROP_XDISTANCE);

                                      OBJPROP_XDISTANCE);
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Accurate. Worth adding that the section's stated purpose is lost either way - because SetCorner cannot move the panel, the position-keyed text-cache regression it was written to guard is no longer exercised by any assertion; a real test would have to call the palette's 'move' action (SnapToCorner) instead of SetCorner.

**Why:** CSSRPanel::SetCorner is `{ m_corner = (c & 3); SavePlace(); Render(); }` (SSR_Panel.mqh:384-385) and m_corner appears nowhere in Render or in any layout computation - its only uses are the constructor, a PrintFormat, SavePlace/RestorePlace and SnapToCorner (grep for m_corner in SSR_Panel.mqh returns lines 121, 287, 350, 385, 386, 543, 579, 598, 606 only). Only SnapToCorner (line 596, reachable from the Move button that v125 removed) recomputes m_x/m_y from the corner. Every object is drawn through CSSRWidgets, whose Common() hard-writes `ObjectSetInteger(m_chart, name, OBJPROP_CORNER, CORNER_LEFT_UPPER)` (SSR_Widgets.mqh:160), so XDISTANCE is always measured from the same chart corner. Two Renders with identical m_x therefore write identical XDISTANCE. (If the object did not exist, ObjectGetInteger would return 0 twice and the first assertion would fail for that reason instead.)

**Verifiers:** Traced the whole path. CSSRPanel::SetCorner is `{ m_corner = (c & 3); SavePlace(); Render(); }` (SSR_Panel.mqh:384-385). I grepped m_corner across SSR_Panel.mqh: lines 121, 287, 350, 385, 386, 543, 579, 598, 606 only - constructor, PrintFormat, SavePlace/RestorePlace, and SnapToCorner. ClampToChart (l.445-481), the only geometry that runs inside Render (called at l.717), never reads m_corner; Render then uses `int x = m_x, y = m_y;` (l.718). 'stbal' is always drawn at `x + SSR_PAD` (l.1929/1947/1988/2001/2015) and CSSRWidgets::Common hard-writes OBJPROP_CORNER = CORNER_LEFT_UPPER (SSR_Widgets.mqh:160), so XDISTANCE is measured from the same chart corner both times. Two SetCorner calls with unchanged m_x therefore write identical XDISTANCE, so both Checks at SSR_T15_Ux.mq5:468-473 fail; if the object were absent, ObjectGetInteger returns 0 twice and the first still fails. Severity MEDIUM rather than HIGH: like tests-b-1 this is a permanently-failing stale test, not a product fault / Verified end to end in source. SetCorner is m_corner = (c&3); SavePlace(); Render(); (SSR_Panel.mqh:384-385). Render takes int x = m_x after ClampToChart (:717-718), and ClampToChart (:445-478) reads only CHART_WIDTH/HEIGHT_IN_PIXELS - m_corner appears nowhere in it. The only place m_corner recomputes m_x is SnapToCorner (:596-618), reachable from the removed [] button and now only from the palette's 'move' action (:2605). 'stbal' is written at x + SSR_PAD on every branch of DrawStatus (:1929, 1947, 1988, 2001, 2015), and SavePlace only writes a file that Render never re-reads, so two SetCorner calls produce identical OBJPROP_XDISTANCE. Both Check calls at SSR_T15_Ux.mq5:468-473 therefore fail. The one alternative path leads to the same place: if m_collapsed was restored true, Render returns before DrawStatus (:702-708) and ObjectGetInteger on a non-existent object returns 0 twice, failing the first assertion anyway. Severity lowered from HIGH: the panel behaves as designed, the test is wrong / Verified independently: SetCorner is `{ m_corner = (c & 3); SavePlace(); Render(); }` (SSR_Panel.mqh:384-385); grep for m_corner in that file returns only 121, 287, 350, 385, 386, 543, 579, 598, 606 - nothing in Render, nothing in ClampToChart (445-481, which reads only chart pixels and m_x/m_y), and the only corner-to-coordinate code is SnapToCorner (596-613), called solely from the palette's 'move' action (2607). Widgets hard-write CORNER_LEFT_UPPER (SSR_Widgets.mqh:160) and stbal is always drawn at x + SSR_PAD in every DrawStatus branch (1929/1947/1988/2001/2015), so two Renders with identical m_x write identical XDISTANCE and both Checks at l.469-474 fail deterministically. Downgraded from HIGH for the same reason as tests-b-1: test-only, no product misbehaviour - but it does mean the text-cache-position regression this section exists to guard is not guarded at all

#### `tests-a-1` — T5.6's click assertion cannot pass: the panel does not handle CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_CLICK at all

**`MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Tests/SSR_T5_Ui.mq5:208`** · category: event-handling

CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_CLICK appears nowhere except the comment at 2878-2882 stating PollClicks is the one mechanism. I checked the two ways this could have been wrong and neither holds - Render() does not call PollClicks (it only reads state and writes widgets), and CFakePort::Play is reached from nowhere else in that block. So the call at T5:208 is a no-op, port.play stays 0, and the assertion fails on every run.
