#### `spikes-audits-21` — C2's restart detector false-fails on every run after the first, and the event it hunts destroys its own evidence file

**`MQL5/Services/SSReplay/Spike/SSR_C2_ServicePersistence.mq5:58`** · category: session-resume

```mql5
double prev_marker = GlobalVariableGet("SSR.c2.launches");
GlobalVariableSet("SSR.c2.launches", prev_marker + 1);
...
SSR_Verdict("no_restart", GlobalVariableGet("SSR.c2.launches") <= 1.0, "1",
            DoubleToString(GlobalVariableGet("SSR.c2.launches"), 0),
            "more than 1 means the service was restarted");
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Accurate, with one nuance: a truncated CSV starting again at seq=1 with a low uptime is itself circumstantial evidence that a relaunch happened; what is irrecoverably lost is the pre-restart row history (and the pre-restart gap statistics), which is what the PASS criterion needs to demonstrate the counter reset.

**Why:** No GlobalVariableDel("SSR.c2.launches") appears anywhere in the file, and line 127 prints 'reset the launch counter before the next run: delete GV SSR.c2.launches'. Line 63 opens SSR_Spike\c2_heartbeat.csv with FILE_WRITE|FILE_TXT|FILE_ANSI (no FILE_READ, no seek to end), so OnStart running a second time rewrites the header at offset 0. seq is a local initialised to 0 at line 51, so the only cross-restart evidence is the GV that is already unreliable. Header line 21: 'PASS: heartbeat counter never resets and no gap exceeds 3000ms.'

**Verifiers:** Both halves verified. (a) Line 58 reads GlobalVariableGet("SSR.c2.launches") (0 when absent), line 59 writes prev+1, and line 115 fails the no_restart verdict whenever that value exceeds 1. A repo-wide grep shows no GlobalVariableDel for this name anywhere - sibling spikes C1 (SSR_C1_ServiceApiAccess.mq5:157) and C3 (SSR_C3_IpcChannel.mq5:127-132) do delete their own GVs, so the omission is an oversight, and line 127 pushes the reset onto the operator. MT5 global variables are persisted by the terminal, so run 2 onward reports launch_count 2+ and FAILs no_restart with no restart having occurred: the verdict measures 'has this spike run before'. (b) Line 63 opens SSR_Spike\c2_heartbeat.csv with FILE_WRITE|FILE_TXT|FILE_ANSI - no FILE_READ and no seek - so a second OnStart truncates and rewrites the header at offset 0, erasing the pre-restart rows that are the only durable evidence for the header's PASS criterion (line 21, 'heartbeat counter never resets'); seq is a local initialised to 0 (line 51) and GV SSR.c2.seq is overwritten every beat (line 94) / Both MQL5 semantics used by the finding are correct. (1) GlobalVariableGet on a missing name returns 0.0, and MT5 global variables are persisted by the terminal between runs and survive terminal restarts; C2 never deletes SSR.c2.launches (no GlobalVariableDel anywhere in the file) and line 127 asks the operator to delete it by hand AFTER the run, so run 2 starts from prev_marker=1, sets 2, and the no_restart verdict at line 115 (<= 1.0) fails although nothing restarted - the verdict measures 'has this spike been run before'. (2) FileOpen(..., FILE_WRITE|FILE_TXT|FILE_ANSI) without FILE_READ truncates the file to zero length, and there is no FileSeek(FILE_END), so a genuine mid-run relaunch rewrites c2_heartbeat.csv from offset 0 (line 63-65). Since a relaunched OnStart never reached SSR_Metric/SSR_Verdict on its first pass, the CSV was the only record of the pre-restart rows, and seq is a local reinitialised to 0 at line 51 - so the evidence for the header's PASS criterion ('heartbeat counter never resets', line 21) is the one thing the restart destroys / Both mechanisms check out. GlobalVariableGet returns 0 for a missing GV, so run 1 stores 1 and passes no_restart, run 2 stores 2 and fails it, with no GlobalVariableDel anywhere in the file. FileOpen at line 63 uses FILE_WRITE|FILE_TXT|FILE_ANSI with no FILE_READ and no seek, so a relaunch truncates c2_heartbeat.csv and rewrites the header at offset 0, destroying the pre-restart rows that would evidence the seq reset the header names as the PASS criterion. But the first half is substantially over-stated: the persistence is the detection mechanism, not an oversight - auto-resetting the GV in OnStart would make an accidental relaunch indistinguishable from a first launch and defeat the check entirely - and line 127 prints the reset as an explicit operator step in a spike whose header already prescribes eight manual steps. Severity downgraded from MEDIUM to LOW: this is a dev-facing spike, the false FAIL is self-diagnosing (results.csv carries launch_count with the note 'must stay 1 for the whole procedure', and the printed remedy names the GV), and nothing here touches money, future data or the virtual-trading guarantee

### LOW (105)

#### `host-expert-11` — EnsureHistory's 60-second budget is computed with a ulong subtraction of a 32-bit tick count and breaks at the GetTickCount wrap

**`MQL5/Experts/SSReplay/SSReplayStandalone.mq5:651`** · category: boundary

```mql5
   ulong t0 = GetTickCount();
   int   stalls = 0;
   while(have < want_bars && (GetTickCount() - t0) < 60000 && !IsStopped())
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: The mechanism is real but the claim's probability framing is wrong. The wrap must fall inside the loop's own lifetime, not merely on a terminal that has been up for weeks - roughly a 60 s window in each 49.7 days, i.e. ~1e-5 per download - and the realistic effect is an early exit part-way through a download (EnsureHistory falls out of the loop and prints its normal tail line), not a systematic no-op that never enters the body.

**Why:** The same pattern is written correctly elsewhere in this file with uint arithmetic - line 2894 `uint now_ms = GetTickCount(); if(!modal && now_ms - g_panel_paint >= 100)` and line 3145 `(GetTickCount() - g_ready_at_ms) > 1500` where g_ready_at_ms is uint (declared 345). Only t0 at 651 is widened to ulong. GetTickCount64() is the wrap-free primitive. Failure needs a 49.7-day-uptime coincidence, hence LOW, but the outcome is a silent no-op on the one code path whose whole job is fetching history.

**Verifiers:** The arithmetic defect is provable. t0 is declared ulong at 651 while GetTickCount() returns uint, so at 653 the fresh uint is widened rather than wrapped and `GetTickCount() - t0` after a wrap underflows in 64-bit to a value near 2^64, which is >= 60000 and ends the loop. The same pattern is wrap-safe elsewhere in the file because both operands are uint (2894 with `uint now_ms`, 3145 with g_ready_at_ms declared uint at 345). GetTickCount64() is the wrap-free primitive and is not used here / The type error is real and provable. GetTickCount() returns uint and wraps every 2^32 ms (~49.7 days of terminal uptime); t0 is declared ulong at 651, so in `(GetTickCount() - t0) < 60000` at 653 the fresh uint is zero-extended to ulong before the subtraction instead of wrapping modulo 2^32. The file writes the same idiom correctly everywhere else with uint operands - `uint now_ms = GetTickCount(); ... now_ms - g_panel_paint >= 100` at 3062-3063 and `(GetTickCount() - g_ready_at_ms) > 1500` at 3146 with g_ready_at_ms declared uint at 350 - so 651 is the lone outlier, and GetTickCount64() is the wrap-free primitive. Consequence as described: if the wrap falls between t0 and a loop test the budget evaluates as exhausted, the download is abandoned, and BuildSession's SHORT ON HISTORY cascade at 1109-1123 then blames the broker. Severity stays LOW - the vulnerable window is roughly the 60 s preceding a wrap that occurs once per 49.7 days of uptime / The arithmetic defect is real: `ulong t0 = GetTickCount()` widens a uint, so after the 49.7-day wrap `GetTickCount() - t0` is evaluated in ulong and yields ~2^32 rather than a small elapsed time, and the file itself writes the same pattern correctly with uint at 2894 and 3145. Downgraded from LOW on the impact lens because the reachable window is vanishingly small: a terminal already past the wrap simply gets a mid-range t0 and behaves normally, so the bug fires only when the wrap lands between t0 and a later loop test - roughly a 60-second window per 49.7 days of uptime, about 1 in 7x10^4 attaches. The consequence is also bounded: EnsureHistory returns the Bars() it already had, and the SHORT ON HISTORY block at 1128-1145 then prints the true situation including 'the broker HAS more - back to <date>' and the Home-key remedy, so the user is not misled about what to do. GetTickCount64() is the correct primitive; worth fixing, not worth ranking above the reachable defects in this batch

#### `host-expert-9` — The one-shot spread diagnostic is consumed by the start-picker phase and then permanently suppressed for the real session

The build happens in the same program instance, so the latch is already spent when the real session starts / Verified by grep: g_spread_reported occurs exactly twice in the file - declared at 2232, set true at 2263 - with no reset anywhere, while BuildSession resets g_timer_ticks at 1577. ReportSpreadOnce() is the second statement of OnTimer (2458), before the g_picking block at 2470, and g_timer_ticks is incremented unconditionally at 2454. The picker arms a 200 ms timer at 2072, so g_timer_ticks reaches 500 after 100 s of picking with the controller unloaded (SpreadBarsRecorded/Fixed forward to the synthesizer's zeroed counters, Core/SSR_ReplayController.mqh:657-658), total==0, the latch is set and the session's one spread diagnostic is spent on a message about a replay that has not started. Which of the two total==0 branches prints depends on the unloaded controller's EffectiveFidelity(), but the latch is set either way, so the outcome does not turn on that / Confirmed: ReportSpreadOnce() is OnTimer's second statement (2456), ahead of the g_picking block at 2465; the picker runs the timer at 200 ms (2072); the latch condition at 2260 releases once g_timer_ticks reaches 500, i.e. 100 s of picking, with the controller unloaded so recorded+fixed==0; g_spread_reported is assigned at 2263 and, per grep, is never reset anywhere, while BuildSession resets only g_timer_ticks (1577). So a user who takes more than 100 s to choose a start loses that session's spread line and gets the misleading 'no bar has been replayed yet' instead. Impact is confined to one diagnostic log line: nothing the engine does changes, the spread actually used is unaffected, and the same facts are still visible on the panel's fidelity indicator. LOW is right (borderline IMPROVEMENT); the reason it is not dismissed is that this line is the one the file itself designates as the evidence to send when reporting a fault, so losing it costs a support round trip

#### `chart-17` — MarkTime puts the registry index in the object name, so bookmarks duplicate after a chart closes

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Chart/SSR_ChartManager.mqh:176`** · category: object-lifecycle

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: MarkTime derives the object-name suffix from the registry loop index, which Remove() reassigns when a chart closes, so re-marking an already-marked timestamp can create a second OBJ_VLINE on a chart that already carries one. **Verifiers:** The mechanism is provable. With two charts marked at time t and the first closed, the second holds SSR_MARK_t_1 and the ObjectFind guard on line 177 then misses when the same t is re-marked under its new index 0, creating a second OBJ_VLINE. Combined with the absence of any deletion path (chart-6) the duplicates accumulate. The visible outcome is overstated, which is why this stays LOW rather than a user-facing defect / The mechanism is provable: the name suffix is the current loop index (line 176), Remove() renumbers by copying entries down (98-106), and ObjectFind is per-chart, so after a registry shift the same chart is asked for a name it does not yet own and ObjectCreate succeeds, leaving both SSR_MARK_<t>_1 and SSR_MARK_<t>_0 on one chart. The index is indeed not a chart identity. The stated user-visible consequence is overstated, though: two OBJ_VLINEs at the same datetime with identical colour, STYLE_DASH and width are exactly coincident, so the user sees one line, not two - the real cost is silent object accumulation, which only matters because of chart-6 / The mechanism is real (Remove() at 98-106 renumbers, the suffix is rebuilt from the loop index) but the state is both hard to reach and unobservable. Reaching it needs: two or more registered replay charts, one of them closed mid-session, and then the SAME datetime bookmarked again - which means rewinding to the identical second, since base is IntegerToString((int)when). And the product of the duplication is a second OBJ_VLINE with identical time, colour, STYLE_DASH, width and BACK on the same chart: it renders exactly on top of the first, so the user observes nothing at all. No count, no arithmetic and no guarantee is affected; the only cost is an extra hidden object. This is a naming-hygiene nit, not a defect the user can see

The claim overreaches on one point: the Session tab that would carry the indicator already prints the keyboard group, and SSR_S_KEYS_3 is "S sessions   F follow   D fidelity   L lines   X flip" (SSR_Strings.mqh:502-503), so the F binding is on screen; what is missing is any indication that a chart is CURRENTLY detached. Also, in the normal case the detach is user-initiated, so the user knows why the chart stopped following; the gap only bites after a false detach (chart-1), which is itself unproven / The absence is provable: SetObserver has one caller in the whole tree and it is Scripts/SSReplay/Tests/SSR_T4_ChartIntegration.mq5, so m_observer is NULL in production and OnUserScrolled is a no-op; charts_detached is assigned at SSR_GroupPort.mqh:122 and read nowhere; SSR_S_FOLLOW_N ('Follow %d  F') and SSR_S_ACT_FOLLOW_N exist but have zero consumers, and SSR_Panel.mqh:2717 records that the follow button was removed. So no live indicator of detach exists. But the claim 'the interface says nothing at all; the user has to already know that F re-attaches' overstates it: the Session sheet renders SSR_S_KEYS_3 = 'S sessions   F follow   D fidelity   L lines   X flip', so the remedy is printed in the panel, and any pause-play re-attaches via the host's FollowAll. Under the impact lens this is a missing status indicator on a dangling wire - informational only, no arithmetic, no leak, no safety consequence - so MEDIUM drops to LOW

#### `chart-7` — LeakGuard::Advice is written far longer than the 49 characters its only consumer can display, so the actionable half never reaches the user

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Chart/SSR_LeakGuard.mqh:93`** · category: string-length

```mql5
      if(m_report.origin_charts > 0)
         return StringFormat("%s is open on %d chart(s) - close it or your backtest is not blind",
                             m_origin, m_report.origin_charts);
      return StringFormat("%s is in Market Watch - its live price is visible", m_origin);
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Advice() is 69 chars (chart case) and 53 chars (Market-Watch case) against 48 usable characters after the 13-char 'Charts' prefix and Clip's 62-char cap, so both lines are truncated with a trailing '~'. The cut falls after 'close it or your' - the actionable verb survives and the rationale is lost - not before 'close it' as the finding states, so the defect is a cosmetically truncated sentence rather than an unreachable instruction.

**Why:** Plain arithmetic on the format strings plus the 62-character Clip. The panel's own comment (SSR_Panel.mqh:1888-1891) records that this line 'has been ending "- close it or your" on the chart, mid-sentence' and clips it deliberately; clipping stopped the ragged cut, it did not make the sentence fit. The wording lives here, so this is where a 49-character message has to be authored.

**Verifiers:** The truncation is confirmed by arithmetic on the actual code. Clip (SSR_Panel.mqh:242-248) caps at 62 and, when over, returns StringSubstr(s,0,61)+"~". '%-12s ' on 'Charts' (SSR_Strings.mqh:433) is a 13-char prefix, so the advice gets 48 characters plus a tilde. The chart variant is 69 chars (not 68) and renders as 'Charts       EURUSD is open on 1 chart(s) - close it or your ~'; the Market-Watch variant is 53 chars (not 54) and renders as 'Charts       EURUSD is in Market Watch - its live price is vi~'. Both are cut, and the panel's own comment at 1888-1891 records that the clip was added to stop a ragged cut rather than to make the sentence fit, so the wording does need to be authored to fit 48 chars here in SSR_LeakGuard.mqh:93-96. Downgraded to LOW because the impact claim does not survive: in the chart case the actionable instruction 'close it' is fully visible and what is lost is the justification 'or your backtest is not blind'; only the Market-Watch case loses a load-bearing word ('visible'). The class's 'never silent when dirty' contract is met - the line is present and coloured SSR_C_HOLD - it just ends in a tilde / The arithmetic is settleable from source and holds. Advice() returns a 69-character string for the origin-charts case and 53 for the Market-Watch case; the sole consumer composes StringFormat("%-12s %s", T(SSR_S_CHARTS), advice) with T(SSR_S_CHARTS)=="Charts" (SSR_Strings.mqh:433) padded to 12 plus a space, giving 82 and 66 characters, and Clip(...,62) (SSR_Panel.mqh:242-248) caps at 62 by returning StringSubstr(s,0,61)+"~". Both variants are therefore truncated, leaving 48 characters of advice plus the "~" marker, and nothing else renders the leak state (other_live_charts and ToString() are log-only). The finding mis-states the cut point and the impact: the rendered text is "Charts       EURUSD is open on 1 chart(s) - close it or your ~", so the actionable instruction "close it" DOES survive - what is lost is the justification clause "backtest is not blind", and the "~" signals the truncation rather than looking like a broken sentence. Hence LOW, not MEDIUM / I redid the arithmetic and it refutes the claim. Clip (SSR_Panel.mqh:242-248) returns StringSubstr(s,0,61)+"~", and the prefix '%-12s ' with T(SSR_S_CHARTS)='Charts' is 13 chars, so 48 advice characters survive - not 49, but more importantly 'close it' occupies advice chars 36-43, well inside 48. The rendered line is 'Charts       EURUSD is open on 1 chart(s) - close it or your~': the symbol, the count, the dirty colour (SSR_C_HOLD) and the instruction all reach the user; only the justification tail 'backtest is not blind' is elided, with the '~' announcing the elision. The Market-Watch variant is 52 chars and renders '...its live price is vis~', which loses nothing operative either. So the class contract 'never silent when dirty' is met, the actionable half is NOT lost, and what remains is a wording-length nit on one line of the Session sheet - no arithmetic, no leak, no safety consequence

#### `chart-12` — Every word the Chart layer draws or hands to the panel is a hardcoded English literal, outside audit A19's reach

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Chart/SSR_TradeLines.mqh:134`** · category: utf8

```mql5
      ObjectSetString (m_chart, n, OBJPROP_TEXT, tip);
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: The Chart layer's on-chart wording is hardcoded English with no SSR_Strings entries and no T() in scope, so a translated session still shows English on the draggable lines, position levels and history tooltips. A19 misses it for two reasons, not one: the "/Ui/" path filter (tools/ssr_audit.py:1458) and, more fundamentally, that A19 only inspects widget draw calls by argument position (:1449) and never raw ObjectSetString(OBJPROP_TEXT) writes.

**Why:** The literals are in the source at the lines quoted; SSR_Strings.mqh has no entries for them; the audit's directory filter is explicit.

**Verifiers:** The literals are all present as cited: "STOP - drag me"/"TARGET - drag me" (:243-244, :277-278, :298-299), "ENTRY - drag me" (:200, :315), written to OBJPROP_TEXT at :134 with CHART_SHOW_OBJECT_DESCR forced on at :183; "BUY"/"SELL"/"SL"/"TP" and the "stop of %s ..." tooltips (:412-438); "#%d %s %s in at %s" (:546-564); and the English leak advice that reaches the panel (SSR_LeakGuard.mqh:94-96). grep confirms SSR_Strings.mqh has no entries for any of them, and this file includes only Common + Ui/SSR_Theme.mqh, so T() is not even in scope. The audit-mechanism explanation is however inaccurate: A19's literal scan matches widget draw calls (`(m_w.)?(Label|ButtonC|Button|Chip|Group|Toast|Edit|Text)(`, tools/ssr_audit.py:1449) and takes the text by argument position, so a raw ObjectSetString(..., OBJPROP_TEXT, ...) in the Chart layer would be invisible to it even if the "/Ui/" filter at :1458 were removed. No functional failure follows - this is an i18n coverage gap / Every literal and every audit fact checks out. The planning-line captions are English literals passed as `tip` and written to OBJPROP_TEXT at :134 - "STOP - drag me" / "TARGET - drag me" (:200, :243-244, :277-278, :298-299) and "ENTRY - drag me" (:190, :315) - with CHART_SHOW_OBJECT_DESCR forced on in Attach (:183), so they are painted on the chart rather than merely hovered. Position levels are likewise literal: side = "BUY"/"SELL" or the caller's `kind`, the "%s %s at %s" tip and the "SL"/"TP" labels (:411-438), and closed trades print "#%d %s %s in at %s" / "#%d out at %s" (:546-564). grep of SSR_Strings.mqh finds no catalogue entry for any of them, and the leak advice really does reach the panel in English (SSR_LeakGuard.mqh:94-96). The audit blindness is exact: A19's literal pass does `if "/Ui/" not in path.replace("\\", "/"): continue` (tools/ssr_audit.py:1458) before it looks at anything, and its vacuous-pass guard is `if seen[1] < 100` (:1491) counted over the Ui files alone, so it still passes. Two notes that widen rather than narrow the point: A19 also matches only Label/Button/ButtonC/Chip/Group/Toast/Edit/Text call sites, so a direct ObjectSetString(OBJPROP_TEXT) like :134 would be invisible to it even under /Ui/; and these captions are 15-16 characters, comfortably inside MetaTrader's 63-char OBJPROP_TEXT limit, so nothing is truncated. Severity is an i18n completeness gap, not a runtime fault / Verified directly: grep for T(SSR_S over MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Chart/ returns nothing at all, the literals are in the source at the quoted lines ("STOP - drag me" :243, "TARGET - drag me" :244, "ENTRY - drag me" :200/:315, BUY/SELL/SL/TP and the "stop of %s ..." / "#%d %s %s in at %s" tooltips :411-438, :546-564), Attach forces CHART_SHOW_OBJECT_DESCR on (:183) so the descriptions really are painted, SSR_Strings.mqh has no entry for them, and CSSRLeakGuard::Advice returns English prose to the panel (SSR_LeakGuard.mqh:94-96). The audit blind spot is also exactly as stated - tools/ssr_audit.py:1458 skips every path without '/Ui/' (and its call regex only matches m_w.Label/Button/... so raw ObjectSetString(OBJPROP_TEXT) would escape it even without the filter). Impact is a genuine localisation gap for the product's own target audience - the translated panel sits beside English captions on the only objects the user is asked to drag - but it is text-only: no arithmetic, no leaked future data, no trading-safety consequence. LOW confirmed

#### `chart-13` — The flight recorder truncates chart_id to 32 bits, corrupting the column that identifies which chart a fault happened on

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Common/SSR_FlightRecorder.mqh:256`** · category: boundary

```mql5
              s.chart_count, (int)s.chart_id,
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Confirmed for chart_id. The emit_ticks/emit_calls half is far weaker: those would need to exceed 2.1 billion in one recording (over 268 million bars at the default 8 ticks/bar) before wrapping, so in practice chart_id is the only column that truncates.

**Why:** The truncation is in the source; the %d specifier forces a 32-bit argument, so the fix is %I64d or IntegerToString rather than the cast. The claim that real chart ids exceed 32 bits is an inference from MT5's id scheme, not from this tree - but the cast is lossy for any id above 2^31 regardless.

**Verifiers:** The truncation is plainly in the source. SSRFlightSample.chart_id is a long (SSR_FlightRecorder.mqh:58), filled from g_charts.IdAt(0) at Standalone.mq5:2408-2409, and Write formats it as (int)s.chart_id against a %d specifier (SSR_FlightRecorder.mqh:243, 256), so any id above 2^31-1 is written wrapped and often negative into the chart_id column of the diagnostic artefact. The finding is honest that "real chart ids exceed 2^31" is an inference about MT5's id scheme rather than evidence from this tree - but the cast is lossy for such ids regardless, and the fix (%I64d or IntegerToString) needs no runtime knowledge. The same (int) cast is applied to emit_calls/emit_ticks/seed_bars/truncations at 254-255 / The cast is real and lossy: FlightRecorder:256 passes (int)s.chart_id into a %d slot of the sample row, and s.chart_id is filled from g_charts.IdAt(0), a long chart id (Standalone:2407-2409). MQL5's StringFormat %d takes a 32-bit argument, so a long id has to be widened to %I64d or routed through IntegerToString rather than truncated; C-style truncation of a value above 2^31 yields a wrong and frequently negative number in the one column that says which window a fault occurred on, in the artefact the author depends on for remote diagnosis. The one thing I cannot settle from this tree is the magnitude of real MT5 chart ids - that comes from MT5's time-derived id scheme, not from source - but the cast is unconditionally lossy above 2^31 whatever the distribution, and no other code in the tree ever narrows a chart id this way. I do refute the extension of the claim to the instrumentation counters: (int)s.emit_ticks and (int)s.emit_calls would need 2^31 ticks in one recording (at 8 ticks per bar that is ~268M bars), which SSR_FLIGHT_MAX_ROWS-capped sessions cannot plausibly reach, so those casts are not a live defect. Severity LOW: a diagnostic column, not behaviour / The cast is in the source and is lossy: the host fills s.chart_id from g_charts.IdAt(0), a long (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2407-2409), and Write() passes (int)s.chart_id against a %d specifier (SSR_FlightRecorder.mqh:243, 256). But the consequence the finding claims - a recording that "carries a chart id that matches nothing the user or the log can show" - does not survive checking: nothing in this tree ever prints a full chart id for the reader to correlate against (no %I64d chart-id line in the host or the chart manager), MT5 does not show chart ids in its UI either, and the truncation is deterministic, so the column still distinguishes one chart from another within a recording, which is all the diagnostic uses it for. The companion claim about emit_ticks/emit_calls is not reachable: overflowing a 32-bit int needs >2.1e9 emitted ticks in one recording, against a synthesiser default of 8 ticks per M1 bar and a recorder capped at 5000 rows (~40 minutes). Diagnostic-file cosmetics, no user-facing effect - IMPROVEMENT

#### `core-sync-3` — Generic CSSRBarProvider::NextBarOpen reads through the guarded ReadBars: it is useless inside a gap and raises up to four 'future access' violations per call

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Core/SSR_IDataSource.mqh:160`** · category: future-data-leakage

```mql5
      for(int i = 0; i < 4; i++)
        {
         int n = ReadBars(symbol, after_msc + 1, after_msc + spans[i], tmp);
         if(n > 0)
            return SSRToMsc(tmp[0].time);
        }
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Same defect, two corrections. (1) The ClampRange snippet is at SSR_FutureGuard.mqh:90-106 (Violation at 80-84), not 312-316 - that file is only 156 lines. (2) The blast radius is narrower than the claim implies and should be read as test-harness-only: CSSRMt5BarProvider overrides NextBarOpen with a times-only CopyTime walk (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:302+), and grep shows CSSRMemoryDataSource is referenced only by MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Tests/* - no production path uses the generic implementation, so the inflated Violations() count cannot reach real UI vitals today and the 'indistinguishable from a real leak' alarm applies to the test/QA harness. The functional half is also masked in tests: StepBars falls back to base = SSRNextBarOpenMsc(now, PERIOD_M1) (line 1165), so dense in-memory data still advances correctly - only gap-skipping is silently lost. Design smell plus a latent trap for any future non-MT5 source; not a live product bug.

**Why:** SSR_FutureGuard.mqh:312-316: 'if(from_msc > m_horizon_msc) { Violation(from_msc); return false; }'. Memory provider ReadBars (SSR_MemoryDataSource.mqh:122-127) calls GuardRange first and returns 0 when it is false. The comment at lines 143-148 acknowledges the INVALID answer ('correctly, and uselessly') but not the violation count. Production is unaffected because CSSRMt5BarProvider overrides with CopyTime (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:302). RECOMMENDATION: make the generic implementation a times-only walk that bypasses the guard (a bar's open time is schedule, not price — the Mt5 override already argues this) or have it not count violations.

**Verifiers:** The mechanism is provable and I could not find a guard that prevents it. CSSRBarProvider::NextBarOpen (SSR_IDataSource.mqh:150-165) calls the virtual ReadBars with from = after_msc + 1 for all four spans. CSSRMemoryBarProvider::ReadBars (Sources/SSR_MemoryDataSource.mqh:113-125) calls GuardRange first and returns 0 when it is false; GuardRange forwards to CSSRFutureGuard::ClampRange, which does `if(from_msc > m_horizon_msc) { Violation(from_msc); return false; }`. The callers do pass after_msc == now: CSSRReplayController::StepBars calls NextTimelineBarOpen(m_clock.now_msc) at line 1166 BEFORE m_guard.SetHorizon(m_clock.now_msc) at 1175, and the horizon is already == now from the previous pump/step (SetHorizon at 1009/1084/1175/1244/1361) or == timeline.start_msc at READY (Arm at 832). So from = now + 1 > horizon for all four spans: four Violation() increments and SSR_INVALID_TIME every time, whether or not there is a gap. The guard does reach this provider - the generic CSSRDataSource::SetGuard (SSR_IDataSource.mqh:244-253) is invoked from the controller at line 573. Two corrections below / Every link verified. CSSRBarProvider::NextBarOpen (SSR_IDataSource.mqh:150-165) calls ReadBars(symbol, after_msc + 1, after_msc + spans[i], tmp) four times. CSSRMemoryBarProvider::ReadBars (Core/Sources/SSR_MemoryDataSource.mqh:115-124) calls GuardRange first and returns 0 when it is false, and CSSRFutureGuard::ClampRange refuses with Violation(from_msc) whenever from_msc > m_horizon_msc (SSR_FutureGuard.mqh:90-96). The horizon equals the clock: SetHorizon(now) on every Pump (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1009) and PumpTo (:1084). StepBars calls NextTimelineBarOpen(m_clock.now_msc) at :1166 BEFORE SetHorizon at :1175, so from_msc = now + 1 > horizon for all four spans - four violations, answer always SSR_INVALID_TIME. CSSRMasterClock multiplies it: NextBarAcross loops every member calling NextTimelineBarOpen (SSR_MasterClock.mqh:329-334) from StepBars (:348) and the idle path (:211), so it is 4 x member count per call, and those counters are summed into the UI vitals (SSR_GroupPort.mqh: out.guard_violations += m.Violations()). Severity LOW and latent, as the finding itself says: CSSRMt5BarProvider overrides with a times-only CopyTime walk (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:302-320), so production never takes this path - the exposure is the memory provider used in tests and any future CSV/external source / The mechanism is accurately described but the state is unreachable in the product, and the base class already specifies the contract. SSR_IDataSource.mqh:143-148 states in terms that 'a provider whose ReadBars is clamped by the future guard will answer INVALID from inside a gap - correctly, and uselessly. Such a provider must override this with a TIMES-ONLY read', and the shipped provider does exactly that: CSSRMt5BarProvider::NextBarOpen uses CopyTime and bypasses the guard (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:302-322). The only class that inherits the generic body is CSSRMemoryBarProvider, and CSSRMemoryDataSource is referenced solely from MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Tests/* - never from MQL5/Experts (the host holds CSSRMt5DataSource g_src / g_src2 at SSReplayStandalone.mq5:189,298) and never from QA/SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5. So the UI-vitals leak alarm the finding worries about is fed only by the MT5 provider and cannot be inflated by this path, and the guard is never falsely tripped in normal use. In the test harness the consequence is also nil: StepBars falls back to base = SSRNextBarOpenMsc (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1165-1168), which is correct for the dense synthetic data those tests use. The residual value is a hardening/hygiene suggestion for a hypothetical future CSV source, not a defect. Note the cited guard lines are wrong - ClampRange is SSR_FutureGuard.mqh:90-106, not 312-316

The rare boundary case preserves the counters but loses the open tick. Either way RestoreSnapshot needs a rewind that re-seats emitted_msc without resetting the counters.

SSR_ReplayCursor.mqh line 25 defines emitted_msc as the last instant handed to the sink. Pump line 1015-1017 emits PendingRange(now) -> cursor.Advance(hi=now) before the checkpoint at line 1039-1044, so emitted == taken_at. #### `data-7` — Discover() discards the last COMPLETE M1 bar whenever the market is closed, shortening every available range by one minute

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Data/SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:125`** · category: boundary

```mql5
      if(last_quote > 0 && last_quote <= lastbar_close)
         out.last_msc = lastbar_open - 1;      // the forming bar is not data yet
      else
         out.last_msc = lastbar_close;
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Correct, and broader than the weekend case: the test fires for ANY last_quote at or before the final bar's close, which includes a stale quote that predates the last bar entirely (a symbol whose M1 was downloaded from the server while it is not being quoted). So the one-minute shortfall applies whenever quoting has stopped or lags the series, not only on a Saturday; the else branch that keeps the full last bar is taken only when the quote feed is ahead of the M1 series.

**Why:** The test asks "does the symbol's last quote fall inside the last bar?" as a proxy for "is that bar still forming", but the two differ precisely when quoting has stopped: for a closed market the last quote always falls inside the last bar, and the bar is nevertheless final. There is no check of the symbol's trade/quote session state (SymbolInfoSessionQuote, SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE) or of how far behind the last quote is relative to wall time, either of which would separate the two cases. The cost is bounded at one M1 bar, which is why this is LOW, but it is a systematic off-by-one on the timeline bound that every other class in the subsystem trusts.

**Verifiers:** Traced and it is worse than runtime-contingent - it is deterministic. The last M1 bar exists because a tick landed in it, so for a symbol that has stopped quoting the last quote necessarily satisfies lastbar_open <= last_quote <= lastbar_close, making the test at SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:123 true and out.last_msc = lastbar_open-1, discarding a bar that can never receive another tick. The else branch is only taken when the last quote is NEWER than the final bar's close, i.e. when the M1 series is lagging the quote feed. The consumer chain is as claimed: SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1075 uses range.last_msc directly as win_end, and CSSRHistoryCatalog exposes the same range. No guard, clamp or later correction exists anywhere on that path / The arithmetic is exactly as described and checks out against the constants: SSR_MSC_PER_MIN is 60000 (SSR_Types.mqh:31), lastbar_close = lastbar_open + 59999, and the true branch sets out.last_msc = lastbar_open - 1, which drops the whole final M1 bar (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:117-125). The forming-bar proxy "last quote falls inside the last bar" is indeed unconditionally true on a closed market, because the tick that created the final bar IS the last quote, and the code tests neither SymbolInfoSessionQuote/SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE nor the lag against wall time. It stays POTENTIAL_RISK under this lens because the conclusion rests entirely on the runtime value SymbolInfoInteger(SYMBOL_TIME_MSC) returns for a closed symbol - plausibly the cached Friday quote (giving the off-by-one), but possibly 0 after a terminal restart or symbol re-select, which takes the else branch and is correct - and that cannot be settled without a terminal. Impact is bounded at one M1 bar on win_end (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1076 uses range.last_msc directly), so LOW is right / The logic is exactly as described. SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:121-128 uses 'is the symbol's last quote inside the last bar?' as a proxy for 'is that bar still forming', and on a closed market the last quote is ALWAYS inside the last bar (the last bar is by definition the one the last tick built), so the test fires and out.last_msc = lastbar_open - 1 drops a bar that can never change again. No session-state check (SymbolInfoSessionQuote, SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE) or wall-clock-lag check exists to separate the two cases. But the impact under any realistic use is one M1 bar at the far end of a timeline thousands of bars long, and it errs in the SAFE direction: it withholds data, it never exposes anything beyond the horizon, so no future-data or money-arithmetic consequence. The user-visible consequence is that LatestStart/CanStartAt/win_end land one minute earlier than they could - nothing they can perceive, and every downstream consumer stays self-consistent because they all read the same shortened bound. LOW overstates a one-minute conservative bias; this is a boundary-precision cleanup

But the finder's worked example is wrong, which is why the severity drops: m_last_seq is overwritten with each executed sequence (line 243), so 1,2,3 after a restart all execute / The ABA weakness is real — `seq == m_last_seq` is plain equality against the last EXECUTED sequence rather than a monotonic test or a comparison with the published cmd.ack, m_last_seq survives client restarts (only Begin() clears it, line 138), CSSRClient::m_seq starts at 0 (SSR_Client.mqh:46) and Refresh() never reads cmd.ack, and on the early return nothing is written to cmd.ack or cmd.rc so the client can only fall out of the spin loop on the timeout branch (SSR_Client.mqh:201-219) with the wrong diagnosis. #### `mt5-symbol-8` — Destroy() reports SSR_OK and marks the symbol gone even when CustomSymbolDelete fails

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Mt5/SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:557`** · category: object-lifecycle

Callers discard the bool: sink Release() (SSR_CustomSymbolSink.mqh:389), sink destructor (73-74) and Create()'s pre-emptive Destroy() (318). So after a refused delete, IsCreated() reports the symbol gone while it remains in the terminal, and no log line records it - the orphan accumulation the file header (10-15) warns about. Only the missing-diagnostic consequence is provable; whether CustomSymbolDelete actually refuses is runtime, which is why LOW is right / Provable from source. Destroy() (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:544-586) captures ok = CustomSymbolDelete(m_symbol), sets m_created = false unconditionally on the next line, calls Succeed() unconditionally at 584 - clearing m_last_error to SSR_OK and m_last_error_text to "" (91-94) - and returns ok. The GetLastError() that the ResetLastError() at 556 was staged for is never read. Every caller discards the bool: the sink destructor (SSR_CustomSymbolSink.mqh:73-74), Release() (385-391), Create()'s own pre-teardown (318), and the T3 tests. So after a refused delete IsCreated() reports false while the symbol is still in the terminal, and LastError()/LastErrorText() report success, which is the opposite of the read-back-and-report discipline the rest of this file applies (chart mode at 387-395, sessions at 195-215). The consequence is bounded - the symbol was already deselected from Market Watch at 553 and the next run's Create()/Destroy() or adopt fallback usually sweeps it - so LOW / Provable as written: Destroy sets m_created=false before knowing the outcome and calls Succeed() unconditionally (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:557-585), so LastError()/LastErrorText() report OK after a refused CustomSymbolDelete, GetLastError() from that call is discarded, and both callers ignore the returned bool (CSSRCustomSymbolSink::Release lines 383-391 and its destructor lines 69-75). The consequence is a silently surviving symbol. Impact is limited, which supports LOW rather than anything higher: the survivor is bounded per slot and is reclaimed on the next run - Create() sets m_symbol then calls Destroy() again (CloseCharts + retry), and failing that the adopt fallback takes it over - and the seed manifest was already invalidated before Destroy, so no stale history can be presented as this session's. Nothing here touches trade accounting or leaks future data; the real loss is the diagnostic line the file header's "forty dead symbols" warning would want

SSR_Types.mqh:35 defines SSR_VERSION as "0.1.0" and `git log -S'define SSR_VERSION'` on that file returns only the initial commit dc87fa3, while the stamp that actually moves lives separately (SSR_Build.mqh:22, "v125 2026-09-12") and never enters the manifest - SSRSeedManifest::Init copies only SSR_VERSION (SSR_SeedCache.mqh:43) and Save writes only that (112). So the guard at 176-177 can never fire for any build of this program, and a manifest plus custom symbol written by any earlier build is honoured whenever origin and range agree. Severity LOW rather than higher because CanReuse still demands origin equality (178), range coverage (184) and live bar evidence from SeriesInfoInteger (188-199); what it cannot detect is a symbol built with different symbol PROPERTIES (e.g. a pre-v120 LAST-mode index CFD), which is exactly the class of change a version guard exists for / Provable: SSR_VERSION is a fixed "0.1.0" (SSR_Types.mqh:35) while the stamp that actually moves lives elsewhere and is not in the manifest (SSR_Build.mqh:22, SSR_BUILD "v125"); SSRSeedManifest.Init copies only SSR_VERSION (SSR_SeedCache.mqh:43), so the guard at 176 can never fire and 'written by another version' is dead text. The concrete hazard is sharper than stated and I verified it: the cache-hit path adopts rather than creates (SSR_CustomSymbolSink.mqh:165-173 -> CSSRCustomSymbolManager::Adopt), and Adopt re-applies SPREAD_FLOAT, TRADE_MODE, Apply247Sessions and CloneMoneyProperties but NOT SYMBOL_CHART_MODE (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:476-497) - the BID forcing exists only in Create (383). So a replay symbol left behind by a pre-BID-fix build on an index/futures CFD can be reused by v125 in LAST mode, where CustomTicksAdd accepts ticks and builds no bars. Severity stays LOW because reaching it needs a stale symbol AND its manifest surviving from an older build on a LAST-mode instrument; within one build the reuse path is safe (coverage check plus Truncate(warmup_to+1) prevents a cached future), and no money arithmetic or trade safety is touched

#### `strategy-integration-report-3` — OnTick fires once per published batch, not once per tick, so the documented intrabar-management use is unreachable and TickCalls() under-reports

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Strategy/SSR_IStrategy.mqh:266`** · category: tick-ordering

```mql5
   //--- every tick, for strategies that manage intrabar. Whatever this
   //--- does on synthetic ticks rests on an invented order of prices,
   //--- and ctx.IsSynthetic() is how it can know.
   virtual void      OnTick(void) {}
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Whenever a published batch carries more than one tick — MAX/very high speed, catch-up, or a candle step — CSSRMarketView retains only the last tick's bid/ask, so the strategy's parameterless OnTick cannot see the intrabar excursion in that batch, and TickCalls() counts batches rather than ticks. At ordinary speeds each batch holds one tick, so the per-tick hook does fire per synthetic tick and the intrabar prices are visible.

**Why:** The hook takes no parameters, so the only tick data a strategy can reach is CSSRMarketView's m_bid/m_ask, which SSR_MarketView.mqh:191-198 sets from ticks[count-1] alone - the rest of the batch is discarded on arrival. CSSRStrategyHost::OnTicks calls m_strat[i].OnTick() once per OnTicks invocation (line 210) and increments m_tick_calls once (line 209). SSR_ReplayController.mqh:506-507 publishes one segment per M1 bar, whose length is m_synth.TicksForBar(fid) = InpTicksPerBar, so one OnTick per 8 ticks at the default. TickSynthesizer places those ticks across the whole minute (base_msc + i*59999/(n-1)) with the last pinned to the bar close, so the high and low genuinely exist in the batch and are genuinely dropped before the strategy is asked.

**Verifiers:** The mechanism is real but the stated frequency is wrong. Confirmed from source: CSSRMarketView::OnTicks keeps only ticks[count-1] (SSR_MarketView.mqh:191-198), the OnTick hook takes no parameters (SSR_IStrategy.mqh:266), and CSSRStrategyHost calls OnTick once per OnTicks per strategy while incrementing m_tick_calls once there too — so everything but the last tick of a batch is invisible and TickCalls() counts invocations, not ticks. What is NOT true is "exactly one OnTick per M1 bar at the default". The controller publishes only the ticks that fall inside the pump window (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:459-492: ticks outside lo..hi are dropped before the segment is formed, and a segment is only published when keep > 0), and the synthesizer spreads InpTicksPerBar ticks evenly across the minute (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:147). At 40 ms pumps (InpPumpMs=40) the window is 40 ms x speed, so below roughly 200x it is shorter than the ~8.5 s tick spacing and each batch carries a single tick — the strategy does see each synthetic price, including the bar's high and low. The collapse to one price per bar happens only where a batch spans a whole minute: MAX speed / catch-up, or a step-a-candle command / The delivery granularity is provable. SSR_ReplayController.mqh:502-511 publishes one bar context then one tick SEGMENT per M1 bar, each segment being that bar's synthesised ticks; CSSRStrategyHost::OnTicks calls m_strat[i].OnTick() exactly once per OnTicks invocation (SSR_StrategyHost.mqh:209-210). So with InpTicksPerBar=8 a strategy gets one OnTick per M1 bar, not per tick, and CSSRMarketView::OnTicks (SSR_MarketView.mqh:190-197) keeps only ticks[count-1], so the intrabar SEQUENCE is unrecoverable. Two parts of the evidence are wrong, hence the correction: the bar's high and low are NOT lost - PublishBar runs before PublishSegment and CSSRMarketView::OnBarContext (172-188) stores the full MqlRates, so ctx.market.High/Low(PERIOD_M1, 0) reaches them; and m_tick_calls is incremented inside the per-strategy loop, so it counts batches x enabled strategies, not batches / The mechanism is confirmed in source: the controller publishes one segment per M1 bar (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:503-511), CSSRStrategyHost calls m_strat[i].OnTick() once per OnTicks and increments m_tick_calls once (SSR_StrategyHost.mqh:209-210), and CSSRMarketView::OnTicks keeps only ticks[count-1] (SSR_MarketView.mqh:191-198). So OnTick fires per batch, ctx.market.Bid() is the batch's last price, and TickCalls()/"ticks=%I64d" names batches. But the impact statement overreaches: the bar context is published BEFORE its ticks and clipped to the window (ClipBar, 461), and CSSRMarketView exposes High()/Low()/Bar() at M1 shift 0 (SSR_MarketView.mqh:224-256), so the minute's high and low ARE readable inside OnTick - only the tick-by-tick ordering is not. Per-tick stop/target/trailing work is done by CSSRTradingEngine, which does receive the full batch, so a strategy using broker.Trail() still gets tick-granular trailing. No money corruption, no future leak, no weakening of the virtual guarantee: what is left is a contract/naming mismatch against the header comment. Downgraded MEDIUM -> LOW

#### `strategy-integration-report-13` — Group() returns shift 0 with a wrong open and an un-aggregated spread when the group began before the buffer did

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Strategy/SSR_MarketView.mqh:136`** · category: boundary

```mql5
      if(seen == shift && open_set)
        {
         if(shift == 0)
            return true;                // forming, and known to be so
         m_refusals++;
         return false;
        }
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Same defect, two corrections. (1) The trigger is not merely "the group began before the buffer did" and it is not reachable via MakeRoom: MakeRoom keeps 2048 M1 bars (~34 hours), which always spans several H4 groups, so the early-return at line 104 fires first. It needs the entire buffer to lie inside the requested shift-0 group, which happens early in a session or just after a rewind that trimmed almost everything. (2) high and low are NOT right either - they are folded only over the minutes present in the buffer, so the group's true extreme can be in the missing earlier part. Only close is certainly correct. out.spread being the newest minute's value (copied once at line 110) is arguably the intended reading of a forming bar's spread rather than a defect.

**Why:** out.open is overwritten on every backward step inside the group (line 125), so when the loop terminates by exhausting the buffer rather than by crossing a group boundary, the last write came from m_m1[0] - not from the group's first bar. The shift==0 early return skips both the m_refusals++ and the false that the shift>0 case gets. out.spread has the same shape: it is copied once from the group's newest M1 bar at line 110 and never aggregated, so it describes one minute rather than the group. Available() does count such a group (it returns 1 when groups==1), so a strategy checking availability first is not protected.

**Verifiers:** Group() does return an un-refused, half-built shift-0 group, but only on a narrower precondition than the finder describes, and more fields are wrong than claimed. Trace: crossing into an older group hits the early `if(seen == shift && open_set) return true;` at 104-105, so a complete group is returned there. Line 136 is reached only when the backward walk never leaves group 0 - i.e. EVERY bar in the buffer belongs to the requested shift-0 group. In that case out.open was last overwritten at 125 from m_m1[0] (the oldest bar the buffer happens to hold), the shift==0 branch returns true, and neither m_refusals++ nor the false that the shift>0 case gets is executed. Available() returns 1 for that single group (372), so an availability check does not protect a caller. Reachable: early in a bar-driven session (OnSessionStart zeroes m_count, the first pump publishes a handful of M1 bars), or right after session start where PrimeView clamps `from` to StartMsc (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:396-397), or after a deep OnRewind - any moment when the whole buffer fits inside one H1/H4/D1 group / The control flow is as described. Group() walks newest-to-oldest; reaching line 136 with seen==0 means no bar from an earlier group was ever seen, i.e. the whole buffer lies inside group 0, so out.open is m_m1[0].open (the oldest buffered M1) rather than the group's true open, and the shift==0 early return at 138-139 skips both m_refusals++ and the refusal that shift>0 receives (140-141). out.spread is whatever line 110's `out = m_m1[i]` copied from the group's NEWEST M1 and is never aggregated. Available() returns 1 for groups==1 (line 372), so an availability check does not protect the caller. tick_volume/real_volume are correctly aggregated (no double count), so the defect is confined to open and spread / The asymmetry is real and provable. When the backward walk exhausts the buffer while still inside group 0, the post-loop block at 132-138 returns true for shift 0 while shift>0 gets m_refusals++ and false, and out.open was last written at line 125 from m_m1[0] - the oldest bar the buffer happens to hold, not the group's first M1 bar. Available() returns 1 for that state (`groups == 1 ? 1 : 0`), so the group is advertised as usable. Impact keeps this LOW: the state needs the entire M1 buffer to lie inside one tf group, which in practice means the first minutes of a session or just after a jump+prime with few bars, and it only ever affects shift 0 - the bar this class already documents as unreliable and tells strategies not to act on. The shipped reference strategy is protected twice over (it requires Available(tf) >= lookback+2 and reads shifts 1 and 2), so nothing in the product observes it today

#### `strategy-integration-report-6` — Prime() and OnRewind() trim on bar-open granularity, so the newest retained bar can hold prices from after the clock

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Strategy/SSR_MarketView.mqh:398`** · category: future-data-leakage

```mql5
         //--- strictly at or before the clock. Never past it.
         if(SSRToMsc(bars[i].time) > now_msc)
            break;
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Accurate. Note the contamination is confined to the newest M1 bar, hence to shift 0 on M1 and to the shift-0 group on higher timeframes; the shipped CSSRRefBreakout reads shift 1 and above and is therefore not exposed.

**Why:** SSRToMsc(bars[i].time) is the bar's open instant, and the comparison is `> now_msc`, so a bar opening at exactly now_msc is taken whole; MqlRates carries no intrabar detail that could be clipped here. OnRewind (lines 204-214) uses the same `<= msc` test on bar open times. Core does clip correctly on the live path (ClipBar, SSR_ReplayController.mqh:150-309), and in the bar-driven fidelities the next pump republishes that same minute clipped, which OnBarContext's time-match branch (lines 180-184) overwrites in place - and because PrimeView runs after g_group.Pump() in OnTimer (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2788 then 2797), that overwrite happens before the next strategy hook. So the exposure is confined to FULL_TICK, where no OnBarContext ever arrives to correct it and the contaminated bar remains the newest bar for the rest of the session.

**Verifiers:** Both tests really are on bar-open granularity and nothing downstream clips. Prime (398-399) breaks on `SSRToMsc(bars[i].time) > now_msc`, so the bar whose open is <= now_msc is admitted whole, high/low/close included - and I confirmed the supply side does not pre-clip: CSSRMt5BarProvider::ReadBars (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:252-285) delegates to CSSRBarWindow::Read, which admits every bar with open <= to_msc verbatim (SSR_BarWindow.mqh:272-277). MqlRates carries no intrabar detail, so the minute cannot be clipped here as ClipBar does on the live path. OnRewind (204-214) has the identical `<= msc` shape on open times. The self-correction the finder describes is real: OnBarContext's time-match branch (180-184) overwrites that minute in place with the clipped `shown` bar from SSR_ReplayController.mqh:459/506, and OnTimer runs Pump (2788) before PrimeView (2797) - but in FULL_TICK no OnBarContext ever arrives, so the correction never happens. LOW is right: the exposure lasts only until the clock walks past that minute, and the shipped reference strategy reads shift 1/2 rather than the shift-0 group that carries the contamination / The comparison at 398 is on bars[i].time, the bar's OPEN instant, so the M1 bar containing now_msc is admitted whole. The data path confirms the bar really is whole: CSSRFutureGuard::ClampRange/Allows work on instants (msc <= horizon) and CSSRBarWindow::Read (257-287) selects bars whose open <= to_msc and copies them unmodified, so PrimeView's ReadBars(g_origin, from, now, bars) returns the current minute with its full high/low/close - up to 59.999 s of prices past the clock. OnRewind (204-214) has the identical `<= msc` test on open times. The mitigations the finding names check out: ClipBar clips on the live path, the republished bar carries the same bar-open `time` so OnBarContext's 180-184 branch overwrites in place, and the pump runs before PrimeView in OnTimer (2788 then 2797), so the contamination is corrected before any strategy hook in the bar-driven fidelities and persists only under FULL_TICK / The trim is on bar-open granularity as claimed, and the layer below does not pre-clip: CSSRBarWindow::Read admits every bar whose open <= to_msc (SSR_BarWindow.mqh:274) and CSSRMt5BarProvider::ReadBars passes that straight back, so PrimeView hands Prime a final bar whose open is <= now and whose high/low/close can be up to 60 s past the clock; `> now_msc` at line 398 then keeps it whole. OnRewind (204-214) has the same open-time test. So the method's own header claim that it "TRIMS to" now_msc is not met for the boundary bar. Impact holds it at LOW: the contamination is confined to one M1 bar at the newest end of the buffer - shift 0 on M1 and part of the shift-0 group above - which this class documents as the forming bar a strategy must not act on, and the shipped reference strategy reads only shifts 1 and 2. In the bar-driven fidelities the next pump republishes that minute clipped and OnBarContext's time-match branch (180-184) overwrites it in place before the next strategy hook (Pump at 2788 precedes PrimeView at 2797), so it self-heals. In FULL_TICK it is never corrected, but within 60 s of replay the clock has passed that minute and the prices stop being future - and the bars are frozen anyway, which is finding -1's problem, not this one's

#### `strategy-integration-report-5` — CSSRMarketView::IsSynthetic() can never return false, so the honesty instrument it exists to be is dead

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Strategy/SSR_MarketView.mqh:427`** · category: spread

```mql5

```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: One narrow exception to "can never return false" that the finding misses, and it does not rescue the code: if fidelity were LOCKED with FULL_TICK requested and the source had no tick provider, Decide returns FULL_TICK unchanged (SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh:105-110), execution falls through to the bar-driven path, and PublishBar would pass synthetic=false over synthesized ticks - a lie in the unsafe direction. It is unreachable in production: CSSRReplayController::LockFidelity (line 679) has no caller anywhere in MQL5/, so m_locked is always false and IsSynthetic() is indeed a constant true.

Its only production caller is PublishBar at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:506, which passes `fid != SSR_FIDELITY_FULL_TICK`. That line is only reachable after the FULL_TICK branch has already returned (line 369) or degraded fid via m_fidelity.Decide() to SYNTHETIC_TICK because the source had no tick provider - in both cases fid != FULL_TICK holds, so the argument is always true. OnSessionStart (lines 159-171) does not reset m_synthetic either, so even a hypothetical false would persist across sessions.

**Verifiers:** m_synthetic is initialised true (151), assigned in exactly one place (175), and that assignment's only caller is PublishBar at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:506 with `fid != SSR_FIDELITY_FULL_TICK`. Fault direction is conservative, hence LOW / m_synthetic is initialised true in the constructor (151), assigned in exactly one place (175), and OnSessionStart (159-171) does not reset it. The only production caller is PublishBar at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:506 with `fid != SSR_FIDELITY_FULL_TICK`, and that line is reachable only after the FULL_TICK branch either returned (369) or degraded fid. Hence IsSynthetic() is a compile-time-constant true, CSSRStrategyContext::IsSynthetic() likewise, and CSSRRefBreakout::Status() always appends the caveat. Fault direction is conservative, as the finding says / Verified: m_synthetic is initialised true in the constructor, assigned in exactly one place (line 175), and its only production feed is PublishBar(seg_bar[sgi], fid != SSR_FIDELITY_FULL_TICK) at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:506 - which is downstream of the FULL_TICK early return at 369, so fid there is never FULL_TICK and the argument is always true. #### `strategy-integration-report-4` — The per-strategy RNG stream is seeded once at registration and is never re-seeded or rewound, so a strategy that uses it is not reproducible across a step-back

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Strategy/SSR_StrategyHost.mqh:141`** · category: session-resume

```mql5
      m_ctx[k].rng.Seed(m_seed ^ NameHash(s.Name()));
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Correct on the mechanism, but two overstatements. The strategy is not wholly powerless: rng is a public member of the context it is bound to (SSR_IStrategy.mqh:202), so a strategy can re-seed it deterministically from replay state in its own OnRewind hook; what it cannot obtain is the host's m_seed, so it cannot restore the host-derived stream. And no shipped strategy draws from ctx.rng, so this is a latent gap in the facility rather than a live reproducibility failure.

**Why:** This is the only Seed() call in the host, and it runs inside Add(). CSSRStrategyHost::OnSessionStart (lines 160-169) resets m_last_bar[] and re-Attaches each broker but does not touch m_ctx[i].rng; CSSRStrategyHost::OnRewind (lines 214-222) resets m_last_bar[i] and forwards OnRewind to the strategy but likewise leaves the RNG state alone. SSR_ReplayController.mqh broadcasts OnRewind at lines 1240, 1286, 1644 and 1669 (step back, reset, jump, snapshot restore) and OnSessionStart only at line 837 (Load), which the EA calls once. The seed is held privately in m_seed with no accessor, and CSSRStrategyContext exposes rng but not the seed, so a strategy has no way to re-derive m_seed ^ NameHash(name).

**Verifiers:** The code property is exactly as described: m_ctx[k].rng.Seed(...) at line 141 is the only Seed() call in the host and it runs inside Add(); OnSessionStart (160-169) resets m_last_bar and re-Attaches brokers only; OnRewind (214-222) resets m_last_bar and forwards OnRewind, leaving the stream advanced. m_seed is private with no accessor and CSSRStrategyContext (SSR_IStrategy.mqh:197-218) exposes rng but not the seed. So a step-back, a bookmark jump or a snapshot restore replays the same minutes with a different RNG stream. I am downgrading to LOW rather than refuting because the defect is entirely latent: grep for `rng.` shows no strategy uses ctx.rng at all (only spikes and CSSRRandomPicker draw from SSRRandom), so nothing in the shipped product is non-reproducible today, and the documented promise in SSR_IStrategy.mqh:20-24 - "the same session replays to the same trades" - is literally about replaying a session from its seed, which does hold / Line 141 is the only Seed() call in the host and it runs inside Add(); OnSessionStart (160-169) resets m_last_bar and re-Attaches brokers only, and OnRewind (214-222) resets m_last_bar and forwards the hook, neither touching m_ctx[i].rng. SSRRandom::Seed is the only state-setting entry point and every draw mutates state, so after a step back, jump or snapshot restore (PublishRewind at 1240, 1286, 1644, 1669) the same minutes replay against an advanced stream. m_seed is private with no accessor and CSSRStrategyContext exposes rng but not the seed / The code is as described: line 141 is the only Seed() call in the host and it runs inside Add(); OnSessionStart (160-169) and OnRewind (214-222) both leave m_ctx[i].rng untouched; m_seed is private with no accessor and CSSRStrategyContext exposes rng but not the seed. So a step back, a bookmark jump or a snapshot restore replays the same minutes with the stream already advanced, and the contract's "the same session replays to the same trades" (SSR_IStrategy.mqh:20-24) does not hold across a rewind for a strategy that draws from it. Downgraded to LOW on impact: no shipped strategy touches ctx.rng - CSSRRefBreakout is fully deterministic - so there is nothing a user can observe today, and the headline reproducibility promise the academy actually trades on (same seed, same candles, twenty students) is unaffected because the stream is seeded identically at registration in every terminal. This is a latent gap in a documented guarantee, waiting for the first strategy that uses the facility

#### `trading-analytics-5` — A day on which only a pending order was placed (even if cancelled) counts as a trading day

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Trading/SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:383`** · category: prop-rules

```mql5
int pos = Positions();
      if(pos > m_last_positions)
        {
         m_last_positions = pos;
         m_day_traded     = true;
        }
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Accurate. One reachability nuance: the count is only re-read inside OnClock, so an order placed and cancelled while the replay is PAUSED is attributed to whatever day is open at the next pump, not to the day it was placed.

**Why:** Positions() returns m_acct.Total() (l.134-135) = m_count, and CSSRTradingEngine::Open() does m_count++ for a pending order at placement (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:719-738) before any fill; cancellation does not decrement m_count. The evaluation only compares the count, never the state.

**Verifiers:** Provable. Positions() returns m_acct.Total() (l.134-135) which is m_count (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:973), and Open() does 'int i = m_count++;' (l.719) BEFORE the pending branch (l.728-737), which returns with state SSR_POS_PENDING and no fill. Cancellation only sets m_pos[i].state = SSR_POS_CANCELLED (l.872) and never decrements m_count - the only m_count-- in the file is the immediate rollback for a pending with no price (l.732). OnClock (l.383-388) compares the count alone and never inspects state, so the next clock after a placement sets m_day_traded = true for the day then open. Three days of place-and-cancel therefore satisfy min_trading_days with zero fills, and a pending placed on day 1 and filled on day 2 credits day 1 - which contradicts the accessor's own comment at l.131-133 ('a trade was OPENED that day'). No QA stage covers it: the evaluation harness (SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:5437-5452) only ever uses market Open/Close / Provable from source. Positions() returns m_acct.Total() (SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:134-135), and Total() returns m_count (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:973). Open() does 'int i = m_count++' before branching, and for a pending order returns after setting state = SSR_POS_PENDING (l.719-738) - the counter rose at placement, with no fill. Close() on a pending sets state = SSR_POS_CANCELLED and never decrements m_count (l.865-876; the only m_count-- in the file is the 'pending order needs a price' bail-out at l.732). OnClock (l.383-388) compares only the count and never the state, so a placed-and-cancelled pending sets m_day_traded = true - satisfying min_trading_days with zero fills - and a pending placed on day 1 and filled on day 2 credits day 1, contradicting the class comment 'a trade was OPENED that day' (l.131-133) / Provable from source: Positions() returns m_acct.Total() (l.134-135) which is m_count (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:973), CSSRTradingEngine::Open() increments m_count and returns at the SSR_POS_PENDING branch before any fill (l.719-738), and Close() on a pending merely stamps SSR_POS_CANCELLED without decrementing m_count (l.868-876) - PendingCount/ClosedCount exist but the evaluation never consults state. So OnClock's `pos > m_last_positions` (l.383-388) does credit a trading day for a pending order that was placed and cancelled, and credits the placement day rather than the fill day - which contradicts the file's own comment at l.131-133 ('a trade was OPENED that day'). Impact is small and confined to a self-imposed training rule: min_trading_days can be satisfied without a fill, but gaming it takes deliberate effort across separate replay days, no money arithmetic is touched, and the header already states that firms differ on this definition and that it is an input. LOW

#### `trading-analytics-9` — Equity ring drops its oldest half, so the live max drawdown can shrink and the peak be lost

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Trading/SSR_Statistics.mqh:272`** · category: drawdown-calc

```mql5
if(m_eq_count >= SSR_EQUITY_SAMPLES)
        {
         int keep = SSR_EQUITY_SAMPLES / 2;
         for(int i = 0; i < keep; i++)
           {
            m_eq_msc[i] = m_eq_msc[i + keep];
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Correct in substance, wrong in one detail: with a peak at minute 100 and a trough at minute 3000, the ring drop keeps samples [2048..4095], so the TROUGH survives and the PEAK is discarded - the statement's SVG and its drawdown number therefore stay mutually consistent, but both silently lose the earlier peak and the reported max drawdown shrinks as the session runs on. Reachable only when the replay span exceeds 4096 sampled minutes (default 2000 M1 bars does not).

**Why:** EquityDrawdown (l.347-364) starts peak at m_eq_val[0] of whatever survived; the drop keeps only samples [2048..4095]. The comment admits it ('drop the oldest half rather than the whole curve') but the peak-carrying half is the one discarded. SaveInto/RestoreFrom likewise cap at 4096.

**Verifiers:** Traced Sample() at SSR_Statistics.mqh:263-288. With SSR_EQUITY_SAMPLES=4096 (l.33) and SSR_EQUITY_INTERVAL_MSC=60000 (l.34), the ring fills after 4096 replay minutes; the truncation copies m_eq_[2048..4095] down to [0..2047] and sets m_eq_count=2048, so the OLDER half - the one that can hold the peak - is what is discarded. EquityDrawdown (l.347-364) seeds peak=m_eq_val[0] of whatever survived and there is no persisted running maximum: out.max_drawdown is recomputed from the live ring on every ComputeFor (l.596). So the reported max drawdown genuinely can decrease mid-session, and the in-code comment at l.272-274 ('losing every early sample would hide the drawdown that produced the peak we are still measuring against') describes the opposite of what the loop does. No guard, clamp or earlier check anywhere prevents it: OnRewind (l.325-338) only prunes forward, SaveInto/RestoreFrom (l.623-659) also cap at 4096. Reachability is real but requires a replay window > 4096 M1 minutes (~68h); InpReplayBars defaults to 2000 (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:71) so the default configuration never reaches it, which is why LOW is the right severity rather than higher / Source-provable: Sample() (SSR_Statistics.mqh:271-282) discards samples [0..2047] when m_eq_count reaches 4096, and EquityDrawdown (:347-364) re-derives peak from m_eq_val[0] of whatever survives. No running max is kept anywhere, so max_drawdown is recomputed over a truncated window and can DECREASE mid-session - a 'max' statistic that is not monotone. Nothing in MQL5 semantics rescues this; ArrayResize/EnsureRing and the copy loop are correct, so the only question is reachability, which is configuration, not opaque runtime: bars are M1 (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1076-1078), so >4096 replay minutes (~68h) is needed. Default InpReplayBars=2000 is safe, a week-long range or a custom range dialog span is not / Sample() (SSR_Statistics.mqh:268-281) keeps samples [2048..4095] on overflow and EquityDrawdown (l.347) restarts peak at m_eq_val[0] of the survivors, so a peak in the discarded half is lost and the reported max drawdown can DECREASE mid-session. Reachability is better than the finder allows: it needs >4096 replay minutes (~68 market hours), not reachable at the default InpReplayBars=2000, but InpStart (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:70) lets a user set any start date against range.last_msc, so 'replay last week' is a normal-use path with no cap in the range code. The wrong number is not cosmetic: max_drawdown/max_drawdown_pct feed the statement (SSR_Journal.mqh:1124-1131), the review card, and the instructor-side class report (SSR_ClassReport.mqh:228), and the error direction always UNDERSTATES risk, which is the dangerous one. Upgraded from LOW on that basis; not higher because it never touches balance/P&L arithmetic and only bites on multi-day windows

LOW is right: the position is virtual and bounded by the spread / Both halves check out in source. **`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Trading/SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:999`** · category: zero-empty

```mql5
double            AmbiguousPercent(void)

```

**Verifiers:** Numerator and denominator genuinely count different populations. m_ambiguous_count is incremented both for still-OPEN positions at fill time (CheckPendings 381-382) and for closes (BookExit 236-240), while AmbiguousPercent (999-1003) divides by ClosedCount(), which counts only state == SSR_POS_CLOSED (988-994). One ambiguous open fill with one unambiguous closed trade prints 100%, two print 200%, and with ambiguous fills but zero closes it prints 0%. The figure is not internal: it is published to external clients as SSR_GV_AMBIGUOUS (SSR_Publisher.mqh:206) and rendered by ToString (1266-1274) / Mismatched numerator and denominator, provable from source. m_ambiguous_count is incremented for a still-OPEN position at the pending-fill site (371-383) as well as for closes in BookExit (236-240), and RestoreFrom 1216-1217 counts the flag on positions in any state, while AmbiguousPercent (999-1003) divides by ClosedCount(), which counts only state == SSR_POS_CLOSED (988-994). So one ambiguous open fill against one clean closed trade reports 100%, two report 200%, and the figure is user-visible: ToString 1266-1273 prints it and Publisher 206 exports it to SSR_GV_AMBIGUOUS. The converse also holds - ambiguous open fills with nothing closed yet report 0.0%. LOW, since it misstates an honesty metric rather than the account / The arithmetic mismatch is real: m_ambiguous_count is incremented for OPEN positions at fill (381-383) as well as for closes (236-240), while AmbiguousPercent's denominator is ClosedCount() (988-994), which counts only state == CLOSED - so the ratio can exceed 100%, and conversely reports a flat 0.0 while ambiguous fills are open but nothing has closed yet. But the blast radius is far smaller than the finding implies: the user-facing honesty figure in the statement, the CSV and the HTML report does NOT come from this method. SSR_Statistics.mqh computes ambiguous_trades over closed positions only (loop filter at 407-408 `!p.IsClosed() -> continue`, count at 463-464) and divides by out.trades (544), which is correct. CSSRTradingEngine::AmbiguousPercent has exactly two consumers: ToString() (1271, a log line) and the Publisher's SSR_GV_AMBIGUOUS global export (SSR_Publisher.mqh:206). #### `ui-port-session-12` — The session list re-reads and fully parses every file on every dialog render

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Ui/SSR_GroupPort.mqh:937`** · category: cpu

**Verifiers:** Trace confirms no cache and no header-only mode anywhere on the path. Severity stays LOW: it is a modal, user-paced interaction and the cost is a file parse per visible row per click, not a correctness fault / Mechanism verified end to end. CSSRSessionManager::Peek (SessionManager:216-243) constructs a local CSSRSessionFile and calls f.Load(Path(name)); Load (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:206-259) reads the file line by line to EOF, appending every key=value pair - including every pos/leg/e row - into the dynamic m_ent_sec/m_ent_key/m_ent_val arrays before Peek reads its five [session] keys. GroupPort::SessionSummary (l.932-940) calls Peek per index with no cache, and the dialog calls m_port.SessionSummary(idx) inside its row loop bounded by SSR_SD_ROWS = 8 (SessionDialog:27, 172-173), with Render() re-entered on up, down, row click, load and after save (SessionDialog:255-257, 264, 284, and Open() from RequestSave). There is no header-only read mode anywhere. Two corrections to the magnitude rather than the mechanism: the parse is bounded by SSR_SF_MAX_ENTRIES = 16384 and SSR_SF_MAX_SECTIONS = 1024 (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:33-34), so the worst case is ~16k entries per file and ~131k per render, not the unbounded 9,000-per-file figure implied; and the cost is string/array work in a modal that a human clicks a handful of times, so it is an efficiency wart, not a hang. Severity stays LOW / The mechanism is real: Peek constructs a CSSRSessionFile and calls Load (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:213-219), which parses every line of the file into three parallel dynamic arrays before a single key is read (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:206-258), and the dialog calls m_port.SessionSummary(idx) once per visible row inside its render loop with SSR_SD_ROWS = 8 (SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:27, 172-174). No cache, no header-only mode. But the cost is far smaller than claimed and the trigger is narrower. Parsing is capped at SSR_SF_MAX_ENTRIES = 16384 entries per file with amortised doubling growth (Reserve, l.64-74), so per-file work is bounded regardless of trade count; and Render() runs only from Open() and from the dialog's own click handler - the host references g_session_dlg only at Create/Destroy/IsOpen/Open/OnEvent (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1466, 2116, 3052, 3091, 3167-3169), so it is not redrawn per pump.
