#### `ui-dialogs-15` — MenuClear only sweeps 32 menu items while presets.ini is unbounded, so a longer preset file orphans buttons on the chart

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Ui/SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:611`** · category: object-lifecycle

```mql5
   void              MenuClear(void)
     {
      m_w.Remove("mbg");
      for(int i = 0; i < 32; i++)
         m_w.Remove("m" + IntegerToString(i));
     }
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: MenuClear's hardcoded 32-slot sweep leaves m32.. on the chart when presets.ini holds more than 31 readable rows; they are stale, latched-looking buttons that persist until the next step change (Repaint/RemoveAll), and they are inert rather than still applying presets, since Poll only checks menu items for the currently open field's option range.

**Why:** LoadPresets sizes m_presets from `int rows = f.Count("p")` with no cap (:331-371); PresetNames returns all of them (:426-433) and DrawMenu creates one button per option (:639-641). Only Repaint()'s RemoveAll (:658, ObjectsDeleteAll by prefix) can clear the surplus, and Render() calls MenuClear - not RemoveAll - on every paint (:668). DrawMenu's off-screen defence is a single flip-upwards test (:633-635), which cannot help a list taller than the chart.

**Verifiers:** The count mismatch is real: LoadPresets applies no cap (rows = f.Count("p"), :331-371, and SSR_SessionFile caps only at 16384 entries), PresetNames returns all 1+n (:426-433), DrawMenu creates one button per option (:639-641), and MenuClear sweeps a hardcoded m0..m31 (:611-616). Render() calls MenuClear, not RemoveAll (:668), so with more than 31 file presets the surplus buttons persist across paints until a step change or Destroy. The 820 px list and the single flip-up test (:633-635) are also as described. One consequence is mis-stated: an orphan m32+ is NOT still applying a preset, because Poll only inspects menu items while m_menu != "" and only for i < n of the CURRENT field's option list (:1084-1096) - an orphan press is simply ignored, leaving a latched-down ghost button / The bound mismatch is real and provable: LoadPresets sizes from `int rows = f.Count("p")` with no cap (:344-346), PresetNames returns all 1+n names (:426-433), DrawMenu creates one button per option (:639-641), and MenuClear (:611-616) sweeps only mbg and m0..m31, so with more than 32 presets the surplus SSRS_m32.. survive every Render() (which calls MenuClear, not RemoveAll, :668) until a step change happens to call Repaint()/RemoveAll. The 820 px list and the single flip-upwards test (:632-635), which can only move an over-tall list off the top instead of the bottom, are also as described. One part of the claim is wrong, and it is the part that carries the severity / The 32-slot sweep in MenuClear (:611-616) really does not match DrawMenu's unbounded creation (:639-641), so the code smell is real - but the described user-visible defect is not reachable and the described click behaviour is wrong. (a) Reachability: presets.ini ships with 4 rows and each row is one challenge SHAPE (the file's own comment says so, :356-363); reaching 32+ requires a hand-edited file of over thirty presets, which is not normal use of this product. (b) The orphans are transient, not persistent: every 'next', 'back', mode press and quick-step press calls Repaint() -> m_w.RemoveAll() (:658), which is ObjectsDeleteAll by prefix and takes m32+ with it, and Destroy() does the same - so nothing survives the panel or even the next step change. (c) The claim that each orphan 'still applies a preset when pressed' is false: Poll only inspects m0..m(n-1) inside `if(m_menu != "")` (:1083-1096), and MenuClear runs precisely when the list has been closed (m_menu == ""), so a click on an orphan is inert - it merely latches the button. The residual worth fixing is the magic 32 itself (sweep ArraySize(m_presets) slots, or cap the list and page it), not a live defect a user can hit

#### `ui-dialogs-10` — The quick step builds the session path itself and skips the session manager's sanitiser, so 'Continue' disappears for names containing a slash or colon

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Ui/SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:712`** · category: input-validation

```mql5
      bool have_last    = FileIsExist(SSR_SETUP_FILE);
      bool have_session = (m_v.session_name != "" &&
                           FileIsExist("SSReplay\\sessions\\" +
                                       m_v.session_name + ".ssr"));
```

**What goes wrong:** Name a session "eu/us open" or "NY:2024-03-05". CSSRSessionManager stores it as sessions\eu_us open.ssr (it replaces \ / : with _), but the quick step tests for sessions\eu/us open.ssr, which cannot exist - so the "Continue ..." button is never offered and the user concludes the session was not saved. The same unsanitised name is what the panel writes to setup.ini and hands to the host.

**Why:** CSSRSessionManager::Path sanitises before use: `StringReplace(safe, "\\", "_"); StringReplace(safe, "/", "_"); StringReplace(safe, ":", "_");` (MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Session/SSR_SessionManager.mqh:92-97), and both Save (:167) and Exists (:117) go through it. SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:713-715 is the only place in the subsystem that concatenates a session path by hand, and Str("ses", ...) (:1175) applies no character validation or length limit of any kind.

**Verifiers:** Verified both sides. SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:713-715 concatenates "SSReplay\\sessions\\" + m_v.session_name + ".ssr" by hand, while CSSRSessionManager::Path (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:92-99) replaces \\, / and : with _ before building SSR_SESSION_DIR + "\\" + safe + SSR_SESSION_EXT (:43-44), and both Save (:167) and Exists (:117) go through Path. So a name containing / \\ or : is saved under a different filename than the quick step probes, have_session is false and the "Continue ..." button (:744) is never offered. Str("ses") (:1175) applies no character filter or length limit, so such a name is accepted. The host's own resume check uses the manager (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2015-2016), which is what makes the panel the odd one out / Verified on both sides. CSSRSessionManager::Path sanitises the name before any file call - StringReplace of \\, / and : with _ (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:92-98) - and Exists (:116-117) and Save (:167) both go through it, with SSR_SESSION_DIR = "SSReplay\\sessions" and SSR_SESSION_EXT = ".ssr" (:43-44). RenderQuick (:712-715) is the one place that concatenates that path by hand, from the raw m_v.session_name, so for a name containing / or : the FileIsExist test addresses a path the manager never writes (with / MQL5 treats it as a directory separator, so it looks inside a folder that does not exist) and have_session is false - the Continue button is never offered even though the .ssr file is on disk under the sanitised name. Str("ses", ...) (:1175) applies no character filter or length limit, so the unsanitised name is also what Save() writes to setup.ini (:1226). Cosmetic-severity: no data is lost, the resume path through the Session dialog still works / Provable inconsistency: RenderQuick concatenates "SSReplay\\sessions\\" + m_v.session_name + ".ssr" by hand (:712-715) while every real access goes through CSSRSessionManager::Path, which replaces backslash, forward slash and colon with underscore (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:92-98, used by Save :167 and Exists :117). A name containing / \ or : therefore tests a path that can never exist. Impact is narrow, though: it requires the user to type a separator character into 'Save as', and the only consequence is that the quick step omits the optional "Continue ..." shortcut. The session itself still saves under the sanitised name and InpResume + Exists still resumes it correctly, because both of those go through the sanitiser - so no data is lost and no state is corrupted; one convenience button is missing and a user could misread that as 'not saved'. Cosmetic-to-minor -> LOW confirmed

The secondary point is also correct but moot: :970 would set CHART_MOUSE_SCROLL true unconditionally, in code that cannot execute. Severity downgraded from MEDIUM: the pick line is a full-height OBJ_VLINE that can be grabbed above or below the panel, so this is a dead feature and a lost preference, not a blocked workflow / The MQL5 semantics are right and the grep is exhaustive. CHARTEVENT_MOUSE_MOVE is delivered only to programs on a chart whose CHART_EVENT_MOUSE_MOVE property is true, and that property defaults to false and has no terminal UI. The only writers in the tree are CSSRPanel::Create (SSR_Panel.mqh:324) and its restore in Destroy (:370) - grep over MQL5/** returns those lines and nothing else. The setup panel is created on the host chart during picking (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2069, ChartID(), so OnChartEvent does reach it at :3117), but g_panel.Create() runs only inside BuildSession (:1467) after the setup panel has been destroyed (:2522), and a prior run's Destroy put the saved value back, so nothing leaks the flag forward. OnChartEvent (:955-998) therefore returns at its first line on every event the chart does deliver: the drag, the CHART_MOUSE_SCROLL suspend/restore pair and SavePlace() are all unreachable, SSR_SETUP_X/Y are never written, LoadPlace never finds them, m_placed stays false and the panel re-centres every run. The secondary point is right too - the exit writes CHART_MOUSE_SCROLL = true unconditionally (:970) rather than restoring, unlike SSR_Panel.mqh:371 / The unreachability is provable from source. The setup panel is created on the EA's own chart in OnInit (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2069, ChartID()) and events are forwarded to it (:3117), so the handler is wired - but a grep of MQL5/** shows CHART_EVENT_MOUSE_MOVE is written in exactly one place, CSSRPanel::Create (SSR_Panel.mqh:324), which runs only later inside BuildSession (:1467) after the setup panel has been destroyed (:2522), and CSSRPanel::Destroy restores the saved value (:370) so nothing leaks into a later run. MT5 emits CHARTEVENT_MOUSE_MOVE only when that property is on and its default is off, so every branch of CSSRSetupPanel::OnChartEvent (:955-996) is dead on a fresh chart. Where I part company with the finder is severity. What the user loses is one convenience - the setup window cannot be dragged - and the fallback is benign: Create() already centres the panel on the tallest step (:531-544), m_placed simply stays false, and the two GlobalVariables are never written, which is not a corruption of anything. Every control is a click, so nothing is out of reach; the orange line can still be dragged wherever the panel is not, or fetched with the 'bring line here' button. No money arithmetic, no future-data leak, no weakening of the virtual-trading guarantee. The secondary point (CHART_MOUSE_SCROLL forced true at :970 instead of restored) sits inside the same dead code and has no effect at all. A documented-but-absent feature plus a small amount of dead code -> LOW, not MEDIUM

#### `ui-dialogs-9` — ReadAll clamps balance, risk, spread and speed but not the three prop numbers, so a typed 0 silently deletes a prop rule

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Ui/SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:1194`** · category: prop-rules

```mql5
      if(m_v.balance      <= 0.0)   m_v.balance      = 10000.0;
      if(m_v.risk_percent <= 0.0)   m_v.risk_percent = 0.5;
      if(m_v.risk_percent >  100.0) m_v.risk_percent = 100.0;
      if(m_v.spread_points < 0.0)   m_v.spread_points = 0.0;
      if(m_v.speed        <= 0.0)   m_v.speed        = 1.0;
      if(m_v.speed        > 10000.0)m_v.speed        = 10000.0;
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: ReadAll validates balance/risk/spread/speed but not the three prop numbers, so a 0 or negative typed into a prop box passes through and the corresponding > 0.0-gated rule is dropped - notably prop_on with profit target <= 0, an unpassable challenge that the panel's own presets.ini loader rejects (:342). The numbers are not hidden (step-3 recap :886-890 and the host's prop.ToString() log), and 0 meaning "no limit" matches the max_days convention, so the defect is the missing keyboard-side validation, not a silent deletion.

**Why:** ReadAll assigns prop_target/prop_daily/prop_total from Num() at :1176-1178 and the clamp block at :1191-1199 never mentions them. Downstream: SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:391 `if(m_rules.max_daily_loss_pct > 0.0 && eq <= DailyFloor())`, :401 the same for max_total_loss_pct, :429 the same for profit_target_pct, :207 `if(!m_started || m_rules.profit_target_pct <= 0.0) return 0`. The values reach the rules via the host's CfgPropTgt/Dly/Tot accessors (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:239-241).

**Verifiers:** The asymmetry is real and provable. ReadAll assigns prop_target/prop_daily/prop_total from Num() (:1176-1178) and the clamp block (:1191-1199) never mentions them; Num() returns 0.0 for a typed "0" because the unreadable-guard only rejects a zero whose first character is not '0' (:295). The host copies them straight into the rules with no validation (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1189-1191), and every rule is gated on > 0.0 (SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:391, :401, :429, and TargetProgress at :207), so a typed 0 or negative disables that rule and a zero target makes the challenge unpassable while the prop chips still show. The panel's own preset loader refuses exactly that shape (:342). Two claim details are wrong: the values ARE echoed - step 3 recaps "Evaluation %.1f / %.1f / %.1f %%" (:886-890) and the host prints prop.ToString() when the evaluation is on (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1201) - and 0 = "no limit" is this codebase's own convention (max_days > 0 at SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:419). What survives is the unvalidated prop_on + target <= 0 combination / The mechanics are confirmed: ReadAll assigns prop_target/prop_daily/prop_total from Num() (:1176-1178) and the clamp block (:1191-1199) names only balance, risk, spread and speed; Num() returns 0.0 for a typed "0" (the :295 guard exempts a leading '0') and passes a negative straight through; the values reach the rules via CfgPropTgt/Dly/Tot (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:239-241) and SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh guards each rule with > 0.0 (:391, :401, :429, :207). But the claim over-reads the guards. `max_daily_loss_pct > 0.0` is the deliberate 'this rule is not configured' convention - a challenge with no daily loss limit is a real firm's terms, and LoadPresets accepts exactly that shape (it rejects only `on != 0 && tg <= 0.0`, :342). So a zero daily-loss or drawdown figure is a configuration, not a dropped rule / Code-provable: prop_target/prop_daily/prop_total are assigned from Num() at :1176-1178 and the clamp block at :1191-1199 never mentions them, so 0 and negatives pass through (Num's unreadable-guard lets "0" through explicitly because the first character is '0', :295). Downstream every rule is gated on `> 0.0` (SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:391, :401, :429, :207), so a zero silently removes the rule, and prop_on + target 0 is a challenge that can never be passed. The panel's own preset loader rejects exactly that shape (:342), so the inconsistency between the file path and the keyboard path is real. Severity stays LOW, and one claim needs correcting: it is not true that 'nothing anywhere says a rule was dropped' - step 3's recap prints the three numbers verbatim, "Evaluation 0.0 / 5.0 / 10.0" (:886-891), on the screen carrying the START button. Nothing here touches money arithmetic or the virtual-trading guarantee; the worst case is a training rule the user believes is armed and is not, on values they can see

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Accurate, with the impact stated more precisely: the wrong hint fails safe (R draws lines, it does not reset), and the authoritative list is still correct because SSR_KeyCard is generated from SSRKeyBindings(); the defect is that the panel's hand-written hint line contradicts it and fa.txt has translated the error.

**Why:** SSR_Keys.mqh's own header (lines 79-88) states the reason the binding table exists: "Two lists drift - always, and silently, and the one that drifts is the one the user is reading." The key CARD is generated from the table, but these three hint lines are hand-written strings in the catalogue and nothing cross-checks them against SSRKeyBindings(). SSR_KeyCard.mqh's header even names this exact case: "R moved from reset to the stop-and-target lines in this very build; a second list would already be wrong."

**Verifiers:** Straight contradiction between two lists, both read. The Persian catalogue faithfully reproduces the error: MQL5/Files/SSReplay/lang/fa.txt:216 reads `keys.2 = + - سرعت    R شروع دوباره    J پرش    B نشانه` ("R start over"). Nothing cross-checks these hand-written strings against SSRKeyBindings() / The mismatch is provable. SSR_Strings.mqh:499-500 sets SSR_S_KEYS_2 to "+ - speed    R reset    J jump    B bookmark" and SSR_Panel.mqh:1902-1904 draws it as the 'keyhint' label on the Session tab. SSR_Keys.mqh:162-164 binds SSR_VK_R to SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE ('stop and target lines on / off') and SSR_Keys.mqh:200-202 binds SSR_CMD_RESET to SSR_VK_0, under a comment block ('RESET MOVED OFF R, and off every letter') that documents the move the hint line was never updated for. Nothing cross-checks these hand-written strings against SSRKeyBindings(). Downgraded to LOW rather than MEDIUM because the consequence is non-destructive in the safe direction - pressing R places the SL/TP lines instead of destroying the session - and the generated key card (H) still lists 0 correctly, so the correct information is reachable in the product / The drift is provable in both directions: SSR_Keys.mqh:162-164 binds SSR_VK_R to SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE and :200-202 binds SSR_CMD_RESET to '0', while SSR_Strings.mqh:499-501 states 'R reset' and SSR_Panel.mqh:1902-1904 draws that string as the 'keyhint' label on the Session tab. Nothing cross-checks the four hand-written SSR_S_KEYS_* lines against SSRKeyBindings(), and fa.txt repeats the error. Downgraded on impact rather than refuted: pressing R runs ArmLines/ClearLines - non-destructive, instantly visible, and undone by pressing R again - and the user who wanted reset has both the panel's own Reset button (SSR_Panel.mqh:1037, which asks for confirmation via ResetWithConfirm at :2292) and the key card, which is generated from the table and therefore names '0  start the session over (asks first)' correctly. So the false statement misleads for one keystroke; it destroys nothing and blocks nothing

#### `ui-plumbing-6` — The property cache has no tombstones: Forget() can silently clear nothing and Keep() then writes a duplicate, leaking slots until the cache stops working

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Ui/SSR_Widgets.mqh:103`** · category: memory

```mql5
   void              Forget(const string name)
     {
      int k = Slot(name);
      if(k >= 0 && m_ck[k] == name)
        { m_ck[k] = ""; m_cn[k] = 0; m_ct[k] = ""; }
     }
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Forget() can resolve to a free earlier slot in the probe chain and clear nothing, after which Keep() stores a duplicate and the off-home entry is orphaned for the life of the cache. Two parts of the finding are wrong, though. (1) The leak is self-limiting, not one slot per Hide at 10 Hz: once the orphan exists it occupies its slot and so removes the free-slot precondition for that chain, and the next Forget/Keep pair re-converges on a stable placement - steady state is a small constant number of orphans per colliding chain, bounded by chain reconfigurations, so the '8-slot probe run fills and the cache switches off' end-state is not established by this code. (2) Contrary to the finding's own evidence, the shadowed duplicate is not always harmless: if another name later occupies the earlier slot, Slot() resolves the name onto the ORPHAN tuple, and Same() then compares the request against a state the object no longer holds - a matching comparison skips the write and leaves the wrong colour/text. That path is neutralised for every Remove()-invalidated name (the object is deleted, so Same()'s ObjectFind check fails) and is only live for Hide()-invalidated names, which are never deleted.

**Why:** Slot() stops at the first slot that is either free or matching, so after any deletion earlier in a probe chain the lookup for a later name resolves to the wrong (free) slot. Forget() guards on m_ck[k] == name and therefore becomes a no-op instead of finding the real entry; Keep() then stores a second copy at the earlier slot. Nothing ever reclaims the old copy: ForgetAll() runs only from Attach() (when chart or prefix changes) and RemoveAll(). The failure is not a wrong pixel - the shadowed duplicate is only reachable once a third name occupies the earlier slot, and by then the object's real state matches the tuple that is found - but the slot is permanently consumed.

**Verifiers:** The mechanism is exactly as coded. Slot() (SSR_Widgets.mqh:58-77) stops at the first free-OR-matching slot, Forget() (101-107) then guards on m_ck[k]==name and silently no-ops when the probe lands on a freed earlier slot, and Keep() (91-99) writes a second copy there; nothing but ForgetAll() (Attach/RemoveAll) ever reclaims the orphan. Home-slot collisions are certain at this load: hashing the panel's real names (SSRP_ prefix, ~264 of them in 512 slots) with the file's own FNV-1a gives 53 colliding home slots (e.g. SSRP_lines/SSRP_pn3, SSRP_riskval/SSRP_spdseg0, SSRP_hintrow/SSRP_palette), and the churn that supplies the freed earlier slot is real - HideSheets() Removes ~100 names and 6x SSR_POS_MAX row names at the top of every repaint, and SSR_Panel.mqh:1937-1940 Hides four status names unconditionally per frame. I could not refute the duplicate-slot leak / The mechanism is fully settled from source. Slot() (SSR_Widgets.mqh:57-76) returns the FIRST free-or-matching slot in an 8-probe run, so once an earlier slot in a probe chain is cleared, a displaced name resolves to it; Forget() (103-108) then guards on m_ck[k]==name and no-ops, and Keep() (86-94) writes a second live copy at the earlier slot, orphaning the later one forever (only ForgetAll(), i.e. Attach-with-changed-chart/prefix or RemoveAll(), reclaims it). Displacement is not hypothetical: I computed FNV-1a exactly as Slot() does over the 107 literal widget ids found in SSR_Panel.mqh under the SSRP_ prefix and 12 of them already land on an occupied home slot - and the real name set is considerably larger (composite widgets add _bg/_fill/_fr/_lb/_lg/_tk/_th/_ac/_lim children, plus 20 spdseg cells, 5 tabs and the list rows). The churn that opens the window is also per-frame and unconditional: Hide() calls Forget() whether or not the object exists (SSR_Widgets.mqh:634-642), and SSR_Panel.mqh:1931-1940 hides stflt/stopen/stspread/stfid on every render while 2085-2099 hides the whole id list, 5 tabs, 20 speed cells and the groove/thumb on every collapse. Two things in the write-up are imprecise rather than wrong, hence the corrected claim / The logic defect is provable: Slot() (Widgets:70-76) returns the FIRST free-or-matching slot in the 8-probe run, so a hole earlier in a chain shadows a real entry further down; Forget() (Widgets:103-108) then guards on m_ck[k]==name and clears nothing, and the next Keep() writes a second copy at the earlier slot, permanently consuming the shadowed one. Nothing reclaims it (ForgetAll only runs from Attach on a chart/prefix change and from RemoveAll). Reachability is in fact far higher than the finder argues: SSR_Panel.mqh:1284-1340 HideSheets() calls m_w.Remove() on ~80 ids plus 6*SSR_POS_MAX row ids at the top of EVERY repaint, so holes are punched and Forget() is called hundreds of times per second. But the impact is bounded and non-visual: the only certain consequence is attrition of a performance cache - and the objects that churn hardest (all sheet labels) are deleted and recreated every frame anyway, so they never benefited from the cache. The claimed end state (an 8-slot run fully saturated, Slot() returning -1, the 561-write/39.05 ms repaint returning) is a projection, not something the source establishes. No money arithmetic, no future data, no virtual-trading guarantee is touched, so MEDIUM is one step too high

#### `spikes-audits-30` — The UIJitter probe divides by its window-size input with no validation

**`MQL5/Indicators/SSReplay/Spike/SSR_Probe_UIJitter.mq5:66`** · category: input-validation

```mql5
g_samp[g_head] = jitter_ms;
g_head = (g_head + 1) % InpWindow;
if(g_count < InpWindow) g_count++;
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: InpWindow is used unclamped as an array size (:34) and a modulus (:66). With InpWindow=0 the first OnTimer's g_samp[0] write is an array-out-of-range critical error that kills the indicator before the modulus runs; with a negative value ArrayResize fails, the buffer stays zero-length and the same out-of-range write occurs (no division by zero). Misuse-only, LOW; a MathMax clamp like CSSRTickSynthesizer::SetTicksPerBar would close it.

**Why:** OnInit does `ArrayResize(g_samp, InpWindow); ArrayInitialize(g_samp, 0.0);` with no clamp, and EventSetMillisecondTimer(InpPeriodMs) is likewise unvalidated. OnTimer's first statement after the timing arithmetic is the indexed write at line 65 followed by the modulus at line 66. Report() guards only against too few samples (g_count < 5 at line 79), not against a zero-length buffer. Compare CSSRTickSynthesizer::SetTicksPerBar (Core/SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:106), where the product clamps the analogous input: `m_ticks_per_bar = (n < 4 ? 4 : n)`.

**Verifiers:** Traced the whole path and found no clamp. OnInit does ArrayResize(g_samp, InpWindow) then ArrayInitialize with no validation (lines 34-35) and starts the timer (line 42); OnTimer's first buffer statement is the indexed write g_samp[g_head] (line 65) followed immediately by % InpWindow (line 66). With InpWindow=0 the array is length 0, so the write is an array-out-of-range critical error on the first timer beat; a negative value makes ArrayResize fail (size stays 0) with the same outcome, and the modulus is a zero-divide. Report()'s only guard is g_count < 5 (line 79), which is downstream of the fault. The comparison to CSSRTickSynthesizer::SetTicksPerBar's clamp is accurate. LOW is right: it needs a deliberate misconfiguration of a dev-only probe whose default is 2000 / Unvalidated input is real: OnInit does ArrayResize(g_samp, InpWindow)/ArrayInitialize with no clamp (:34-35) and OnTimer indexes g_samp[g_head] then takes % InpWindow (:65-66); Report()'s only guard is g_count < 5 (:79). With InpWindow=0 the indexed write into a zero-length dynamic array is an out-of-range critical error, which is established MQL5 semantics, and it stops the program before the modulus is ever evaluated - so the 'divides by zero' ordering is wrong. The negative case is also mis-described: ArrayResize with a negative size fails and leaves size 0, so the same out-of-range write occurs, but % with a negative modulus is well defined and is not a fault. Reaching any of this requires a deliberately invalid input to a spike probe, and whether the terminal reports or silently removes the indicator is runtime behaviour - hence at most POTENTIAL_RISK, LOW / Missing validation is real and provable: SSR_Probe_UIJitter.mq5 OnInit does ArrayResize(g_samp, InpWindow) with no clamp (:33-34 of the file), and OnTimer writes g_samp[g_head] then takes (g_head+1) % InpWindow (:65-66) - with InpWindow=0 the indexed write hits a zero-length array and a negative value gives ArrayResize a negative size; Report() guards only g_count<5. Compare CSSRTickSynthesizer::SetTicksPerBar, which does clamp. But impact under normal use is nil: the default is 2000, this is a developer-only diagnostic indicator that ships to no trader, and the failure requires someone to deliberately type 0 or a negative into a 'Samples kept for percentiles' input. Nothing is corrupted, nothing is leaked, and the failure is loud and immediate (the probe dies on attach) rather than silent. IMPROVEMENT, not LOW

#### `qa-smoke-7` — Stage 7 increments the pass count with no condition tested

```

**What goes wrong:** This is the only unconditional Ok() in the file and it asserts nothing: reaching the line is the whole of its evidence, which is implied by control flow. The file's own rule for an unmeasurable property is Note(), which moves neither counter (lines 262-263, used at 1789, 2212, 4153, 4390, 4464, 4609, 4646, 4731, 4980, 5057, 5075).

**Verifiers:** Line 724 is `Ok("manager redraws on demand", "Redraw(force) returned")`, unconditional inside the `if(Check("a chart can be opened..."))` block, and Ok() at line 226 does `g_pass++` with no predicate. grep '^\s*Ok(' returns exactly two hits, 724 and 2207, and 2207 sits inside `if(!loaded) { if(cal.Available()) ... }`. Note() at 262-263 moves neither counter, which is the file's own idiom for an unmeasurable property. The suggested alternative is also available: CSSRChartManager::Redraw is declared `bool Redraw(const bool force = false)` (SSR_ChartManager.mqh:531) and Snaps() is already read two lines above at 719 / Confirmed from source. `grep '^\s*Ok('` returns exactly two hits (724 and 2207); 2207 sits inside `if(cal.Available())` (2206). Line 724 `Ok("manager redraws on demand", "Redraw(force) returned")` takes no condition, so g_pass is incremented for a property nothing evaluated - reaching the line is implied by the control flow that already ran mgr.Redraw(true) four times above. CSSRChartManager::Redraw does return bool (SSR_ChartManager.mqh:531) and mgr.Snaps() (589) is read two lines above, so an assertable value is in hand; Note() (262) is the file's own device for an unmeasurable property / Verified: l.724 is the only unguarded Ok() in the file (the other, l.2207, sits inside `if(cal.Available())`), it tests nothing, and it adds one to g_pass on every run, so the '=== N passed ===' headline overstates measured properties by one. Downgraded from LOW to IMPROVEMENT under the impact lens: the effect is confined to one line of a self-report the author reads, the detail string is honest about what happened ('Redraw(force) returned'), and mgr.Snaps() two lines above was already asserted by the neighbouring check - so no property the user depends on is left unmeasured. This is test hygiene, not a defect with an observable consequence

So a future regression in the price-scale restore would be reported as PASS / The asymmetry is provable: the Apply assertion (1140-1143) names CHART_SHOW_OHLC and CHART_SHOW_PRICE_SCALE, the restore assertion (1144-1147) names only CHART_SHOW_OHLC, and had_scale is never captured beside had_ohlc at 1130. Stage 36 repeats it (3700-3702). Two corrections: CSSRBlindMode::Restore (SSR_BlindMode.mqh) writes all three remembered properties back (CHART_SHOW_DATE_SCALE, CHART_SHOW_OHLC, CHART_SHOW_PRICE_SCALE) from a snapshot taken once per chart, so the product does not in fact leave a chart without its price axis - this is a QA coverage gap, not the trap the finding implies. And 'the default in several shipped MetaTrader profiles' is an unverifiable claim about terminal defaults; the vacuous `false == false` case is real but only on a terminal whose template has OHLC off / The asymmetry is real and provable: the Apply assertion at l.1143-1146 names CHART_SHOW_OHLC and CHART_SHOW_PRICE_SCALE, the restore assertion at l.1144-1149 names only OHLC, and had_scale is never captured beside had_ohlc at l.1130; stage 36 repeats it at l.3696-3702. But the finding's stated consequence does not follow. CSSRBlindMode::Restore (SSR_BlindMode.mqh) writes CHART_SHOW_DATE_SCALE, CHART_SHOW_OHLC and CHART_SHOW_PRICE_SCALE back from per-chart saved state unconditionally, so there is no reachable state in which a user's chart is left without a price axis - the product keeps the promise the check only half measures. The second half ('vacuous when the template has OHLC off') is correct in form but its trigger is the terminal's default template, which I cannot settle from source. #### `qa-smoke-12` — SSR_Z_Gaps can report more than 100% of minutes present, and InpMinRun=0 turns every bar into a hole

**`MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/QA/SSR_Z_Gaps.mq5:52`** · category: boundary

```mql5
   int span = (int)((InpTo - InpFrom) / 60);
   PrintFormat("  %d bars across %d minutes (%.1f%% present)",
               n, span, span > 0 ? 100.0 * n / span : 0.0);
...
      if(gap < InpMinRun)
         continue;
```

**What goes wrong:** CopyRates with a start_time/stop_time pair is inclusive of both ends, so the default range 11:00..12:00 returns 61 bars for a span computed as 60 minutes and the script prints '61 bars across 60 minutes (101.7% present)'. The whole point of this script is to be the arbiter of whether missing candles are the broker's fault, and a coverage figure above 100% undermines the one number the reader is being asked to trust. Separately, InpMinRun is used unclamped: set it to 0 and every consecutive pair of bars has gap == 0 >= 0, so the script reports n-1 'holes', prints twenty lines reading 'HOLE 0 minute(s) missing after ...', and then concludes 'A replay crossing these will show the clock moving with no new candle' about a range with no holes in it at all.

**Why:** span counts intervals while n counts bars over an inclusive range, so n == span + 1 on a complete range - (InpTo - InpFrom)/60 + 1 is the matching denominator. The gap test at line 63 has no lower bound on InpMinRun, and the input's comment ('Report holes of at least this many minutes') does not describe 0 as a value; a MathMax(1, InpMinRun) at the top of OnStart matches the documented intent.

**Verifiers:** Both halves check out in source. (a) span = (InpTo-InpFrom)/60 counts intervals (line 52) while n counts bars returned by CopyRates(sym, PERIOD_M1, InpFrom, InpTo, r) (line 41), whose start/stop form includes both boundary bars - the repo itself relies on that inclusivity elsewhere (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:389-394 documents CopyTicksRange as 'INCLUSIVE at both ends' and compensates by +1ms). A complete 11:00..12:00 range therefore yields n = span+1 = 61 and prints 101.7%. (b) gap = intervals-1 at line 62 and the filter is gap < InpMinRun at line 63, so InpMinRun=0 makes every adjacent pair (gap 0) a hole: holes = n-1, twenty 'HOLE 0 minute(s) missing' lines, then the '... and N more holes' tail and the closing 'A replay crossing these...' conclusion, on a range with no missing minute. Nothing clamps InpMinRun anywhere in OnStart. Cosmetic/reporting only, in a diagnostic script - LOW / The InpMinRun half is airtight from source: gap = (dt/60) - 1 is 0 for adjacent bars and the filter is 'if(gap < InpMinRun) continue' (:62-63), so InpMinRun=0 (or negative) passes every one of the n-1 pairs, prints up to twenty 'HOLE 0 minute(s) missing' lines, skips the NO HOLES branch (:76) and ends with the broker-blame conclusion on a range with no holes. The coverage half rests on documented CopyRates(start_time, stop_time) inclusivity of both ends, which makes n = span + 1 on a complete range and prints 101.7% for the default 11:00..12:00; span counts intervals while n counts bars, so (InpTo-InpFrom)/60 + 1 is the matching denominator. Nothing here contradicts established ground truth. LOW, as claimed - a QA script's cosmetic/threshold nit, not product behaviour / Both halves check out against SSR_Z_Gaps.mq5. (a) span = (InpTo-InpFrom)/60 counts intervals (:52) while CopyRates with a start/stop pair is inclusive of both endpoints, so a complete default range 11:00..12:00 yields 61 bars over span 60 and line 53 prints '101.7% present'. This is the default path - no unusual input needed. (b) The gap filter at :63 is 'if(gap < InpMinRun) continue' with no lower clamp, so InpMinRun=0 admits gap==0, making every consecutive bar pair a 'HOLE 0 minute(s) missing' and driving the script past the 'NO HOLES' branch into the broker-blaming conclusion (:82-84) on a range with no holes. Impact is bounded: this is a QA diagnostic script the author runs by hand, its output is a printed log line, and the hole list itself (times and sizes) is still correct - only the coverage percentage and the InpMinRun=0 degenerate case mislead. No money arithmetic, no user-facing surface. LOW is right

The cost objection is also real and sits two comments below the author's own note that a single day of ticks per probe made the audit 'look hung' (lines 60-64): a week of COPY_TICKS_ALL per symbol, up to InpMaxAuto=6, and if the allocation fails got is -1 and cap = -1 is published as a tick count. #### `spikes-audits-14` — C3's torn-read test runs the writer and the reader sequentially in one thread, so 'race-free' cannot fail

**`MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Spike/SSR_C3_IpcChannel.mq5:82`** · category: event-handling

Nothing refutes the finding / Verified at SSR_C3_IpcChannel.mq5:79-98. The writer block (lines 82-85) and reader block (lines 88-96) are consecutive statements inside one for-loop body of a single script; MQL5 script execution is single-threaded and GlobalVariableSet/Get are synchronous, so a1/a2/a3 are always the values just written for the current i, and `seq != last_seq` is true every iteration with seq == i. `torn` is therefore structurally 0 and `seq_last_protocol_safe` cannot fail. I confirmed nothing else in the tree writes SSR.c3.cmd.* (grep across MQL5/ finds only this file), and the suite has no concurrent pair: MQL5/Services/SSReplay/Spike holds C1 and C2 (each standalone) and MQL5/Indicators/SSReplay/Spike holds only the two probes, neither of which touches GlobalVariable*. So the concurrency claim in the header (lines 6-7) is untested anywhere / Mechanically true. SSR_C3_IpcChannel.mq5:79-98 is one for-loop inside a single OnStart: four GlobalVariableSet calls then three GlobalVariableGet calls, no Sleep, no second program, no timer, no indicator/service. `seq` is read immediately after being written, so `a1==seq*7` etc. hold by construction and `torn` is structurally 0; the verdict seq_last_protocol_safe cannot fail, and would still pass with the seq-last ordering removed. No second program is instantiated anywhere in the spike suite. A torn read, if it ever happened, would land on a virtual-only command (SSR_CMD_BUY volume/sl/tp) with no real-money path. HIGH overstates it - the finding is a measurement-validity gap in a research spike, not a defect a user can reach

The supporting metric at 109-119 likewise counts every Market Watch symbol whose SYMBOL_TIME exceeds a 2024 timestamp, which is every symbol quoted since then, closed markets included. The symbols_ahead_of_replay metric (lines 109-119) likewise counts every Market Watch symbol quoted since 2024, including permanently closed ones, under a note claiming each 'can drag TimeCurrent forward'. CustomTicksAdd's int return is indeed discarded at line 70 / Both halves check out. (a) InpStart is D'2024.01.08' (SSR_C4_ReplayClock.mq5:20) and sym_t is SYMBOL_TIME after injecting ticks stamped from that base, so `(long)tc != sym_t` at line 119 is true by the input contract on any connected terminal; it demonstrates two clocks reading differently, not the stated counter-claim that other Market Watch symbols drag TimeCurrent forward. symbols_ahead_of_replay (lines 108-118) counts every symbol quoted since 2024, closed markets included, which is effectively total_mw. (b) Line 69 is a bare `CustomTicksAdd(InpTest, tk);` with the accepted count discarded, and SSR_MakeSymbol (SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:303-335) never sets SYMBOL_CHART_MODE to BID, so a rejecting clone is a live possibility. T13.8 draws no random number and never touches a context: s1.Name() == s2.Name() compares the constant "ref-breakout" (SSR_RefStrategy.mqh:48) against itself, h2.Count() counts registrations, and the NULL check only proves Add succeeded. #### `tests-b-5` — T15.8 never establishes its precondition, so all four keyboard-takeover assertions pass on a chart where quick navigation is already off

**`MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Tests/SSR_T15_Ux.mq5:421`** · category: event-handling

```mql5
      long was_nav = ChartGetInteger(chart, CHART_QUICK_NAVIGATION);
      long was_key = ChartGetInteger(chart, CHART_KEYBOARD_CONTROL);
      ...
      CheckEq("quick navigation is off while the panel lives",
              0, ChartGetInteger(chart, CHART_QUICK_NAVIGATION));
      ...
      CheckEq("quick navigation is given back",
              was_nav, ChartGetInteger(chart, CHART_QUICK_NAVIGATION));

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: The test is not unconditionally vacuous - on a default chart (quick navigation and keyboard control both on) all four assertions do bite. The defect is the missing precondition: it never asserts or forces was_nav/was_key == 1, so the section silently stops guarding on any chart where they are already off (including one left that way by an earlier T15.8 run that died between Create and Destroy).

**Why:** The section reads the current values into was_nav/was_key and never forces them to a known state (no ChartSetInteger(..., true) before Create). CSSRPanel::Create saves them (SSR_Panel.mqh:320-321) and writes false (343-344); Destroy writes the saved values back (372-373). With was_nav == 0 the first CheckEq compares 0 against a value that was already 0, and the restore CheckEq compares 0 against 0. So SSR_T1_CoreEngine.mq5:355 `CheckEq("warmup survived the reset", seeded, sink.SeedBarCount())` can only fail on spurious re-seeding, never on warmup deletion. The sink's public surface (lines 129-145: TickCount, SeedBarCount, Truncations, Seeks, Resets, FirstTickMsc, LastTickMsc, TickAt, CountAfter) exposes no live bar count, so the claim that no assertion in the current API could detect a deleted warmup holds. SSR_T8:315-320 repeats the same pattern for Restart, as claimed / Verified: CSSRRecordingSink::SeedBars is `m_seed_bars += count;` (SSR_RecordingSink.mqh:69-72) and m_seed_bars is written nowhere else except Clear(). TruncateFrom (102-121) rewrites m_ticks/m_tick_count/m_last_msc only. CSSRReplayController::Reset (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1268-1297) calls m_sink.TruncateFrom(m_timeline.start_msc) then m_sink.OnReset(), and OnReset is `{ m_resets++; }`. So `CheckEq("warmup survived the reset", seeded, sink.SeedBarCount())` compares a monotone write counter against itself; it can only fail on extra re-seeding. T8.8:315-320 is the same pattern for Restart / The mechanics are exactly as stated: CSSRRecordingSink::SeedBars is `m_seed_bars += count;` (SSR_RecordingSink.mqh:71), TruncateFrom (103-119) rewrites m_ticks/m_tick_count/m_last_msc and never touches m_seed_bars, and only Clear() resets it. So CheckEq("warmup survived the reset", seeded, sink.SeedBarCount()) at T1:355 cannot fail if Reset deleted the warmup - it only catches the opposite fault, spurious re-seeding. #### `tests-a-9` — T2.6's stated dangling-guard test never lets the guard die

**`MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Tests/SSR_T2_DataEngine.mq5:297`** · category: object-lifecycle

To actually test it, the guard must go out of scope (or be `new`/`delete`d) before the post-detach read.

**Verifiers:** Lifetimes traced and the claim holds. `CSSRFutureGuard guard;` is declared at T2:267 as a stack object inside the `else` block opened at :265 and closed at :304; DetachGuard() is at :299 and the read at :301, both while `guard` is still alive, so no dangling pointer can be dereferenced. The assertion is also insensitive to the behaviour it names: CSSRMt5BarProvider::ReadBars (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:259-263) returns 0 via `Succeed()` when GuardRange rejects the range, so if DetachGuard were a no-op the still-armed guard would refuse the pure-future window and na would be 0 — `na >= 0` passes either way, exactly as it passes when detach works and bars come back. `src` is declared at T2:183, outside the block, so the two lifetimes are inverted relative to the hazard the comment describes. Severity lowered from MEDIUM: the production lifetime handling is correct — DetachGuard only nulls pointers, it never dereferences — so this is purely an untested-path gap, not a live object-lifecycle defect / The assertion is provably non-discriminating. CSSRMt5BarProvider::ReadBars (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:259-263) returns 0 - not -1 - when GuardRange refuses the range, and T2:282 already pins that behaviour. So at T2:301-303 na is 0 if DetachGuard did nothing (guard still armed at win_start, range wholly in the future) and > 0 if it worked; `na >= 0` passes in both cases, testing only 'no crash', never the detach. The guard object is still in scope (declared T2:267, block closes T2:304), so the stated use-after-free is not exercised at the read. One claim in the evidence is wrong: the post-scope dangling path IS traversed later - T2.9 (:416-444) calls src.Mt5Bars().ReadBars after the guard's block has closed - it is simply unasserted and would manifest as a crash or garbage rather than a red check, which is also runtime behaviour I cannot settle from source / Scope proves it. `CSSRFutureGuard guard;` is a stack object of the else block opened at T2:265 and closed at T2:304, and the post-detach read is at T2:301, so the guard is still alive at the read and the stated use-after-free lifetime is never created. The check is weaker still than the finding says: `na >= 0` passes whether DetachGuard worked (guard gone, future bars returned, na > 0) or did nothing (guard still armed, refusal, na == 0), so it does not even verify detachment, only that the call did not error. Impact is nonetheless test-coverage only: no defect in the guard itself is shown, and the future-leak protection is asserted positively elsewhere in the same section (T2:280-295). MEDIUM overstates a missing test; LOW

T3:434 calls second.Destroy(), which reaches CustomSymbolDelete(m_symbol) at SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:544-556, so the symbol is gone when T3.8 begins. T3:441 mgr.Destroy() then re-runs CloseCharts/SymbolSelect(false)/CustomSymbolDelete on an absent name, its return value discarded, and the assertion at 448 (`e != 0 || d == 0` after SymbolInfoInteger on a nonexistent symbol) passes for a reason unrelated to teardown. OpenChartCount() at 450 likewise returns 0 trivially. No intervening guard recreates the symbol between 434 and 441 / T3.7 (SSR_T3_CustomSymbol.mq5:414-435) ends with second.Destroy(); a.Create and mgr.Create both resolve m_symbol via SSRReplaySymbolNameFor(origin, slot, m_anonymous) (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:307), and T3:427 asserts second.Symbol() == a.Symbol(). Destroy (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:543-586) closes charts, deselects, then CustomSymbolDelete, so the symbol is gone before T3.8 runs; mgr.Destroy() at line 441 is then a no-op whose return value is discarded, and SymbolInfoInteger on an absent symbol yields d==0 with a non-zero error, satisfying `e != 0 || d == 0` regardless. I also checked that no other section could catch a Destroy regression: Create() explicitly adopts a pre-existing replay symbol when CustomSymbolCreate fails (lines 328-348), so T3.7's 'second create succeeds over the leftover' would still pass with Destroy stubbed out / Traceable end to end. mgr, a and second all call Create(origin, InpSlot) and set m_symbol = SSRReplaySymbolNameFor(origin, slot, m_anonymous) (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:307), and T3:427 asserts second.Symbol() == a.Symbol(). T3.7's last statement is second.Destroy() (T3:434), which reaches CustomSymbolDelete (line ~550). So by T3.8 the symbol is already absent, mgr.Destroy() is effectively a no-op whose bool return is discarded, and both assertions - `e != 0 || d == 0` and OpenChartCount()==0 (which can only count charts on a symbol that no longer exists) - pass regardless of what Destroy does. Impact is bounded, though: a regressed Destroy would leave a custom symbol behind, and the product already treats that as survivable - Create() calls Destroy() then adopts a leftover (T3.7 is the test for exactly that), and SSR_Z_Cleanup exists (T3:456). #### `tests-a-13` — T8.5's clamp and no-op assertions read only a return value, and one of them is a hardcoded true

**`MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Tests/SSR_T8_Navigation.mq5:223`** · category: boundary

```mql5
      Check("jumping to now is a no-op", ctrl.JumpTo(ctrl.Now()));

      //--- out of range must be clamped, not refused into an error
      Check("clamped past the end", ctrl.JumpTo(g_end + 999999999));
```

**What goes wrong:** "jumping to now is a no-op" can never fail: `JumpTo` returns a literal `true` on the equal-target path. "clamped past the end" never reads `ctrl.Now()` afterwards, so it cannot tell a correct clamp to `end_msc` from a clamp to the wrong instant - clamping to `start_msc`, or landing one bar short, would pass while silently rewinding the user's whole session. The section is titled "JumpTo picks the right direction" and the out-of-range case is the one place where the landing point is never checked; every other jump in T8.5 does assert `ctrl.Now()`.

**Why:** `CSSRReplayController::JumpTo` (SSR_ReplayController.mqh) clamps with `long target = SSRClampMsc(target_msc, m_timeline.start_msc, m_timeline.end_msc);` and then has `if(target == m_clock.now_msc) return true;` - an unconditional true for the no-op case - plus `if(delta <= 0) return true;` on the backward path. For the over-range case it falls through to `return (JumpForward(target) >= 0);`. Adding `CheckEq("landed on the end", g_end, ctrl.Now())` (or the bar-open form used at T8:220) would close both.

**Verifiers:** Traced CSSRReplayController::JumpTo (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1484-1520). With the clock configured (Wire/Load succeeded earlier in T8.5), JumpTo(ctrl.Now()) clamps to the same value, fails `target < m_clock.now_msc`, hits `if(target == m_clock.now_msc) return true;` at line 1517 and returns an unconditional true - so T8:223 is a tautology for any loaded controller. For T8:226, JumpTo(g_end + 999999999) clamps to m_timeline.end_msc and returns (JumpForward(target) >= 0); the section's only follow-up is Status() != SSR_STATE_ERROR (line 227), never ctrl.Now(), so a clamp to the wrong instant - or a short landing - is invisible, unlike every other jump in the section which does assert the landing point (lines 214, 218-220). Confirmed as described; severity IMPROVEMENT since this is missing test coverage, with no evidence the clamp itself is wrong / Both halves check out against CSSRReplayController::JumpTo (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1484-1512). With a configured clock, JumpTo(ctrl.Now()) clamps to now (SSRClampMsc against a range that contains it) and hits `if(target == m_clock.now_msc) return true;` - an unconditional true, so T8:223 cannot fail for any state the section can reach (the backward path has the same `if(delta <= 0) return true;`). For the over-range case, JumpTo(g_end + 999999999) clamps to end_msc and returns JumpForward(target) >= 0; T8:226-228 then asserts only the bool and Status() != SSR_STATE_ERROR, never ctrl.Now(), so a clamp to the wrong instant - start_msc, which would take the StepBackward branch and also return true - would pass. Every other jump in T8.5 does assert the landing point (T8:216-220), which makes the omission the section's one hole / Both halves verified against CSSRReplayController::JumpTo (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1484-1519). With the clock configured and now_msc inside [start_msc, end_msc], JumpTo(ctrl.Now()) clamps to now, skips the backward branch and hits 'if(target == m_clock.now_msc) return true;' - an unconditional true, so T8:223 cannot fail (the backward branch likewise returns a literal true when delta <= 0). T8:226 reads only the boolean from the over-range call and never re-reads ctrl.Now(), so a clamp to the wrong endpoint would also pass: clamping to start_msc would take the backward branch and StepBackward returns true. Every other jump in T8.5 does assert the landing point (lines 215, 219, 220-221), which makes the omission visible. Severity LOW is right: the clamp in the code is correct (SSRClampMsc against timeline start/end), so this is missing coverage rather than a live defect; no money arithmetic, no future-data exposure, and the neighbouring check at line 227 still proves the state is not ERROR. Fix is one CheckEq on ctrl.Now() after line 226

SeekTo(target) }`. StepBackward picks between the snapshot branch and the SeekTo fallback at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1451-1472, and the only observable that separates them is m_restores, exposed as Restores() (line 90) and bumped solely by NoteRestore() (line 162) on the snapshot branch. I grepped the whole MQL5 tree: Restores() has zero callers, and SnapshotText() (controller:1591) is passed only as the FAIL detail string, which is never printed on a pass. So both of T9.7's rewinds could take the SeekTo fallback with every assertion still green. Severity lowered to LOW: this is a missing assertion in a test, not a defect in shipped behaviour, and the fallback branch is itself correct (it seeks, it just restarts counters) / Verified: StepBackward branches at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1450-1472 between RestoreSnapshot+NoteRestore and the SeekTo fallback, and CSSRSnapshotStore::Count() (SSR_SnapshotStore.mqh:87) reports ring occupancy only - the branch-distinguishing counter Restores() (line 90, incremented solely in NoteRestore at 162) is public and never touched by T9.7. So the section's stated subject, the snapshot path, is not asserted. Impact is bounded though, which is why MEDIUM is too high: the fallback branch is not a wrong-answer path - it performs a correct SeekTo and the controller itself logs a warning ("no checkpoint before ...; counters will restart", lines 1467-1469), so a silent slide onto it degrades counter continuity rather than corrupting the rewind. The two assertions the phase actually turns on (the trade ceased to exist, open count restored) remain valid on either branch, so no future-data leak or money error can hide here - only loss of coverage over RestoreSnapshot

#### `spikes-audits-22` — C2's documented manual procedure stops the service 60 seconds before its own run-length gate is satisfied

**`MQL5/Services/SSReplay/Spike/SSR_C2_ServicePersistence.mq5:121`** · category: measurement-validity

```

**What goes wrong:** The header's step-by-step procedure ends with 't+300s stop the service' while InpRunSec defaults to 360, and the gate requires uptime >= 342 s. An operator who follows the printed instructions exactly gets IsStopped() at 300 s, an uptime of 300 s, and a FAILED survived_full_run - so the correct execution of the procedure guarantees a failing verdict, and the spike's result cannot be read as evidence either way.

**Why:** Header line 19: 't+300s  stop the service'. Line 28: `input int InpRunSec = 360;`. The loop at line 69 is `while(!IsStopped())` and exits early on operator stop; uptime_s is then computed at line 106 from the real elapsed time. 300 < 360*0.95 = 342, so the verdict fails. The other two verdicts (no_restart, no_long_gaps) are unaffected, which makes the failure look like a partial result rather than an instruction/default mismatch.

**Verifiers:** Arithmetic and control flow both check out. Header line 19 instructs 't+300s stop the service'; InpRunSec defaults to 360 (line 28); the loop is while(!IsStopped()) (line 69) with an internal break only at uptime >= InpRunSec*1000.0 ms (line 97), so an operator stop at 300 s exits via IsStopped(). uptime_s is then computed from real elapsed microseconds (line 106) and the gate at line 121 requires uptime_s >= 360*0.95 = 342, so 300 < 342 FAILs deterministically for anyone following the printed procedure. no_restart and no_long_gaps are computed independently and are unaffected, matching the claim. Downgraded to LOW: this is a header/default mismatch in a spike harness, fixed either by changing the printed t+300s or the InpRunSec default, and it produces a false FAIL rather than a false PASS / Purely arithmetic and provable from the file. Header line 19 instructs 't+300s stop the service'; line 28 is `input int InpRunSec = 360;`; the loop at line 69 is while(!IsStopped()) and breaks early when the operator stops it, after which uptime_s is computed from the real elapsed microsecond count at line 106; the gate at line 121 is uptime_s >= InpRunSec * 0.95 = 342. So an operator who follows the printed procedure exactly gets ~300 s and a FAILED survived_full_run, while the other two verdicts pass - which reads as a partial result rather than as an instruction/default mismatch. Severity lowered to LOW: this is a false FAIL in spike code, visible immediately and fixable by one number, not a false PASS that could mislead a design decision / Verified: header line 19 is 't+300s stop the service', line 28 is input int InpRunSec = 360, and line 121 gates survived_full_run on uptime_s >= InpRunSec * 0.95 = 342 s. The loop at 69 is while(!IsStopped()) and exits as soon as the operator stops it, after which uptime_s is computed from real elapsed time at line 106, so following the printed procedure exactly yields ~300 s and a guaranteed FAILED verdict while the other two verdicts pass - which reads as a partial result rather than an instruction/default mismatch. Severity downgraded from MEDIUM to LOW on impact: the failure is self-explaining because SSR_Verdict prints expected '360s' beside actual '300s', so the arithmetic is visible in the result row; an operator who simply lets the service run to its own break at line 97 gets a PASS; and this is a Tier-C measurement spike with no product surface - no money arithmetic, no future-data leak, no weakening of the virtual-trading guarantee. One-line fix either way (InpRunSec = 300, or amend the header to t+360s)

**`tools/ssr_audit.py:425`** · category: audit-coverage

METHOD_DEF = re.compile(r'^\s*(?:virtual\s+|static\s+|const\s+)*'

The ([^)]*) truncation on a default argument containing parentheses is also real (verified: 'bool Load(const int a, const int b=f(1))' keys on the truncated arg string). The contrast with DECL_METHOD (line 348, '\s*[\*&]?\s*') and its comment at 343-345 is exactly as quoted / Verified by executing the regex. METHOD_DEF (ssr_audit.py:425-427) is `[A-Za-z_][\w:]*\s*[\*&]?\s+` — the `\s+` after the optional star is mandatory, so `   CSSRBarProvider *Bars(void)` and `   CSSRBarProvider  *Bars(void)` both return None, while `   CSSRBarProvider* Bars(void)` matches. The codebase uses the star-hugs-name form in 16 places (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:566, SSR_StrategyHost.mqh:99, SSR_ChartManager.mqh:191, SSR_ReplayController.mqh:617-618,1590, SSR_MasterClock.mqh:89, SSR_IDataSource.mqh:93, SSR_Mt5DataSource.mqh:142-144, SSR_CustomSymbolSink.mqh:128,132, SSR_GroupPort.mqh:66, ...), so A9 cannot see a duplicate of any of them — exactly the 'member function already defined' shape A9 exists for, and exactly the bug the comment at 343-345 records fixing in DECL_METHOD (346-349, which correctly uses `\s*[\*&]?\s*`). The `([^)]*)` argument group also truncates at the first ')', so a default argument containing parens yields a wrong key. Tool-coverage gap only, no shipped defect today, hence LOW / The regex gap is real and I reproduced it: METHOD_DEF's mandatory `\s+` after the optional `[\*&]?` means `CSSRBarProvider *Bars(void)` never matches (tested; `CSSRBarProvider* Bars(void)` does). 16 declarations in 11 files use the star-hugs-name style the tree actually writes, so a duplicate of any of them is invisible to A9 — the exact accident A9 was written for, and with no MT5 compiler in the build environment an audit blind spot is the only line of defence. BUT the second half of the claim is false: I ran A9's loop over a class containing a duplicated pointer method AND a duplicated void method, and it still fired on the void duplicate. Class-scope bookkeeping is brace-counting on every line, independent of METHOD_DEF, so nothing 'is found only by luck'. Impact-wise nothing is user-observable: no shipped behaviour changes, the cost is one MetaEditor round trip if a future patch duplicates a pointer-returning getter. LOW, not higher

#### `core-sync-6` — SnapshotStore::DropFrom leaves holes in the ring without adjusting m_count/m_head, so Count() over-reports and the next checkpoints overwrite the oldest survivors instead of refilling the holes

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Core/SSR_SnapshotStore.mqh:140`** · category: boundary

```mql5
   int               DropFrom(const long msc)
     {
      int dropped = 0;
      for(int i = 0; i < m_count; i++)
        {
         if(m_ring[i].taken_at_msc >= msc)
           { m_ring[i].Init(); dropped++; }
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Real but overstated in one respect: overwriting the oldest entry is normal full-ring behaviour, so the loss versus an ideal implementation is k checkpoints (k x 5 min) of the oldest history plus a temporary rewind depth of 64-k until the head wraps onto the holes - not '5h of rewindable history destroyed'. The observable wrongness is Count()/the panel's 'checkpoints' figure over-reporting, and the reduced depth.

**Why:** m_count is only incremented in Checkpoint (line 107-108 'if(m_count < SSR_CHECKPOINT_RING) m_count++') and reset in ClearCheckpoints; m_head is only advanced in Checkpoint (106). DropFrom (140-160) touches neither. T8.2 tests DropFrom with 10 entries (no wrap) and asserts only the dropped count and the newest survivor. RECOMMENDATION: on DropFrom, rewind m_head to the slot after the newest survivor and set m_count to the survivor count (entries are written in time order, so dropped entries are always the newest contiguous run behind the head).

**Verifiers:** DropFrom (SSR_SnapshotStore.mqh:140-160) Init()s matching slots and recomputes m_last_msc but touches neither m_count nor m_head; m_count is only raised in Checkpoint (107-108) and zeroed in ClearCheckpoints, m_head only advanced in Checkpoint (106). So after a step back from a full ring, Count() still reports 64 (surfaced as ReplayVitals.checkpoints via SSR_GroupPort.mqh:148) while k slots are empty, and the head keeps writing forward over the oldest live entries instead of reusing the holes, which stay empty until the head wraps. NearestAtOrBefore is unaffected (it skips taken_at<=0, 126) / Provable from source: DropFrom Init()s the matching slots and recomputes m_last_msc but touches neither m_count nor m_head (SSR_SnapshotStore.mqh:140-160), while m_count/m_head are only ever moved in Checkpoint (105-108) and ClearCheckpoints. So after a StepBackward -> DropFrom(now+1) (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1475) Count() keeps returning the pre-drop total - and that is a user-visible number, GroupPort publishes it as 'checkpoints' (SSR_GroupPort.mqh: out.checkpoints = c.Snapshots().Count()) - and the next Checkpoint writes at m_head, i.e. over the OLDEST live entry, while the freed holes near the head stay empty until the head wraps. Rewind depth therefore degrades to the survivor count for a full lap of the ring. NearestAtOrBefore is unaffected because it skips taken_at <= 0 (119-136), so no wrong restore results - IMPROVEMENT is the right grade, and the suggested fix (rewind m_head/m_count to the newest survivor) is sound since dropped entries are always the newest contiguous run behind the head / Provable: Checkpoint is the only writer of m_head/m_count (SSR_SnapshotStore.mqh:105-108), ClearCheckpoints the only resetter (:69), and DropFrom touches neither (:140-160) - it only Init()s slots and recomputes m_last_msc. So Count() over-reports and the head keeps walking over live slots while holes sit unused. Correctness is untouched (NearestAtOrBefore scans i<m_count and skips t<=0, :123-127; IsDue uses the recomputed m_last_msc), so the only user-visible artefact is the panel's 'checkpoints' figure via GroupPort (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:147) reading 64 when fewer are live. The claim over-states the damage: the next k checkpoints overwrite the k OLDEST slots, costing k*5 minutes of rewind depth prematurely, not '5h of rewindable history'

#### `data-11` — Every data-quality number this subsystem measures is computed on the hot path and then discarded; the only route to a human is a ToString() with no caller

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Data/SSR_Mt5DataSource.mqh:146`** · category: input-validation

```mql5
   string            ToString(void)
     {
      return StringFormat("mt5[%s open=%s ticks=%s %s]",

What is unreachable is CSSRMt5DataSource::ToString and every host-side route: nothing in the shipped EA/Ui ever prints m_dropped or any SSRDataReport field, so a live user's gappy or sanitised range produces no diagnostic line.

**Why:** Repo-wide grep confirms the chain is dead at both ends: no caller for CSSRMt5DataSource::ToString, none for CSSRBarWindow::ReportInto or Dropped(), and no occurrence of "dropped", "micro_gap", "session_gap" or "duplicates" anywhere in MQL5/Experts, Ui, Common or Core outside the validator itself. CSSRMt5TickProvider::Pages/TicksRead/ReadTimeMs are equally unread. The instrumentation was written deliberately — SSR_BarWindow.mqh:53 says "instrumentation, so Phase 7 tunes with numbers not opinions" — so this is an unfinished wiring, not an absent idea. It compounds data-2 and data-1: both of those failures are silent precisely because this telemetry never surfaces.

**Verifiers:** The wiring really is dead at the host end. CSSRMt5DataSource::ToString (SSR_Mt5DataSource.mqh:146-152) has no caller anywhere; CSSRBarWindow::ReportInto (SSR_BarWindow.mqh:329) has no caller (the only ReportInto with one is CSSRLeakGuard's); and micro_gaps/session_gaps/duplicates appear nowhere outside SSR_DataValidator.mqh and the T2 test script, i.e. never in MQL5/Experts, Ui, Common or Core. So the per-range validation report and m_dropped (accumulated at SSR_BarWindow.mqh:210) never reach the log, the vitals line or the flight recorder, which is exactly why data-2's failures are silent / The dead-end is verifiable by grep and by reading the files: CSSRBarWindow computes m_last_report (ValidateBars over the exact loaded range: duplicates, out_of_order, micro_gaps, session_gaps, largest_gap_msc) and m_dropped on every miss (SSR_BarWindow.mqh:208-210), exposes them through ReportInto (329) and Dropped() (321), and neither has any caller; CSSRMt5DataSource::ToString - the single expression that formats the window (SSR_Mt5DataSource.mqh:146-152) - has no caller either (the host only ever uses g_src.Open/Close/RangeInto/Bars/History), and no occurrence of 'dropped', 'micro_gap', 'session_gap' or 'duplicates' exists in Experts, Ui, Common or Core outside the validator. So the telemetry never reaches the log, the vitals line, or the flight recorder. This is unfinished wiring rather than incorrect behaviour, hence IMPROVEMENT, and the observation that it is what makes data-2 and data-1 silent is fair / The dead ends are real: grep shows CSSRBarWindow::ReportInto and Dropped() have no caller outside the class, Window() is touched only by SSR_T2_DataEngine.mq5, and CSSRMt5DataSource::ToString (SSR_Mt5DataSource.mqh:146-152) is never invoked - the host never calls g_src.ToString(). PrintVitals composes its line from the sink, charts and clock only, so duplicates/micro_gaps/session_gaps/dropped never reach a human. But this is absent diagnostics, not a defect: nothing the product does is wrong because of it, and the user observes nothing. It is also partly mitigated - the default vitals line does print the replay symbol's M1 bar count and last bar time once a second, which is how 'candles missing in the middle of Tuesday' would first be seen. IMPROVEMENT, not LOW

#### `strategy-integration-report-15` — SSR_CMD_SPEED reports success for a value the clock silently rewrote

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Integration/SSR_Publisher.mqh:283`** · category: input-validation

```mql5
         case SSR_CMD_SPEED:
           {
            m_group.SetSpeedX100((long)a1);
            return SSR_RC_OK;
           }
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: SSR_CMD_SPEED returns an unconditional SSR_RC_OK with no bounds test, so a client sending 0 or a negative x100 is told the command succeeded while the clock has clamped the value to 1 (0.01x). The finding's upper-bound half is wrong: SetSpeedX100 has no upper clamp (SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:78) and SSR_SPEED_MAX is only the UI ladder's last stop and a name/meaning threshold, so a request above it is applied verbatim and OK is accurate.

**Why:** The case returns a constant OK with no inspection of a1 and no bounds test. SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:76-80 is `speed_x100 = (s < 1 ? 1 : s);` with no upper bound. SSR_Types.mqh:131 defines SSR_SPEED_MAX = 100000 and the ladder's stop 19 (SSR_Types.mqh:298) is that value, so the contract exposes a range the UI does not. Contrast SSR_CMD_STEP and SSR_CMD_JUMP, which both propagate the engine's bool.

**Verifiers:** The premise 'every other command reports what the engine actually did' is refuted by the file itself: SSR_CMD_JUMP is documented as clamp-and-succeed three lines above the speed case — 'clamped by the engine into its own timeline, so a client asking for an instant outside the session lands at the edge rather than anywhere strange' (lines 289-292) — and SeekTo (SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:104-112) unconditionally returns true after SSRClampMsc, so JUMP also answers OK for a value the engine rewrote. Speed follows the same established pattern. No incorrect state results: SetSpeedX100 clamps to >= 1 (SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:76-80), the group propagates the clamped master value to every stream (SSR_MasterClock.mqh:281-288), Advance saturates at end_msc (SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:99-108) so no overflow or runaway follows a huge value, and every consumer treats speed_x100 >= SSR_SPEED_MAX as 'as fast as ticks feed' (SSR_Types.mqh:241, 352) — so 5,000,000 runs exactly as the caller asked. The authoritative value is republished in SSR_GV_SPEED on the next Publish (line 190) and the shipped client's only speed reading is that field (SSR_Client.mqh:120); nothing in the contract lets a client display its own request. The residual discrepancy — OK for a1 <= 0 which becomes 0.01x — is an API-consistency improvement, not a defect / The source facts hold for the low side: SSR_CMD_SPEED (SSR_Publisher.mqh:283-287) returns a constant SSR_RC_OK with no inspection of a1, while CSSRReplayClock::SetSpeedX100 is `speed_x100 = (s < 1 ? 1 : s);` (SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:76-80), so a client sending 0 or a negative x100 is told OK and the replay runs at 0.01x. CSSRReplayGroup::SetSpeedX100 (SSR_MasterClock.mqh:281-289) is void, so there is genuinely no engine bool to propagate — unlike SSR_CMD_STEP/JUMP, which do. The high-side half of the claim is refuted: there is no upper clamp anywhere, and SSR_SPEED_MAX (SSR_Types.mqh:131) is only the UI ladder's top stop (line 298) and a display threshold (lines 241, 352), so 5,000,000 is honoured rather than rewritten and the OK is truthful. Improvement-grade: a bounds test or a read-back of m_group.SpeedX100() before answering / Verified: the SSR_CMD_SPEED case returns a constant SSR_RC_OK with no inspection of a1, while CSSRReplayClock::SetSpeedX100 is `speed_x100 = (s < 1 ? 1 : s);` (SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:76-80) and CSSRReplayGroup::SetSpeedX100 (SSR_MasterClock.mqh:281-288) just forwards, so 0 or a negative becomes 1 (0.01x) and is still reported as success — inconsistent with STEP/JUMP, which propagate the engine's bool. Correctly filed as IMPROVEMENT, and the impact is smaller still because Publish() writes m_group.SpeedX100() to SSR_GV_SPEED every pump (line 190), so the truth is always on the wire for any client that reads it. One correction: the 5,000,000 example is not a value 'the clock silently rewrote' — there is no upper clamp anywhere, so that speed is accepted verbatim and OK is truthful; it merely exceeds the range the UI ladder exposes

#### `ui-plumbing-5` — SSR_Layout.mqh is dead in production: nothing outside the QA smoke test positions anything through it, so the RTL plan it exists to enable has no backing

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Ui/SSR_Layout.mqh:67`** · category: rtl

```mql5
int SSRLead(const SSRFrame &f, const int off, const int width)
  {
   if(!f.rtl)
      return f.x + f.pad + off;
   return f.x + f.w - f.pad - off - width;
  }
```

**What goes wrong** *(as corrected by the verifiers)*: Accurate as described. Only the severity is over-stated: nothing misbehaves at runtime; the cost is that the RTL phase will have to rewrite the inline arithmetic the helpers were built to prevent, and the file header asserts a constraint the codebase never adopted.

**Why:** The file's header states the constraint it was built to impose: "The localization plan therefore places one constraint on every phase after this one - position through here, never by hand - and this file is that promise made concrete." The constraint was never adopted; every UI file computes x positions inline (e.g. SSR_KeyCard.mqh:74-93 `int x = 14; ... x + 12 ... x + 86`, SSR_Panel.mqh:889 `int cx = x + 140`). The smoke test's own note (SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:4984) records the file as "written and deliberately OFF", which is true of the mirroring flag but understates it: the helpers are not merely off, they are uncalled.

**Verifiers:** Grep over every .mqh/.mq5 is decisive: SSRLead/SSRTrail/SSRCentre/SSRInner/SSRColW/SSRColX/SSRFrame/SSRRows appear only in SSR_Layout.mqh itself, in SSR_Panel.mqh:44 (a bare #include that uses nothing), and in SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:3354-3386 (the only caller and the only rtl=true). SSRCentre and SSRInner have no call site at all except SSRColW's internal use of SSRInner. Production draw sites do compute pixels inline (SSR_ReviewCard.mqh:112-204 is a full page of m_x+12 / m_x+SSR_RV_W-96 arithmetic, exactly the pattern the header forbids). So flipping SSRFrame.rtl changes nothing on any screen and the header's claim that later phases position 'through here, never by hand' is not honoured anywhere. No runtime defect exists today, hence LOW rather than MEDIUM: this is an unadopted abstraction plus an over-stated header, not a fault a user can hit / Grep over every .mqh/.mq5 confirms the only callers of SSRLead/SSRTrail/SSRColW/SSRColX/SSRFrame/SSRRows are SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:3354-3386; SSR_Panel.mqh:44 only #includes the header. No production draw site positions through it, so flipping SSRFrame.rtl is a no-op on screen - provable from source, no MQL5 semantics involved. But there is no runtime defect: the header itself states 'mirroring is IMPLEMENTED and OFF', RTL is not a shipped feature, and MQL5 compiles uncalled global functions without complaint. The finding is accurate technical debt, not a MEDIUM behavioural bug, and one sub-claim is wrong: SSRInner IS called, at SSR_Layout.mqh:134 inside SSRColW (only SSRCentre is truly callerless) / The grep is accurate (MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Ui/SSR_Layout.mqh's helpers are referenced only by SSR_Panel.mqh:44's #include and SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:3354-3386), but nothing here is a defect a user can reach or observe. Every draw site positions correctly today; SSRFrame.rtl is never true outside the test, so no pixel is misplaced, no string is cut, no arithmetic is wrong. The file's own header (lines 28-31) states the status the finding reports as a discovery: 'mirroring is IMPLEMENTED and OFF. Nothing calls it with rtl=true yet, because no string has been translated. Phase 10 turns it on.' Pre-built, deliberately unwired scaffolding whose adoption is scheduled for a later phase is a planning observation, not a bug, and MEDIUM misrepresents a zero-impact state as a product fault. The residual point - that the promised 'position through here, never by hand' constraint was not adopted, so Phase 10 will cost a manual rewrite of eight UI files - is worth recording at IMPROVEMENT, no higher

#### `ui-port-session-16` — data_mode is on the wire, set by nobody and read by nobody

**`MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Ui/SSR_ReplayPort.mqh:54`** · category: zero-empty

```mql5
   ENUM_SSR_DATA_MODE data_mode;
```

**What goes wrong:** The one port implementation never assigns this field, so it permanently reports SSR_DATA_MEMORY; the first consumer to trust it will describe a disk-backed session as in-memory.

**Why:** Init() sets `data_mode = SSR_DATA_MEMORY;` (l.250) and CSSRGroupPort::ReadState never touches it, although the value exists on the controller and is written into the session file (`f.SetInt("data_mode", (int)m_state.data_mode);`, ReplayController.mqh:1728). A grep for data_mode across Ui and Integration returns only the declaration and that Init line - no writer, no reader. Either fill it in ReadState beside fidelity (l.110-112) or drop it from the struct: SSRUiState is the IPC contract, and a field that is always a default is a field the promised Ipc port will silently get wrong.

**Verifiers:** Traced every occurrence of data_mode in the tree: SSR_ReplayState.mqh:35/55 (engine field, defaults MEMORY), SSR_ReplayController.mqh:693 SetDataMode and :1728 the session-file write, SSR_PositionFile.mqh:79/119, and in the UI layer only SSR_ReplayPort.mqh:54 (declaration) and :250 (Init sets SSR_DATA_MEMORY). No ReadState implementation assigns it and no panel/dialog reads it. Meanwhile production really does set the engine to a different value (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1150 and :499 call SetDataMode(SSR_DATA_BROKER)), so the wire field is not merely unset, it is provably inconsistent with the controller it is supposed to mirror.
